author: Sharon Zhang
title: Alex Karp Says Palantir Is “Progressive” Now, Months After Fascist Manifesto
content:
Karp, who gave $1 million to MAGA Inc. in 2024, said after the midterms that he’s been a Democrat his “whole life.”

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

As Democrats prepare for their sweeping campaign to investigate corporate abuses during the upcoming Congress, Palantir CEO Alex Karp claimed this week that he and his company — a massive Trump administration collaborator — are actually “progressive” now.

Karp, who gave $1 million to MAGA Inc. in 2024 and another million for Donald Trump’s inauguration, told Politico Playbook on Wednesday that he’s always been a Democrat.

“I’ve been a Democrat my whole life. I grew up in a far left environment. I know more about being a progressive than almost anybody on the planet, and I absolutely believe Palantir — all of our products are essentially progressive,” he told Politico, speaking of his company that has a $30 million contract with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to aid Trump’s mass deportation campaign.

Far from being progressive, Karp and his company have helped to accelerate the Trump administration’s descent into fascism while wooing Trump in order to gain favor with the government.

Just in April, Palantir landed in hot water for posting a far right, 22-point manifesto that it said was a summary of Karp’s 2025 book, The Technological Republic. Critics described the X post as technofascist, as it espoused a pro-war, pro-policing ideology, lamented the post-Holocaust “neutering” of Nazi Germany and Japan, and said that cultures that have “produced vital advances” are superior to those that are “dysfunctional and regressive.”

The tech CEO has been on the record many times branding himself and Palantir as undertaking a far right effort, with Karp calling his company “anti-woke” and praising the Trump administration’s anti-immigration measures.

But in the Politico interview, Karp claimed that he was happy that Trump acknowledged that “we kinda went too far” on immigration — a misrepresentation of Trump’s words earlier this week. Karp used the word “progressive” eight times to describe his political philosophy, despite the fact that progressivism is typically known for being antiwar, pro-immigrant, and opposed to tech companies like Palantir.

On top of Karp’s contributions to Trump, Palantir was recently revealed to have donated $10 million to Trump’s East Wing ballroom project. In exchange for these gifts, the Trump administration has helped to propel Palantir to being one of the top recipients of federal contracts, embedding its AI systems in the military and recruiting the company to mine Americans’ data to help monitor and build cases against people targeted by Trump’s deportation campaign.

Karp also appears to have given Republican House candidate Jay Obernolte $7,000 in January, federal disclosures show, though he listed his employer as “Plantatir Technologies” — making it so that his company wouldn’t come up in database search queries for Palantir, spelled correctly.

Karp’s comments represent what is likely a naked attempt to woo Democrats before they take control of Congress in January.

Some Democratic committees have already looked into Palantir for its dealings with the Trump administration and its work in building out mass surveillance systems for the federal government. This has spurred Palantir to hire former Democratic Sen. Jon Tester this week, in preparation for the new Congress. Palantir and other tech firms have also donated to House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-New York), who is poised to become speaker of the Democratically-controlled House.

Donations are down for Truthout at a time when media is under immense pressure. Google’s AI search has driven our traffic down by 15 percent, Trump is arresting journalists, and many independent media organizations face heartbreaking cutbacks and closures.

At the same time, movement media is vital in the fight against Trump’s authoritarian reign. Our mandate to tell the truth, share strategies for resistance, and speak against fascism is ever more urgent in this deluge of political censorship and misinformation. Yet, we are struggling to meet our publishing costs when our work is so urgently needed.

We are fundraising right now for those basic operating expenses — we need $44,000 in the next 7 days. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will …

title: „Tag der Ehre“ und „Lukov-Marsch“ 2023: Deutsche Polizei behindert Antifa-Proteste in Bulgarien und verfolgt Angriffe auf Nazis in Ungarn
content:
Dossier


„Am 24. Februar 2023 wurde Florian Gutsche, Bundesvorsitzender der VVN-BdA, am Berliner Flughafen von Beamten der Bundespolizei im Rahmen einer offensichtlich vorbereiteten Aktion abgefangen. Gutsche war auf dem Weg nach Bulgarien, wo er als Beobachter an internationalen Protesten gegen den faschistischen „Lukov-Marsch“ in Sofia teilnehmen wollte. Er wurde zwei Stunden festgehalten und befragt, sein Gepäck durchsucht und mit einer sechsseitigen „Ausreiseuntersagung“ wieder entlassen. Diese beinhaltete die Drohung, dass man ihn bei Zuwiderhandlung „in Gewahrsam nehmen“ und strafrechtlich verfolgen werde. Das Ausreiseverbot wurde im Rahmen des Passgesetzes für jegliche Auslandsreise an dem Wochenende erlassen. Die Verfügung wurde damit begründet, dass damit zu rechnen sei, dass Gutsche „das Ansehen der Bundesrepublik Deutschland im Ausland erheblich schädigen“ würde…“

Pressemitteilung der VVN-BdA vom 6. März 2023


 und mehr daraus sowie dazu:

Trotz des Machtwechsels in Ungarn können wir aus Majas, Tobis und Ilarias Erfahrungen erahnen, was ihn dort erwartet: Isolation, Gewalt und Willkür, sowie ein politisches Verfahren. Zudem sind die ungarischen Behörden und das Knastsystem für ihren gewaltvollen Rassismus bekannt. Wir gehen zusätzlich davon aus, dass Zaid eine Abschiebung von Ungarn nach Syrien drohen würde. Währenddessen sitzt Maja seit über 2 Jahren in Ungarn im Knast. Zuletzt wurde Majas Urteil zu 7 Jahren Haft unter strengsten Bedingungen rechtskräftig. Maja wurde eine Rücküberstellung nach Deutschland zugesichert. Während eine rechtswidrige Auslieferung nur wenige Stunden dauert, schieben sich die deutschen Behörden die Zuständigkeit für die Rücküberstellung hin und her. ..“

title: Enzo Traverso: “La revuelta juvenil tiene una dimensión política evidente”
content:
Paris 2026: «siamo tutti antifacisti»


https://www.facebook.com/reel/1145355668017795


.


Enzo Traverso: “La revuelta juvenil tiene una dimensión política evidente”


Enzo Traverso

 


06/11/2026


En “Supervivencias de la revuelta”, el historiador pone de relieve la “vida póstuma” de las experiencias emancipadoras, a contracorriente de los relatos nacionales. En una entrevista con Mathieu Dejean para Mediapart, descifra los vínculos subterráneos que unen esta memoria rebelde y el movimiento social actual.


Contra la despolitización y la anestesia del pasado, el historiador Enzo Traverso, profesor de la Universidad de Cornell (Ithaca, Nueva York), revive las memorias rebeldes. Después de 

La melancolía de izquierda 

(2016) y 

Revolución 

(2022), su nuevo libro, 

Supervivencias de la revuelta. Ensayo sobre la dialéctica de la memoria 

(2026) -en francés en las ediciones La Découverte- cierra esta trilogía advirtiendo a los ciudadanos contra las políticas de memoria regidas por las instituciones e invitándolos a apropiarse de la tradición de los oprimidos.


“Esta memoria de las revueltas es subterránea, discreta, pero surge de forma imprevista”, 

escribe. El 17 de octubre de 2026 es una demostración de ello: varias capas de memorias rebeldes se entrecruzaron, desde el 17 de octubre de 1961 en la Comuna de París en 1871. Vuelve, en una entrevista con 

Mediapart

, sobre lo que el movimiento social actual lleva de recuerdos y sobre sus potencialidades, a pesar de la incertidumbre, para finalmente 

“dejar la época contemporánea”.


“Mediapart”: Un alto funcionario de la policía dijo, sobre el 

17 de octubre

: “Era la Comuna de París el día del Black Friday. ¿No es la memoria anti Comuna la que se manifiesta con fuerza desde esa fecha?


Enzo Traverso: 

Hay algo asombroso en la posteridad de la Comuna de París, que tiene tanto el estatus de paradigma para las memorias rebeldes -resurge constantemente, no solo en Francia, sino a escala global- como para el pensamiento reaccionario. Ha proporcionado un repertorio de figuras, referencias, símbolos, imágenes en la cultura reaccionaria, que se ha reactivado constantemente durante un siglo y medio.


De hecho, este es el caso desde el 17 de octubre, no solo en Francia sino también en Italia, donde se invocan los mismos motivos -la civilización amenazada por la barbarie, los salvajes que se apoderan de los centros de las ciudades-, con una dimensión xenófoba y racista particularmente importante. La juventud de los suburbios postcoloniales actúa como un nuevo chivo expiatorio. Un imaginario reaccionario global está tomando forma.


¿Cuáles son las referencias adoptadas precisamente de la memoria anti Comuna?


Si pensamos en la literatura anti Comuna, Théophile Gautier calificó a los protagonistas de la Comuna de París de 

“bestias”, 

“animales apestosos” 

y 

“venenosos” 

escapadas de un zoológico, que hacen estragos en la ciudad porque el guardián se olvidó de cerrar la jaula. Son los mismos clichés que se propagan hoy.


Una gran figura del pensamiento reaccionario de la época, Alphonse Daudet, dijo al día siguiente de la Comuna: 

«¡París estaba en manos de los negros!

 Es una racialización y una animalización de la revuelta y los rebeldes que, en una continuidad asombrosa, perduran hasta nuestros días.


En ambos casos, podemos destacar la negativa de los gobernantes -en este caso Emmanuel Macron, Sébastien Lecornu y Laurent Nuñez- a 

cuestionar las causas sociales y políticas de la revuelta

. Como en la Comuna de París, la revuelta es para ellos un fenómeno mucho más biológico que social. Lo que explica la revuelta es la naturaleza racial o religiosa de los rebeldes, aunque muchos jóvenes blancos fueron muy activos el 17 de octubre. En su imaginación, hay que ver al rebelde como un cuerpo ajeno a la nación.


En términos más generales, parece que el pueblo ha permanecido, en la mente de las élites gobernantes, una “multitud vil”, como dijo Adolphe Thiers.


Esta es una observación interesante, porque lo que también llama la atención es el relativo silencio de la extrema derecha, que a menudo se califica de “populista”. A menudo ha reivindicado la ira legítima de las clases populares contra el 

establishment

, del pueblo virtuoso contra las élites corruptas. Pero a diferencia de 2017 y 2022, Emmanuel Macron se encuentra en tal estado de derrota que Rassemblement national (RN) se ha ganado la confianza de las élites dominantes, de las que se ha …

author: Stephen Lerner
title: Trump and technofascism took a hit — now we must act
content:
This article

Trump and technofascism took a hit — now we must act

 was originally published by

Waging Nonviolence

.


The midterm election was a repudiation of Trump and of his Silicon Valley billionaire enablers. This has created a huge opening that we should celebrate — yet we should be clear-headed about the challenges ahead. Victory over Trumpism and Silicon Valley technofascism is by no means assured. Trump’s

appointment of Stephen Miller, a white nationalist

, to chief of staff is a flashing warning sign. 


Trump and Miller have massive power to use the Justice Department, Immigration and Customs Enforcement, or ICE, and other tools of the federal government to target Trump’s opponents. And the Silicon Valley billionaires will use their extraordinary wealth and power to try to crush attempts to stop the build-out of massive data centers, which they desperately need to power their AI expansion. There are growing fears that AI investments have created a stock market bubble that is leaking and ready to burst. The $2.5 trillion sell-off of AI and tech stock on Nov. 5 is a terrifying illustration of how

AI speculation may crash the whole economy

. So while we should breathe in the hope the electoral results have delivered to us, we must also redouble our resolve and prepare for the battles ahead.


Over the past two years, many of us felt overwhelmed, strangled and suffocated by unrelenting attacks that came from every direction, from ICE kidnapping our neighbors, to the U.S. bombing and warring on other countries, to absurd conspiracy theories and racist ranting by Donald Trump, Elon Musk and their ilk. As we can now see, the increasingly vicious nature of their words and actions was also a sign of their weakness and growing desperation. 


Sign Up for our Newsletter


We’ll send you a weekly email with the latest articles.


But weakness and desperation should not be confused with surrender. As our history reminds us, the forces of entrenched power and wealth are nothing if not resilient. They will use every tool at their disposal to deflect or dilute reform, divide their opponents, and prepare countermoves that will roll back our gains. The Reconstruction of the post-Civil War years gave birth to the reactionary “Redeemers,” who succeeded in undoing efforts to advance racial equality. The forward thrust of the New Deal was blunted by the Red Scare. The civil rights gains of the 1960s were challenged by the Southern Strategy and the Reagan Revolution.   


So we should prepare ourselves for the reality that the forces that we have been fighting will not simply throw in the towel. We should not assume that the lawless ways of the Trump presidency will suddenly cease or that its billionaire backers will retreat to the comfort of their gated communities and private jets and cease their efforts to commandeer our future. Far from it. We must expect that they will use every bit of the considerable power they still hold to thwart real change.  


Silicon Valley AI billionaires have made clear that they aren’t content with just becoming billionaires and trillionaires. Their goal is far more expansive and scary. They want to eliminate democracy altogether and replace it with a CEO autocracy. Palantir co-founder Peter Thiel is worth $37 billion and publicly says, “I no longer believe that freedom and democracy are compatible.” 


Defunding AI


The election has shown that the popular mood is behind us. We have a unique window to thwart the Silicon Valley billionaires and to build and exercise power. None of us has a road map of how to do this, but there are some promising paths we can take. A central task is figuring out how we stop funding, bankrolling and purchasing from the technofascist billionaires. We need to stop financing our own destruction. 


There are a series of exciting campaigns already happening

that are trying to do exactly that, and each one offers opportunities for people to be involved individually and organizationally. These campaigns offer, if successful, a vehicle to organize and activate hundreds of thousands of new activists directly in the fight for democracy and against the Silicon Valley AI overlords.

source of capital

author: labor4pal
title: The Teamsters’ Midterm Disaster (Joe Allen)
content:
The Teamsters’ Midterm Disaster

Despite a post-election effort to perfume up the performance of the Teamsters’ in the recent midterm elections, a string of high profile endorsements, many with the blessing of its General President Sean O’Brien went down to a thumping defeat. The historic ‘blue wave’ changed the color of the electoral map in the United States and raised political hopes for many people that a change in direction in the country is possible. Trump’s second term was a nightmare and saw a dramatic shift to the left by many working class people.

Liz Shuler, president of the sclerotic and long declining AFL-CIO captured some of this feeling when she boasted:

“This blue wave was union-made. The billionaires had the money in this election, but working people had the power. The people who make this country run issued a clear mandate last night. Speaking with a unified voice, workers demanded that their elected leaders fight to raise their wages and lower costs, expand access to health care and unions, hold billionaire CEOs accountable, and check the Trump administration’s attacks on their freedoms. The labor movement is ready to work with these newly elected members of Congress, governors and state legislators on a bold agenda to deliver real change for the working class.”

Whether workers get real change after many failed blue waves during the last twenty years, is another question, but can Sean O’Brien make the same claims as Shuler? With a necklace of far right creeps hung around the Teamsters’ neck going down to glorious defeat, most notably Greg Abbott in Texas and Vivek Ramaswamy in Ohio, it is hard to see how the Teamsters have any credibility with anyone, anywhere. It’s worth asking out loud a question that many people have asked privately, are the Teamsters trying to be the most hated union in the United States?

The Teamsters’ midterm disaster has been foretold for several years now. Soon after the Teamsters settled their overhyped 2023 contract with United Parcel Service (UPS), Sean O’Brien, the union’s General President elected in 2021, had a string of chummy meetings with far right political figures in Washington, D.C. with then Senator J.D. Vance and Missouri Senator Josh Hawley. O’Brien was then invited to Mar-a-Largo by then former President Donald for an amiable meeting and photo opportunity. Trump was then invited to the Teamsters’ headquarters in Washington. For all this outreach to the far right, O’Brien was rewarded with a prime time speaking slot at the 2024 Republican Convention.

From there, it just got worse, as documented by Current Affairs contributor Hank Kennedy in his article, Sean O’Brien Sold Labor to Trump, and Got Nothing:

Under O’Brien the Teamsters went on record supporting the president’s pick for Secretary of Labor, Lori Chavez DeRemer, and O’Brien himself wrote an op-ed calling her “The Pro-Worker Choice for Labor” in Compact. Under questioning, DeRemer admitted she no longer supported the section of the PRO Act weakening state anti-union right-to-work laws. This bothered O’Brien not a bit. On Fox, he said that he and his bosom buddy Josh Hawley were working on a version of the PRO Act that “may not include [a ban on right-to-work]” O’Brien seemed to say that right-to-work laws could be “what works” for certain states. At least, that’s how the vehemently anti-union National Right to Work Committee interpreted his remarks in a post on X.

DeRemer resigned in disgrace, but was a guest of Sean O’Brien, whom she called her “good friend,” at the recent Teamsters convention in Las Vegas.

The Teamsters didn’t formally endorse Trump or the Democratic presidential candidate Vice-President Kamala Harris, but the non-endorsement of Harris was seen as a victory by Trump. Speaking to reporters, Trump said of the Teamsters decision not to endorse a candidate: “It’s a great honor. They’re not going to endorse the Democrats. That’s a big thing.” Most people following union and Teamster politics saw it as a backhanded endorsement of Trump.

“Sean O’Brien is not the first Teamster leader to have endorsed right-wing politicians hostile to organized labor,” Kennedy argued. “The Teamsters endorsed Richard Nixon, Ronald Reagan, and George H.W. Bush, usually in a cynical effort to stave off federal investigations and indictments of corrupt leadership. As far as is known, there’s no such cloud hanging over O’Brien’s head. He walks this road to perdition under his own steam.”

content:
Sommes-nous dans une situation pré-autoritaire ou pré-révolutionnaire ? L'insurrection est-elle un devoir en plus d'être un droit ? Faut-il articuler l'émeute au moment électoral ou pas du tout ? Nous nous posons ces questions avec Tristan Garcia (L'autorité est un chantage, 2026) et Patrice Maniglier (La terre ou le monde. Divergences cosmopolitiques. Avec Étienne Balibar. 2025).


À voir lundi 9 novembre :


Quand Marc Crépon affirme sur

C politique

 que l'incendie de la Mairie de Limoges le 17 octobre 2026 relève d'une « ivresse de la destruction » qui – d'une manière honnêtement

boomer

 – évoque pour lui la tarte à la crème du nihilisme des

Possédés

 de Dostoïevski, il ne se rend peut-être pas compte de l'hilarité universelle qu'il suscite chez à peu près tout le monde. Lorsque l'historien, professeur au collège de France, Patrick Boucheron, dans un entretien de Libération, le 31 octobre : dénonce ceux qui continuent de

« croire que la violence émeutière est toujours émancipatrice »

 et pose le constat que nous sommes en situation pré-autoritaire et pas prérévolutionnaire. Il ne se doute pas que nous rions tout autant.


Lundimatin

 n'a que faire des tautologies nihilistes et des dissociations sociales-démocrates. Notre position a toujours été celle de l'

Encyclopédie des émeutes

 : « Ce qui est intéressant dans l'émeute n'est pas une cause, mais un possible » (BE, II, 54). « Toute tentative des pauvres modernes pour organiser le débat sur le monde commence par une émeute : 1789, 1848, 1871, 1917, 1968, et en 1978 en Iran et au Nicaragua. » (BE, II, 55) C'est pourquoi l'émeute est pour nous « le début possible de la fin du monde » (55) et, en général, « un début de débat » sur cette fin (55). Toute émeute ne conduit pas à une insurrection ou une révolution, mais « il n'y a pas de révolution ni d'insurrection qui ne commencent par une émeute. » (55).


Nos invités ont peut-être d'autres idées sur la question, il faut néanmoins assumer que le débat sur le monde vient d'être relancé.

title: Feindbild Antifaschismus: Inflationärer Einsatz von Öffentlichkeitsfahndung
content:
Feindbild Antifaschismus: Inflationärer Einsatz von Öffentlichkeitsfahndung


Ende Oktober 2026 hat das Landeskriminalamt Baden-Württemberg eine Öffentlichkeitsfahndung gegen Antifaschist*innen gestartet, gegen die es wegen schweren Landfriedensbruchs ermittelt. Damit droht ein neuer Dammbruch, indem dieses schwer wiegende Repressionsinstrument inflationär gegen Linke eingesetzt werden könnte.

Initiiert hat die Fahndung die Kriminalpolizei Heidelberg, der das regionale Dezernat Staatsschutz – die Politische Polizei – angegliedert ist. Sie ermittelt gegen rund 40 Antifaschist*innen, die an einer körperlichen Auseinandersetzung mit Rechten am 29. August 2026 in Mannheim beteiligt gewesen sein sollen. Der konkrete Straftatbestand, der ihnen vorgeworfen wird, ist schwerer Landfriedensbruch – ein Pauschalvorwurf, der einen individuellen Tatnachweis obsolet macht und die bloße Anwesenheit in einer Gruppe verfolgt. Der Paragraf wird häufig angewandt, um nach Demonstrationen oder anderen Aktionen dutzende oder gar hunderte Aktivist*innen zu kriminalisieren.

Indem auf der Homepage des Landeskriminalamts 13 Fotos von Beschuldigten veröffentlicht wurden, ist eine neue Stufe der Repression gegen Antifaschist*innen erreicht: Nur vereinzelt wurde diese massive Maßnahme bisher im Kontext von linken Protesten eingesetzt. Dass es hier in erster Linie um Einschüchterung und Abschreckung geht, zeigte eine erste Hausdurchsuchung in diesem Verfahrenskomplex, bei der die Einsatzkräfte rabiat auftraten.

„Dass das Landeskriminalamt Baden-Württemberg die Beschuldigten an den Online-Pranger stellt, zeigt, dass im Kampf gegen Antifaschismus alle Dämme brechen“, erklärte Hartmut Brückner vom Bundesvorstand der Roten Hilfe e. V. „Ob nach Blockaden, Demonstrationen und Aktionen, ob bei Öffentlichkeitsarbeit oder schlichtweg gegen antifaschistische Einrichtungen und Infrastruktur: Kaum ein Repressionsinstrument wird ausgelassen, um Aktivist*innen und die gesamte Bewegung einzuschüchtern und von weiterem Engagement abzuhalten. Umso wichtiger ist es, die Betroffenen nicht alleinzulassen, sondern im Repressionsfall solidarisch zu unterstützen. Wir sind alle Antifa!“

author: Julius Gavroche
title: The Hot Potato Changes Hands Again
content:
On the 2026 Midterm Elections


from the

CrimethInc.

collective, 06/11/2026


Ultimately, the Democrats are no more capable of addressing the root causes of popular anger than the Republicans. State power will continue to swing back and forth more and more wildly between different parties until our rulers consolidate an autocracy or we manage to effect revolutionary change.


As we anticipated

in April

, the death knell of the Trump era has rung. Despite being

historically unpopular

, Democratic politicians won a sweeping victory in the November 2026 midterm elections. Many are describing the rout as an “

extinction-level event

” for the Republican Party.


All this should feel familiar. Only two years ago, when Democrats lost the 2024 elections, pundits across the political spectrum rushed to declare the collapse of the Democratic Party. Summarizing a widespread perception, one

expert

 claimed that


“Fundamental shifts are occurring in the body politic that have left Democrats on the wrong side of the popular vote, congressional races, and the country’s shifting demographics.”


Two years later, people are saying the same things about the Republican Party. The backlash against Republicans in this year’s election eclipses the gains they made in 2024. Yet the pendulum has been swinging wildly back and forth between parties for over a decade now—and it could be that the wildest swings have yet to come.


For all the talk of political polarization, loyalty to political parties is at its

lowest

 in decades. Since at least 2016, anger at the status quo has been the most powerful force in politics; Democrats like Hillary Clinton and Joe Biden who attempted to present themselves as its defenders have learned that the hard way. Likewise, Donald Trump has only able to win elections when he is not in office. Whenever Trump represents the ruling order, he draws the same backlash that he once managed to channel.


Since 2014, we have argued that state power itself has become a hot potato that burns whoever holds it. In a globalized economy, in which governments can no longer mitigate the impact of capitalism on their citizens without investors taking their money elsewhere, no party is able to hold state power for long without losing credibility with voters. Similarly, the challenges of maintaining position as a waning imperial power inevitably undercut the legitimacy of whoever controls the state: just as the genocide in Gaza damaged the Biden administration’s support, Trump’s

war with Iran

 has contributed to driving away voters.


Similar things are taking place all around the world.

British politicians

 have also seen rapid reversals in fortune. The centrist parties that have long ruled Germany and France are in precipitous decline. One Latin American government after another has swung to the far right, but that hardly indicates a

social consensus

 in favor of

any political camp

.


Only countries under continuous autocratic rule, such as Russia, Belarus, China, and North Korea, are excepted from the hot potato pattern. Donald Trump has made no secret of his desire to establish a similar state of affairs in the United States. Yet even in Hungary, which Republicans took as a model for their illiberal aspirations, the long-running autocratic government ultimately lost control. The same has occurred in Poland and, more recently, Serbia. Wherever voters have an opportunity—however narrow—to demand change, they do so—however arbitrarily and capriciously.


With no prospect of improving life for his rank-and-file supporters, Trump’s solution was to

inflict violence

 on their behalf, offering them the vicarious thrill of watching the state cause harm to others as an outlet for their frustration.

Less bread, more circuses

.


Republicans and Democrats—trash and recycling.


It might have worked—if ordinary people had not courageously taken the streets to interfere. We owe Trump’s failure to those who assembled at

Tesla dealerships

 in spring 2025, who

rose up

Chicago

,

Minnesota

, and elsewhere. As we previously saw in

the movement against police and white supremacy

, when people take risks in solidarity with others, this makes it possible for more people to experience empathy where previously, they only felt dissociation and apathy.

title: YPJ spokesperson Ruksen Mihemed: We can only achieve our freedom through our own struggle
content:
What does self-defense mean for women whose identity, history and social existence have been subjected to attacks for generations? And what conditions must be established to ensure that women no longer have to depend on others to make decisions about their security, their rights and their future?


According to Ruksen Mihemed, spokesperson for the Women’s Protection Units (YPJ) in Rojava, these questions lie at the heart of a struggle that extends far beyond armed resistance.


In an interview with ANF, Mihemed reflected on 15 years of women’s organizing and self-defense in Northeast Syria. She discusses the establishment of the YPJ, the experiences of the women’s revolution and the challenges arising from the ongoing restructuring of Syria.


“When a woman defends herself, there is life. But if she entrusts her defense to others, she cannot protect her life. The consequence is death,” Mihemed said.


https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/7e263871_20261110221245_2026-11-10-qamislo-ruksen-mihemed-ypj-komutani-jpj-ve-25-kasim_1.mp4


Self-defense begins with awareness of one’s own identity


The emergence of independent women’s defense structures was closely linked to the social organizing that developed during the Rojava Revolution. Women began establishing their own institutions, taking responsibility in political decision-making processes and organizing independently in the field of defense.


“With the Rojava Revolution, women began to organize, and their participation in defense became a necessity. But first, women had to recognize their own identity and existence, learn about their history, understand themselves and develop an awareness of self-defense,” the YPJ spokesperson said.


She continued: “Our fundamental principle was that women should gain confidence in themselves, be able to express their thoughts freely and make their own decisions. On this foundation, they subsequently became increasingly involved in the field of defense.”


YPJ wrote a new chapter in the history of women’s struggle


With the formation of the YPJ, an independent women’s military organization emerged within the Kurdish freedom movement in Rojava. Its development was part of a broader social process in which women established their own political and institutional structures.


“With its establishment, the YPJ also wrote a new chapter in history: the history of a new women’s struggle. For the first time, an autonomous women’s force was established. This gave women the opportunity to create their own representation in all areas,” Mihemed noted.


“If self-defense has no place in a woman’s life, neither her rights, her legal status nor her life are protected. This is precisely where the YPJ took action. It created a system intended to ensure security, dignity and a life free from violence.”


Mihemed also emphasized the international impact of the YPJ: “Over these 15 years, the YPJ’s struggle has brought together not only women in Rojava and the Middle East, but also women around the world under a common banner of struggle. It has helped foster a shared stance and a spirit of solidarity among women.”


Women’s rights as a point of contention in Syria’s restructuring


As negotiations continue over Syria’s political and institutional future, questions are also emerging about the preservation of the women’s structures established in Northeast Syria over the past several years. Mihemed directed her criticism particularly at the Syrian transitional government, saying: “Damascus is still not convinced that the women’s question and women’s freedom are fundamental issues. It has failed to recognize that no country can be built without women’s organizing and that lasting stability in the fields of defense and security is impossible without their participation. Instead, a male-dominated mentality continues to prevail.”


According to the YPJ spokesperson, negotiations over the country’s future political system are therefore inseparably linked to women’s legal status: “This mentality must change. We must not forget that injustice committed against women is also an injustice against society as a whole. Women’s political and legal rights must be guaranteed within the emerging system.”

author: Freedom Editor
title: Dignity walks in the heart
content:
Mexico’s search collectives make alliances with Zapatista army to confront the systematic violence of enforced disappearances and femicides

It is dawn again and 12-year-old Ariana is getting ready to leave her home with her grandmother. Together they walk in the mountains of Chiapas to a nearby ranch to care for their family animals. After that? We cannot say, as they both stepped out of this world and disappeared. We only know for sure that they were never seen alive again.

The family and neighbours began the search until two days later, the body of 55-year-old Miriam Cruz Alpuche was discovered on the bank of a local stream. She was wrapped in black bin bags and community rescue units discovered multiple signs of violence. By the end of the week, Ariana Scarlet Velázquez Cruz was found close by.

“The demand for truth and justice for disappearances,” said Captain Marcos of the EZLN (Zapatista Army of National Liberation) “enforced disappearances and disappearances by individuals – must be assumed a national responsibility.” Marcos was speaking in San Cristóbal de las Casas (Jovel) in Chiapas after meeting with “mother seekers” in el caracol Jacinto Canel.

In the Zapatista territories, EZLN and colectivos de búsqueda (search collectives) have pledged to form alliances in confronting the Mexican government for it’s role in facilitating disappearances, murders, gender-based violence and wars. They will meet in Ajusco in December, an area that is a high risk for disappearances, as well as a delegation to Mexico City to both expose and find community-based resistance to this crime against humanity.

With more than 130,000 people missing in Mexico, decades of activism and legal battles against systematic violence and enforced disappearances, the United Nations has finally got involved in offering the state of Mexico assistance. Predictably as the families of the disappeared arrived to give their own testimony, the Mexican government denied this pain with their own historical fiction.

In Chiapas there have been 30 documented cases of femicide and 440 across Mexico in the first half of 2026. These numbers are reflections of the activities of local groups, not the true scale of the problem. Government corruption has hidden the mass killings of women and children, as well as a clear complicity in the enforced disappearances of it’s own citizens. If the body is never recovered, it cannot be known how the person died.

Investigations into femicides in Mexico are impacted by a loss of evidence, an inadequate investigation or when the gender perspective is not applied correctly. Families of the missing are re-victimised by the process of seeking justice while authorities fail to examine crime scenes, secure evidence or carry out acid phosphatase tests. All of this impacts the possibility of justice for the affected and their families.

Femicidal violence “leaves indelible consequences, deep traumas and an irreparable void in their families… in their communities and in the entire social fabric of the state,” said the Observatorio Ciudadano Nacional del Feminicidio (National Citizen Observatory of Femicide) following the murder of Miriam and Ariana. They demand an immediate gender – child perspective investigation.

The inaction of the authorities when a woman or child has gone missing is deadly, with some regional police asking families to wait 72 hours before reporting a missing person. This would have been too late for Miriam, as it would likely be for 12-year-old Ariana. The logic should be to investigate when a person is noticed missing.

In the absence of executing justice, various instruments of the law such as the Attorney General’s Office (FGE) work as a mechanism to prevent the opening of investigations, with “omission… a lack of commitment and responsibility,” observed Guadalupe Isabel Mondoza Pérez, who has been looking for her husband Alfonso since July 30, 2024 after he disappeared in Yajalón.

Authorities limit complaints by creating an administrative hole called “registros de attención” (care records) as a way of killing formal investigations. With legal advice from Colectiva Cereza (Cherry Collective), families can see what missing persons reports have been shelved in care records and which are open investigations.

If the aim is to tear the social fabric of our shared relations – it would make sense to weave these communities with shared struggles and resources to resist the stranglehold of the law as …

title: Cathy Levine - Tyrannei der Tyrannei
content:
Katalog Liste aller Texte AutorInnen Themen Letzte Einträge Zur Bibliothek hinzufügen

Mehr Kontakt Material Sticker, Plakate, etc.

Der Text „Die Tyrannei in strukturlosen Gruppen“ erfreut sich nach wie vor einer erneuten und breiten Zirkulation. Angesichts der Geschichtslosigkeit der antiautoritären Linken – diesem Hybrid zwischen Anarchismus und Linkstum – ist die damalige – prägnante, logische und unwiderlegte Antwort von antiautoritärer Seite in der heutigen Diskussion völlig ignoriert worden. Der Text ist deshalb allemal dokumentierenswert, und sei es nur, um sich über die Seite „barrikade.info“ lustig zu machen, die behauptet anti-autoritär zu sein, allerdings den Text von Joe Freeman unhinterfragt reproduziert – wie manch anderen Schwachsinn, der dies bestimmt noch überbietet. Gleiches gilt für eine Edition ‚Von unten auf‘, welche Joe Freemans einseitige Sicht reproduzierte, und deren Broschüren vom ‚Syndikat A‘ kolportiert werden. Und so sind es angeblich Antiautoritäre, welche die tatsächlich antiautoritäre Antwort auf diese autoritär-demokratischen Ergüsse durch ihre Ignoranz vergessen machen!

Aber zum vorliegenden Text, welcher Joe Freemans Text noch zur Genüge einer beherzigenswerten Kritik unterziehen wird: Die Schwäche dieser Antwort von Cathy Levine offenbart sich meiner Meinung nach in Bezug auf die Linke. Natürlich, die damalige ‚Neue Linke‘ kann vielleicht noch gewisse Hoffnungen und Illusionen bezüglich der Linken verständlich machen. Aber ebenso: die Ablehnung nur einer ‚männlichen‘ Linken ist eben halbgar, und die heute mehr oder weniger erfolgreiche Feminisierung der linken Bewegung hat auch nicht das geringste an ihrem autoritären Kern ändern können. Siehe Awarenessteams, Identitätspolitik, die kritiklose Unterstützung des Lockdowns anhand von Versatzstücken einer ‚Care‘-Ideologie… die neue Linke, und auch die noch neuere, autonome, postmoderne, etc. sind heute längst ein Bestandteil der Rekuperation, Integration und sogar direkten Verteidigung des Bestehenden…

Aber was sage ich ‚längst‘? Schon immer natürlich, schon immer. Und natürlich, die paar in der Linken gefangenen antiautoritären Individuen und Grüppchen, die deren immerneue Bolschewisierung (heute auch aka. Lockdownisierung) bekämpfen, sind relativ sympathisch, auch wenn sie sich an einem Gegenstand aufreiben, der eben ohnehin nicht das hält, was er zu versprechen scheint – und ihr Potential bindet.

Die kleine Gruppe zumindest bleibt agil, und im besten Falle betrachtet sie sich nicht als Teil von Bewegungen, die ein schwankendes Verhältnis zur Autorität haben. Aber natürlich: die Verstrickung der anarchistischen Geschichte mit der Linken macht es teilweise notwendig, auch Texte zu benutzen, deren Kritik ansonsten zwar exquisit ist, die aber auf dem ‚linken Auge blind‘ sind, wie andere umgekehrt. Wobei man Cathy Levine ja eigentlich nur eine Halbblindheit unterstellen muss, aber eine solche zumindest… denn eigentlich wärmt sie das ewige ‚eine andere Linke muss her‘ auf, anstatt das destruktive Beziehungsmuster zu durchschauen. Dadurch, dass eine Partnerschaft mit der Linken, wie sie viele anarchistische Menschen pflegen, gerade wieder einmal in psychischer und physischer Gewalt, Übergriffen und Unterdrückung endet, ist das besonders betonenswert. Die Selbstverleugnung muss aufhören, wenn es Anarchie geben soll. Die Trennung muss vollendet werden, die Linke verlassen werden, die Gruppen sich auf anarchistische Basis stellen…

Unstrukturiert anarchistisch natürlich, informell und chaotisch, denn die plattformistischen Plattitüden halten uns eben gerade in einem Fahrwasser der Linken und der Tyrannei der Tyrannei… und angesichts der immer wieder aufkommenden ‚antiautoritären Linken‘: lasst uns die Bruchgeschwindigkeit beschleunigen und an der Zerstörung der Linken arbeiten, denn sie ist jene Kraft, die sich immer offensichtlicher einer revolutionären Gärung in den Weg stellt.

Soviel dazu, Offtopic gewiss, aber ich kanns mir nicht verkneifen… denn es ging mir eben um Geschichtslosigkeit. Und solange wir mit den Linken verweilen, werden wir eben keine wirklich eigene Geschichte haben – sondern die ihre. D.h. die Geschichte unseres nützlichen Idiotentums, unserer eigenen Rekuperation, Verdrängung, Verleugnung, Integration, Verdrehung, Unschädlichmachung,…

Und selbstverständlich ergeht und erging es radikalen Feministinnen wohl ähnlich, man betrachte sich etwa die Tatsache, dass der Linken die Vergewaltigungen und Übergriffe, welche …

author: Darío Aranda
title: Día de la Maestra y el Maestro Rural: sembrar el derecho a la educación en cerros, llanuras y bosques
content:
Por Marcela Isaías


El primer día de su trabajo Leila quedó largas horas empantanada en el camino hacia la escuela. Ese fue su bautismo como maestra rural en el norte santafesino. Sandra enseña arte en secundarias rurales de Entre Ríos; todo el tiempo denuncia el mal estado de las rutas y la fumigación de los campos con agrotóxicos. El femicidio de la directora correntina Nancy Godoy le llegó muy de cerca. Adolfo da clases en un pueblo jujeño cercano a La Quiaca, en sus tareas diarias incluye la huerta escolar como un espacio de encuentro con las familias.


Ni heroínas ni apóstoles. Historias que hablan de cómo trabajan maestras y maestros rurales para garantizar el derecho a la educación.


Norte de Santa Fe


Leila Díaz vive en Tostado, cabecera del departamento 9 de Julio, bien al norte de la provincia de Santa Fe. Desde el año pasado es maestra reemplazante, siempre en la ruralidad. Su primera suplencia la hizo en una escuela rural ubicada a unos 44 kilómetros de Tostado. Una buena parte del trayecto hasta ese establecimiento es por un camino de tierra, y sí o sí lo tiene que hacer en un vehículo propio. “La primera vez que fui me llevó mi papá. Hacía dos días había llovido y en el primer charco nos quedamos”, repasa ese recuerdo que atesora.


Con ella viajaba la cocinera de la escuela. Llevaban las provisiones de comida para la semana, la garrafa, agua, además de los materiales y útiles para las clases. Debieron caminar varios kilómetros hasta el cruce con la ruta para buscar ayuda.


Leila había soñado con ese primer día de trabajo como maestra, “nunca con algo parecido” a lo que pasó. Igual siguió adelante y se enamoró de la enseñanza rural: “Lo maravilloso fue cuando llegamos a la escuela, conectamos el wi-fiy mandé un mensaje al grupo de las familias para que sepan que iba a haber clases. A los dos o tres minutos empezaron a llegar todos los niños y las niñas. Ahí entendí lo importantes que somos”.


Foto: Gentileza Leila Díaz


Vivir la semana en el lugar donde enseña es parte de su trabajo. Por lo general, quienes permanecen en estas experiencias son la docente, que hace también tareas de dirección al ser personal único, la portera o cocinera y la maestra de nivel inicial. “Las tres solitas en el medio de la nada”, dice recordando una noche de tormenta en la que además se cortó la luz.


Leila se explaya en la charla sobre su vida familiar, su hija pequeña, su marido. Del intercambio que tiene con sus alumnas y alumnos, que enriquecen la experiencia pedagógica y remiten al legado freiriano: “Siento que me escuchan, que se llevan algo de mí, como yo me llevo de ellos, porque siempre me están enseñando”.


En ese ir y venir de relatos, reconoce que no puede dejar de pensar en lo que le pasó a Nancy Godoy, la docente correntina víctima de un atroz femicidio. “Pude haber sido yo o cualquiera de mis compañeras. Todas nos sentimos identificadas con ella”, comenta ese sentimiento de espanto colectivo.


“Después de lo que pasó con Nancy —continúa— te preguntás hasta qué punto te podés exponer. Más cuando, en Santa Fe, un reemplazo lo cobrás a los 60 días”.


Las condiciones laborales, en particular la movilidad, se vuelve un tema ineludible, atraviesa todo el tiempo la conversación con quienes ejercen en la ruralidad. Si hay que hacer dedo “siempre tratamos de ser dos o más, ir en grupo”. Pide más empatía a quienes tienen a su cargo las escuelas y exigen llegar sí o sí a dar clases, “sin importar a costa de qué”.


Cierta vez viajaba en auto junto a otras maestras a dar clases a la localidad de Esteban Rams, a 77 kilómetros de Tostado. Por la imprudencia de otro conductor estuvieron a poco de un accidente: “Nos salvamos de milagro”. Es ineludible la mención a la tragedia del 27 de mayo de 2013, ocurrida en el norte santafesino y en la que perdieron la vida diez personas, entre ellas siete maestras. Pasaron más de diez años y el reclamo para que se atienda el traslado cuidadoso de la docencia rural sigue pendiente.


Daniela Spárvoli fue víctima de femicidio en 2003 - Foto: Amsafe Delegación Iriondo


Nancy y Daniela


El femicidio de Nancy Godoy puso en la agenda pública otra vez el trabajo de las docentes rurales. Nancy era de Esquina (Corrientes) y desde agosto pasado ejercía como directora suplente en la Escuela Rural N° 626, en el Paraje El Malezal. Un lugar al que le demandaba horas llegar por distintos medios, incluso a caballo. A poco de asumir su cargo denunció el abandono en el que encontró la …

author: Bahar Sheikh
title: Lieblingsstreberin: Paula Saunders
content:
In der Apple-TV-Serie „Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed“ gerät Tatiana Maslany als geschiedene Mutter in einen Scam aus Cybersex, Erpressung und Verschwörung.

Geschiedene Soccer Mom, gewissenhafte Fact-Checkerin, falsch Verdächtigte? Paula Saunders (Tatiana Maslany), Protagonistin der Apple-TV-Serie „Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed“, lässt sich auf kein Label festlegen. Sie jongliert mit einem Sorgerechtsstreit und einem schlecht bezahlten Medien-Vollzeitjob – worüber sie sich beim Online-Sexarbeiter Trevor ausheult, der ihr empathisch zuhört, solange sie ihn bezahlt. Bis Trevor plötzlich bei ihrer Camsex-Session entführt wird. Kurze Zeit später kriegt sie einen Anruf, dass sie 15.000 Dollar zahlen soll, um ihn freizukaufen. Von der Polizei wird sie mit dem Hinweis, dass das sicher Betrug ist, abgewimmelt. Als sie nicht zahlt, wird sie mit Cybersex-Aufnahmen erpresst. Da das Sorgerecht für ihre Tochter auf dem Spiel steht, nimmt sie die Sache selbst in die Hand und spürt anhand von ein paar wackeligen Screenshots und einer Überweisung die Erpresser*innen auf. Sie beherrscht alle Techniken der Open-Source-Recherche, ist kreativ und fokussiert, wenn es darum geht, die Fakten herauszufinden. Bis die Frage aufkommt: Wer sind eigentlich die Scammer hinter Trevor? Während die Darstellung von Online-Sexarbeiter*innen als „Scammer“ klischeehaft ausfällt, finden sich alle menschlichen Ambivalenzen in Paulas Charakter wieder, was sicher auch Tatiana Maslanys schauspielerischem Können zu verdanken ist. Paula wird von einer Mischung aus Erpressung, Gewalt und Tatendrang weiter in den Scam hineingezogen, bis sie der ziemlich nutzlosen Polizei immer verdächtiger erscheint. Dabei will Paula nach eigenen Angaben nur eine gute Mutter sein und legt sich dafür regelmäßig mit ihrem Ex-Mann Karl (Jake Johnson) an. Neben all dem coacht sie die Fußballmannschaft ihrer Tochter bis zum Gewinn und scheint immer kurz vor einer Beförderung zu stehen. Neben all dem coacht sie die Fußballmannschaft ihrer Tochter bis zum Gewinn und scheint immer kurz vor einer Beförderung zu stehen. Wenn sie nur ihre Unschuld beweisen und die große Verschwörung aufdecken …

author: Unknown
title: Dilek Şen’in isyanı, cinsiyetçi küfürler ve Çiğdem Aydın’ın anması
content:
“Ben Dilek Şen. Bu kez sana bir gazeteci olarak değil, adalet arayan bir yurttaş olarak yazıyorum. Çünkü AKP’ye geçen Cemil Tugay’ın yönettiği İzmir Büyükşehir Belediyesi, evimizi apar topar yıkmaya çalışıyor. Annemle babam, 86 ve 89 yaşlarındaki nenemle dedem, ellerinde büyüdüğüm komşularım, en ağır işlerde çalışarak yaptıkları evleri boşaltıyor.”


Bu kez “Kadınların Gündeminde” kuş olup daldan dala konacağız. Gündemleştirilmesi gereken çok konu var malum memleket çelişkiler, tutarsızlıklar ve hak ihlalleri cennetindeyiz! Bence cinnetindeyiz!


Hemen Dilek Şen’den başlayalım. Dilek günlerdir sesini duyurmak için çırpınıyor. Bir gazeteci olarak, bu memlekette kendisine yapılan büyük bir haksızlığın duyulmasını, görülmesini istiyor. Nasıl çırpındığına hepimiz şahidiz. Ne var ki birçokları gibi onun da çabaları görünmedi, isyanı duyulmadı. Evleri yıkıldı.


İzmir Büyükşehir Belediyesi (İzBB), İzmir’in Buca ilçesinde, Bulgaristan göçmeni ailelerin yaşadığı altı apartmanı yıktı. 


Dilek, hemen her gün bölgeden haber aktarıyor, fotoğraflar paylaşıyor. Bugünkü paylaşımlarından birinde, “Kırmızı boyalı odam” diyerek evlerinin yıkılan bir bölümünü gösterdi.


Dilek’ten ilk mesaj geldiğinde bu yıkımın kentsel dönüşüm, depreme hazırlık ya da benzeri bir gerekçeyle yapıldığını düşündüm. Bunun dışında insanların evleri neden yıkılsın ki?


Yol yapımıymış.


Altı aileyi bu kadar kolay gözden çıkarabiliyorlar. Peki, bu aileler ne yapacak? Bazı ailelere karşı böyle şeyleri yapmak neden bu kadar kolay?


Bizim memlekette bir söz vardır "Derdumi diyeceğim hiç derdi olmiyene". Yani herkesin derdi var fakat cidden bazılarının bu memlekette yüzü hiç gülmeyecek.


Düşüsenize biraz rahat edelim, vatanımıza gidelim demişler, kılı kırk yarmışlar, memleketin kaymağını yiyenlerin aksine dürüstçe, emek emek evlerini yapmışlar ve bir gün aman yol geçecek bilmem ne olacak, belki bir AVM yapılacak diye evleri başına yıkılmış. Bu hangi düzenin adaletidir? 


"Eylül ayı boyunca Çevre ve Şehircilik Bakanlığı yetkilileri dahil her yere ulaştık. Fakat herkes kayıtsız kaldı. Meğer Cemil Tugay’ın ‘bağımsız’ son görev günleriymiş!" diyor, Gazeteci Dilek Şen. Şöyle devam ediyor:


“Ben 1989’daki zorunlu göçle Bulgaristan’dan Türkiye’ye sığınmış ve İzmir Buca’da 30 yılı aşkın süredir aynı mahallede yaşayan bir ailenin ferdiyim. Evimizin bulunduğu arsa yol bahanesiyle 2019’da kamulaştırıldı. Avukatlar ‘Kazanılamayacak dava’ deyince mecburen kamulaştırmanın iptali yerine bedele itiraz davası açtık. Çünkü onca yıllık emeğimizin karşılığını almayı ve olabildiğince uzun süre mahallemizde yaşamayı istiyorduk. Zaten Kamulaştırma Kanunu da ‘Gerçek bedel ödenir’ diyor.


2024’te bedel davası sonuçlandı ve hak sahiplerine 25 bin TL ila 320 bin TL arasında paralar depo edildi. En son evlerimize 21 Ağustos 2026 tarihli tahliye muhtırası getirildi. 85 yaş üstü, yatağa bağlı yaşlılarımızın da bulunduğu evlerimiz için 15 günlük tahliye baskısı kuruldu. 


"Dava açtık"


Asıl bedel tespiti davamız istinafta, icraya itirazımız ise Yargıtay’da sürüyor. CHP’den seçilen Cemil Tugay, 1 Ekim 2024’teki yüz yüze görüşmemizde istinaf mahkemesi kararının bekleneceği sözünü dört yurttaşın gözünün içine bakarak vermişti. O söz tutulmadı, tutulmuyor."


Dertlerini anlatıp çözüm bulamayınca yargıya başvurmuşlar. Şöyle anlatıyor o süreci de: 


Birkaç hafta önce, 8 Ekim’de bir dava daha açtık. Çünkü öğrendik ki esas neden yol değilmiş. Mesele, bizim hisseli tapuya sahip olduğumuz arsamızı müteahhide götürmemizin önünü açmak, komşularımızla aramızda çatışma yaratıp tüm parseli boşaltmak ve buraya 15 katlı bir TİCK (Ticaret-Konut) yapmakmış! 14 Mayıs’ta onaylanan imar planı revizyonu, parselimizi ‘boş arazi’ gibi düşünüp haritalandırmış. Bu planda Dr. Cemil Tugay adına İzBB Başkan Vekili Dr. Zafer Levent Yıldırım’ın, Buca Belediye Başkanı Görkem Duman’ın, dönemin İzBB Başkanı Tunç Soyer adına dönemin Harita ve CBS Dairesi Başkanı M. Kubilay Yıldırım’ın ve teknik heyetlerin imzaları bulunuyor.”


Kadınları evsiz bırakmak, yaşlı insanlara bu uygulamaları reva görmek, tam olarak kapitalist sistemin normallikleri olur. Kapitalizmin normali elbette yaşamın anormalidir!


***


Diğer konu, pelesenk gibi dillere dolanan “3 harfli” küfürler.


Şöyle ki, geçen gün yani 6 Kasım’da  Gençlik Komünleri’nden öğrenciler YÖK'ü ve çocuk emeği sömürüsünün devlet eliyle meşrulaştırıldığı MESEM'leri proteso etti.

author: Wütende Flintas*
title: Patriarchale Strukturen und Täterschutz in Hannover
content:
Wir sind wütende FLINTA*s aus Hannover. Wütend auf patriarchale Gewalt, auf Mackertum in linken Strukturen und auf diejenigen, die sich nach außen feministisch geben, während sie im eigenen Umfeld wegschauen. Und wir haben keine Lust mehr, dazu zu schweigen.


Am 18.10. veröffentlichte das Offene Antifa Café (OAC) Hannover gemeinsam mit dem „FLINTA Bündnis“ einen Aufruf zum gemeinsamen Bannermalen anlässlich des 25. November, dem internationalen Tag gegen patriarchale Gewalt.


Ein Aufruf, der uns fassungslos und wütend macht.


Denn während das OAC nach außen feministische Kämpfe unterstützt, erleben wir seit Jahren, wie in seinem Umfeld patriarchale Gewalt relativiert, Tätern der Rücken gestärkt und Betroffene im Stich gelassen werden.


Feminismus ist kein Banner, das mensch einmal im Jahr hochhält, um sich anschließend wieder mit den eigenen Mackern gutzustellen.


Aus Rücksicht auf die betroffenen FLINTA*s werden wir an dieser Stelle bewusst keine detaillierten Schilderungen der Gewalterfahrungen veröffentlichen. Ihre Geschichten gehören ihnen. Niemand ist verpflichtet, eigene Traumata öffentlich auszubreiten, damit patriarchale Gewalt endlich ernst genommen wird.


Was wir aber benennen wollen, ist der Umgang mit den Vorwürfen und den beschuldigten Personen.


In einem der uns bekannten Fälle wurde eine Person nach unserem Kenntnisstand wegen Gewalt gegen eine FLINTA* gerichtlich verurteilt. Trotzdem ist für uns bis heute keine klare Distanzierung des OAC von dieser Person erkennbar.


Wie weit die Solidarität mit Beschuldigten im Umfeld des OAC reicht, zeigte sich aus unserer Sicht auch am Rande der Demonstration „Nazizentren dichtmachen“. Nachdem Ordner*innen die betreffende Person von der Demonstration ausgeschlossen hatten, solidarisierten sich dem OAC nahestehende Personen unter Protest mit ihr und verließen anschließend gemeinsam die Demonstration.


Anstatt den Ausschluss zu respektieren, wurde öffentlich Solidarität mit der ausgeschlossenen Person gezeigt.


Was ist eine feministische Haltung wert, wenn sie genau dort aufhört, wo es um die eigenen Freunde und Genossen geht?


Für uns steht dieser Vorfall nicht isoliert. Seit Jahren bestehen enge Verbindungen zwischen dem OAC-Umfeld und einem Kreis von Graffiti-Malern, dessen Umgang mit patriarchalem Verhalten wir als zutiefst problematisch erleben. Gegen mehrere Personen aus diesem Umfeld wurden in den vergangenen Jahren Vorwürfe erhoben. Konsequenzen blieben nach unserer Wahrnehmung in vielen Fällen aus.


Es geht uns dabei nicht um eine vermeintliche moralische Reinheit linker Räume. Es geht um Verantwortung. Um die Frage, ob Betroffene ernst genommen werden oder ob persönliche Freundschaften, Szenezugehörigkeit und die eigene politische Reputation am Ende schwerer wiegen.


Patriarchale Gewalt ist kein Problem, das nur außerhalb unserer Strukturen existiert. Sie verschwindet nicht, weil Menschen sich Antifaschist*innen nennen, linke Parolen rufen oder feministische Sticker verkleben. Auch linke Räume sind durchzogen von patriarchalen Machtverhältnissen, Männerbünden und Schweigestrukturen.


Gerade deshalb ist es notwendig, das eigene Umfeld zu hinterfragen, statt Gewaltvorwürfe als unangenehme Störung des Szenealltags zu behandeln.


Wer feministische Kämpfe für sich beansprucht, muss sich auch dann mit patriarchaler Gewalt auseinandersetzen, wenn die Vorwürfe die eigenen Genossen betreffen.


Wir sind es leid, dass FLINTA*s in vermeintlich emanzipatorischen Räumen immer wieder selbst dafür kämpfen müssen, ernst genommen zu werden. Wir sind es leid, dass der Schutz Betroffener zur Verhandlungssache wird, sobald die beschuldigte Person gut vernetzt ist. Und wir sind es leid, dass diejenigen, die diese Widersprüche ansprechen, häufig mehr Widerstand erfahren als die Strukturen, die sie kritisieren.


Besonders bitter ist es, wenn wir uns nicht einmal bei einem Vorbereitungstreffen zum Tag gegen patriarchale Gewalt darauf verlassen können, dass die beteiligten Strukturen selbst eine konsequent antipatriarchale Haltung vertreten.


Der 25. November ist kein Tag für feministische Selbstdarstellung. Er ist ein Kampftag gegen patriarchale Gewalt. Ein Tag, an dem Betroffene und ihre Perspektiven im Mittelpunkt stehen sollten – nicht das Bedürfnis linker Gruppen, sich ein feministisches Image zu geben.


Antipatriarchale Praxis beginnt nicht beim Bannermalen. Sie beginnt dort, wo Solidarität unbequem wird.

author: Chris Walker
title: AIPAC-Funded House Dem Loses to DSA-Backed Challenger in California
content:
Angela Gonzales-Torres is one of at least six DSA-backed candidates to win election to Congress this week.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Angela Gonzales-Torres, a Democratic candidate for Congress in California who is endorsed by the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), has defeated establishment Democrat Rep. Jimmy Gomez, who has been in office since 2017.

As of Thursday morning, Gonzales-Torres led Gomez by 18.4 points, with 74 percent of the vote in so far. The race has been called by all major news networks.

A noted community organizer, Gonzales-Torres has been involved in progressive politics since she was a teenager.

“Some of my earliest memories were fighting the Afghanistan and Iraq invasions,” she said in an interview last month. Besides being anti-war, Gonzales-Torres has also advocated for affordable housing measures in the Los Angeles area, the abolition of ICE, and Medicare for All.

She is one of at least six DSA-endorsed candidates to have won their elections to Congress as part of Tuesday’s midterm elections.

Both candidates have at least some progressive bona fides. But earlier this year, it was announced that the House Ethics Committee had opened an investigation into Gomez over sexual abuse allegations.

Gomez has admitted to making “personal mistakes” outside of his marriage, and has long been accused of having extramarital affairs with House staffers. House rules forbid lawmakers from having relationships with their staff, but a loophole in the rule allows members of Congress to have relationships with other members’ workers.

The inquiry was officially announced this summer. According to a lawyer representing a woman involved in the case, Gomez is under investigation by a House committee for “sexual harassment and assault.” The congressman maintains that any relationships he’s had have been consensual.

Responding to the allegations during the campaign, Gonzales-Torres called on Gomez to resign, and said it was time to “get creeps out of office.”

Beyond those allegations, however, the two candidates differed in other ways, particularly on the issue of Israel and its continued genocide of Palestinians in Gaza.

Although Gomez has called for a ceasefire in the region, he has expressed strong support for Israel, and opposed legislation that would restrict U.S. arms sales to that country. And while Gonzales-Torres has refused to take any money from the pro-Israel political action committee AIPAC, Gomez has received $2.6 million from the group during the campaign.

Announcing her victory on Tuesday night, Gonzales-Torres promised to represent voters instead of special interests while serving in Congress.

“Los Angeles doesn’t belong to AIPAC, Los Angeles doesn’t belong to Crypto or Big AI, Los Angeles doesn’t belong to corporate real estate developers. It belongs to us,” she said in a statement on X.

author: La Zarzamora
title: La Chilean Horror Story, nuevas temporadas
content:
El mal sigue aquí. 56 engendros, extorsionadores de mujeres, violadores, pedófilos y torturadores de la DINA-CNI, responsables de marcar a sus víctimas con cuchillos de combate, amarrarlos a rieles y tirarlos vivos al mar, de violar y abusar sexualmente, fueron liberados por la Kasta gobernante y están listos para reincidir.

En este thriller maldito, la Kasta está siendo coherente con sus siniestras convicciones y su maligna esencia blancona. Es la Chilean Horror Story, en la que calzan perfecto: dictadura, “Colonia Dignidad”, Paul Schäfer, Spiniak, “los coroneles” de la derecha, los decretos de libertad a criminales, y el alienado proyecto de ley de la escalofriante Vanessa Kaiser contra las víctimas.

Son crímenes inmortales de la continuación del horror político de “los nuevos padres fundadores” de los años 70 y 80, coordinados por el funesto subsecretario general de Pinochet, Jovino Novoa, el psicópata serial Paul Shäfer y los demonios de la DINA-CNI, que usaban como cuartel general de violaciones y otras torturas, la pedófila “Colonia Dignidad”.

No es casual que 20 años más tarde, en 2002, se inaugurara el siglo XXI con el sacrificio de niños y niñas de clases pobres, una nueva temporada de horror pedófilo por el mismo protagonista de la anterior, Jovino Novoa, esta vez acompañado por los libertinos vejadores Carlos Bombal de la Unión Demócrata Independiente y Nelson Ávila del Partido Radical; y dirigidos por el escatófilo Spiniak (pedófilo invitado).

El sacrificio fue quitada de cartelera informándose que Novoa, Bombal y Avila habrían sido “falsamente” acusados. Sin embargo, fue una generación que también en los años 90 albergó demonios torturadores y pedófilos organizados en el estado, especialmente los perturbados “Amigos de la Colonia Dignidad”. Algunos ya están muertos vivos como el asesinado, pero no menos maligno, ideólogo de la dictadura Jaime Guzmán; también, los “malditos Sergios”: dos ministros del interior de Pinochet, Sergio Onofre Jarpa y Sergio Fernández, y el grotesco delegado en la ONU, Sergio Diez. Y siguen vivos muchos “vampiros amigos” del Paul Schäfer” que traspasan siglos: Hernán Larraín Fernández, ministro de justicia y “derechos humanos” del piñerismo2 junto al conspirador Andrés Chadwick Piñera, ministro del interior de la misma masacre, el piñerismo2, ambos responsables de mutilaciones y violaciones a manifestantes del estallido.

Chadwick además, integra los “coroneles”, pilares del poder de los fundadores de la derecha, junto a Juan Antonio Coloma, quien fuese base “juvenil” de la dictadura, y también junto a Pablo Longueira, el mismo que habla con espectros. No hay que olvidar a las estrellas femeninas como la implacable -ya desaparecida- Mónica Madariaga, ministra de justicia y de educación de la dictadura, que dio el visto bueno a la constitución de Pinochet junto a Guzmán, ni debemos dejar fuera a la ambiciosa -y muy viva- Evelyn Matthei, reciente ex candidata presidencial, candidateándose otra vez, y defensora -solapada- de la criminal junta de gobierno, del golpe de estado y de la dictadura en que participó su padre. Todas y todos son villanos políticos, fríos y calculadores, además de grandes amigos de la pedófila “Colonia Dignidad” de Schäfer.

Nueva temporada: “La liberación”

La línea de la historia chilena del horror que continúan los padres fundadores-Generación Z, es innegable. En este inolvidable octubre 2026 de la Kasta, Fernando Rabat Celis, ministro de Justicia, Luis Silva Irarrazaval, vicepresidente del partido republicano y ahora ex subsecretario de Justicia, y Pablo Mira Hurtado, subsecretario subrogante, firmaron los decretos de liberación de sus engendros y mintieron diciendo que estaban “obligados” por una doctrina inexistente de la Corte Suprema, misma institución judicial que, apurada, mediante un fallo, los desmintió.

Ninguno de los criminales liberados por ellos había presentado individualmente un recurso de amparo porque los pedófilos están informados de sus derechos. author: rti_admin
title: Miss X Versus Late Rekha Waghmare: The Selective Outrage of Telangana Civil Society
content:
In Telangana, the term “civil society” evokes images of principled activism: women’s groups marching for justice, human rights organisations amplifying marginalised voices, and political parties channelling public anger into demands for accountability. Yet this activism reveals a troubling selectivity when the victim belongs to a Scheduled Caste (SC) community, especially a vulnerable migrant labourer. The stark contrast between the high-profile handling of the Miss X POCSO case and the alleged gang-rape and murder of Late Rekha Waghmare exposes what can only be described as caste-driven hypocrisy. Telangana’s so-called civil society functions less as a beacon of universal justice and more as a caste society indifferent, even complicit, when atrocities target SC “untouchable” communities.

The Miss X Case: Swift Action, Political Storm, and Current Legal Position

In May 2026, Bandi Sai Bhageerath, son of Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Bandi Sanjay Kumar, faced serious criminal allegations under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act and relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). The complaint, lodged on May 8, 2026, by the mother of Miss X, a 17-year-old girl, accused him of repeated sexual harassment, assault, emotional manipulation, and coercive acts over several months at various locations, including a farmhouse in Moinabad.

Despite his father’s prominent political standing, the initial state machinery moved with noticeable readiness. Following an intense police manhunt and the issuance of a lookout notice, Telangana police arrested Bhageerath on May 16, 2026. He was remanded to judicial custody, subjected to custodial police interrogation, and the investigation proceeded swiftly amidst massive public scrutiny. Protests erupted across Hyderabad and throughout the state; women’s groups, student organisations, and opposition parties (including BRS, CPI, and others) staged aggressive dharnas and demonstrations demanding accountability and an impartial Special Investigation Team (SIT) probe. The media covered every twist and turn relentlessly, ensuring that political patronage could not quietly bury the case.

Regarding the latest position in the case, after spending over 50 days in judicial detention, Bandi Sai Bhageerath approached the Telangana High Court seeking regular bail. On July 9, 2026, Justice K. Sujana of the Telangana High Court granted him regular bail subject to strict conditions. Following his release on bail, Bhageerath moved the High Court seeking orders to restrain social media platforms and mainstream media outlets from publishing defamatory content or reporting prejudicial material concerning the POCSO case, in which the High Court subsequently passed interim restraining directions and sought counter-affidavits from the respondents. While the prosecution’s trial process and chargesheet proceedings continue under the statutory oversight of the special POCSO court, the case stands out as a prime instance where public mobilisation, political contention, and intense civil society pressure forced law enforcement to register the FIR promptly, arrest a powerful minister’s son, and hold custodial interrogation.

The Late Rekha Waghmare Case: Systemic Silence, Cover-Up, and Institutional Apathy.

At roughly the same time, an appalling horror unfolded in Donkeshwar village, Nandipet Mandal, Nizamabad district. Late Rekha Waghmare, a 32-year-old Scheduled Caste woman and migrant agricultural labourer hailing from Patoda Khurd village in Dharmabad Taluka, Nanded district, Maharashtra, was found dead under highly suspicious circumstances on the afternoon of February 13, 2026.

Since 2021, Rekha and her husband, Devidas Waghmare, along with their two young daughters (Jeevika, aged 10, and Sona, aged 8), had been living in a small shed on the agricultural land of a local influential landlord, Barla Narsing Reddy, working on a salaried labour basis. According to the consistent representations submitted by Rekha’s brother-in-law, Sri S. Sanjeev, the landlord had repeatedly harassed Rekha and attempted to exploit her. On February 13, 2026, Narsing Reddy intentionally sent Devidas away to work at another distant agricultural plot with strict orders not to return until all work was finished. The children were away at school. Taking advantage of Rekha being completely alone, Barla Narsing Reddy and his associate, Vittal Empalwad (or Emphalwar), allegedly broke into the …

author: Mag
title: Frauen in Argentinien gegen die Kettensäge, Femizide und den Machismo: „Ni una Menos“ (Nicht eine weniger)
content:
Dossier


„

Wieder einmal haben sich die Frauen und verschiedenen Bildungsarbeiterinnen von CTERA der feministischen und transfeministischen Bewegung angeschlossen und unter dem Slogan „Ni una Menos“ gegen Femizide, Transfemizide und Transvestizide im ganzen Land, im Rahmen unserer CTA-T und durch alle Basisorganisationen von CTERA, diese Forderung, die vor 9 Jahren auf die Straße ging, begleitet. (…) „Hass und Hunger töten“, gewalttätige, fremdenfeindliche, frauenfeindliche, diskriminierende, verleugnende, antifeministische und LGBT+-hassende Diskurse sind das, was tagtäglich in unserer Gesellschaft zirkuliert, ausgehend von denen, die uns regieren, einer Regierung, die es sich zur Aufgabe gemacht hat, öffentliche Politiken mit einer Gender- und Diversity-Perspektive im Hinblick auf die Menschenrechte zu entleeren

…“ Aus dem span.

Aufruf bei der Bildungsgewerkschaft CTERA

 (maschinenübersetzt) zu landesweiten Frauenprotesten am 3. Juni 2024 – siehe mehr zum Thema und Hintergründe:


„Nos falta Nancy“: Bildungsgewerkschaft CTERA hatte am 29. Oktober zu landesweitem Lehrkräftestreik und Protesten in ganz Argentinien nach Femizid an Lehrerin Nancy aufgerufen


Femizid an Lehrerin führt zu Protesten in Argentinien


„

Buenos Aires/Esquina. Im ganzen Land hat der Gewerkschaftsverband der Lehrkräfte (CTERA) in Argentinien am vergangenen Donnerstag infolge des Femizids an der Lehrerin Nancy Godoy zu einem nationalen Trauertag und zu Streiks aufgerufen. Die Protestierenden zogen in verschiedenen Provinzen, darunter Buenos Aires, Corrientes und Córdoba, durch die Straßen und machten mit Bannern und Schildern, auf denen „Nos falta Nancy“ (Nancy fehlt uns) zu lesen war, auf den Mord an der Lehrerin aufmerksam. Mit dem Fall rücken auch die Bedingungen in den Fokus, unter denen Lehrkräfte in ländlichen Regionen arbeiten. Godoy selbst hatte sich gegen die Missstände ausgesprochen.


Die 52-Jährige war stellvertretende Leiterin der ländlichen Schule Nr. 626 im Paraje El Malezal in der subtropischen Provinz Corrientes im Nordosten Argentiniens. Unter der Woche blieb sie dort, da der Weg nach Hause bis zu drei Stunden dauerte. Mobil- und Satellitenempfang gibt es in dieser Gegend oft nicht. Ihre letzte Meldung an einen ihrer Söhne erfolgte daher rund eine Woche, bevor diese sie am 7. Oktober als vermisst meldeten. Am vergangenen Mittwoch fand die Polizei ihre Leiche. Laut vorläufigem Obduktionsbericht hatte sie Stichverletzungen und Abwehrverletzungen. Fünf Personen wurden festgenommen, gegen drei wird wegen Femizids ermittelt, gegen zwei der drei unbegrenzte Untersuchungshaft angeordnet. Gegen zwei weitere Tatverdächtige ermittelt die Staatsanwaltschaft wegen eines Tötungsdeliktes bzw. Falschaussage. Der Anwalt der Familie, Gustavo Briend, sprach von einem „Akt absoluter Barbarei“ und geht davon aus, dass mehrere Personen beteiligt waren. author: S. Baum
title: Justice Department Official Who Led Attacks on Gender-Affirming Care Resigns
content:
Brett Shumate is the fourth DOJ official to resign since the midterms after leading investigations that pressured hospitals to end care for trans minors.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Brett Shumate has become the fourth Department of Justice official to join the post-election exodus from the agency following Republicans’ crushing midterm defeat — marking the end of the tenure of a man who helped grease the wheels of the anti-trans machine.

“The rats are fleeing the sinking ship,” Alejandra Caraballo, a lawyer and trans rights scholar, posted on Bluesky, alongside news that Shumate, the Assistant Attorney General for the Civil Division, was resigning.

Under Shumate’s leadership, the DOJ aggressively targeted providers of gender-affirming care, subpoenaing patient records and waging False Claims Act investigations to intimidate hospitals. This caused some major hospitals to end care for trans minors and pay millions in settlements to the government. He was also instrumental in defending these actions in court against claims they were unlawful government overreach.

No hospital or clinic has been successfully sued because it provides evidence-based medicine, but some of them signed agreements with the DOJ to stave off the worst of federal threats: the demand that providers hand over identifiable patient data about thousands of transgender children and their families. Not all of these investigations or deals have been public.

Still, hospitals shut down their gender-affirming care programs for trans youth, leaving care deserts across the country. Lower courts condemned the government’s ploy, with one Boston judge calling it “a fishing expedition.” In a similar Rhode Island case, another judge said the DOJ — under Shumate’s leadership at the time — “has proven unworthy of this trust at every point in this case.”

In June 2025, Shumate issued a memo directing Civil Division employees to prioritize attacks on gender-affirming care, courtesy of the whims of President Donald Trump and then-Attorney General Pam Bondi, who was ousted in April. Shumate’s memo announced the Civil Division will “prioritize investigations of doctors, hospitals, pharmaceutical companies, and other appropriate entities” that ostensibly violate Trump’s declarations about transgender youth care. “In addition, the Civil Division will aggressively pursue claims under the False Claims Act against health care providers that bill the federal government for impermissible services.”

This largely included providers of wholly legal gender-affirming care, even in blue states — such as Children’s Hospital Los Angeles in California and Mount Sinai Hospital in New York. There is no federal ban on gender-affirming care.

Attorney General Todd Blanche, in announcing Shumate’s departure on X, praised him for “shutter[ing] dozens of clinics” for gender-affirming care.

The DOJ also saw the departure of Harmeet Dhillon, who led the Civil Rights Division, and whose firm previously represented “ex-trans” activist Chloe Cole in her lawsuit against Kaiser Permanente for providing gender-affirming care.

Jason Reding Quiñones, U.S. attorney for the Southern District of Florida, and John Eisenberg, assistant attorney general for the National Security Division, also resigned. The department is also reeling from general attrition of staff throughout. The DOJ is not likely to stop pursuing political targets, including trans people and their caretakers and doctors, but if nothing else, the turmoil at the DOJ is liable to make it less effective. Under Trump, “a drastically diminished Justice Department workforce is struggling to keep up with its civil side caseloads,” The Hill found.

“A series of charts, apparently inadvertently shared and then recalled, show how the number of attorneys within the civil division has plummeted under the Trump administration.” This may slow down some of the destructive efforts by the DOJ — going after lawful gender-affirming care providers, defending the government from lawsuits over human rights violations. But others question how this might shape the department politically as new hires grow increasingly conservative and less qualified or willing to defy unlawful orders. Other important targets of the DOJ, such as those guilty of terrorism or white-collar crime, may also benefit from less competence in oversight.

A replacement for Shumate has not yet been announced.
