author: rezgar2
title: The Dark Side of the “Machine God”: 5 Unsettling Truths About Big Tech’s AI Obsession
content:
Silicon Valley routinely promises a sparkling utopia where artificial intelligence will cure complex diseases, optimize global labor, and render the very concept of money obsolete. Yet behind the polished keynotes and corporate public relations, a far more unsettling reality is taking shape. A small handful of ultra-wealthy tech oligarchs, the heads of Meta, Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, and xAI, are making unilateral decisions about the collective future of humanity, operating entirely outside democratic oversight or public accountability.

Silicon Valley routinely promises a sparkling utopia where artificial intelligence will cure complex diseases, optimize global labor, and render the very concept of money obsolete. Yet behind the polished keynotes and corporate public relations, a far more unsettling reality is taking shape. A small handful of ultra-wealthy tech oligarchs, the heads of Meta, Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, and xAI, are making unilateral decisions about the collective future of humanity, operating entirely outside democratic oversight or public accountability.

This concentration of power exposes a jarring central paradox: the exact same tech CEOs who claim AI will solve humanity’s greatest challenges simultaneously warn that the technology could trigger civilizational extinction, openly describing their pursuit as “summoning the demon.” Rather than pausing development, these executives have accelerated an apocalyptic arms race to build ultra-powerful systems, framing themselves as indispensable guardians of human survival.

To understand where artificial intelligence is truly taking society, we must look past corporate marketing and examine the underlying worldviews, historical lineages, and material harms driving the tech elite. Moving beyond superficial consumer hype reveals how a toxic mix of fringe ideologies, extractive labor practices, and authoritarian state alliances is steering Silicon Valley toward what critical theorists and legal scholars call “techno-fascism.”

To make sense of Silicon Valley’s relentless drive toward Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) and Artificial Superintelligence (ASI), one must understand the bizarre ideological framework shaping its leaders. Coined by philosopher Emile Torres and computer scientist Timnit Gebru, the acronym TESCREAL encapsulates a bundle of tightly interwoven worldviews: Transhumanism, Extropianism, Singularitarianism, Cosmism, Rationalism, Effective Altruism, and Longtermism.

Dr. Emile Torres highlights a critical historical truth at the heart of this ideology: transhumanism is fundamentally “eugenics on steroids.” Unlike nineteenth-century eugenics, which sought merely to optimize the existing human species through selective breeding, transhumanism seeks to use radical technology to completely replace and transcend humanity, engineering an entirely new posthuman species. Within Silicon Valley AI circles, this hypothetical superintelligence is explicitly referred to as a “Machine God.” Tech CEOs effectively act as high priests, competing to bring an all-knowing digital deity into physical existence.

This radical ideology shapes corporate roadmaps in concrete, disturbing ways:

Sam Altman (OpenAI): In a blog post titled “The Merge,” Altman argued that AI surpassing human intellect is inevitable, framing un-merged human beings as a temporary “biological bootloader” for digital intelligence that will ultimately fade into an evolutionary side-branch. Altman notably paid $10,000 to join a brain-uploading waitlist with Nectome and co-founded a brain-computer interface venture to facilitate digital integration.

Ray Kurzweil & Demis Hassabis (DeepMind): Representing Extropianism and Singularitarianism, Kurzweil champions the doctrine of living long enough to achieve digital immortality, targeting a self-improving “singularity” by 2032. Hassabis, DeepMind’s co-founder, operates under a similar singularitarian impulse to engineer self-evolving intellect.

Eliezer Yudkowsky (Rationalism): A foundational figure in modern rationalist thought who famously posited a utilitarian moral calculation arguing that forcing a single person to endure 50 years of relentless torture is ethically preferable to an unfathomable number of people experiencing the mild inconvenience of a speck of dust in their eye.

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "Birds of War": New Film Tells a Story of Love and Journalism from Syria to Lebanon
content:
We speak with Janay Boulos and Abd Alkader Habak, filmmakers and subjects of the new documentary

Birds of War

, which tells their epic love story through years of upheaval in the Middle East. Boulos, a London-based Lebanese journalist working for the

BBC

, and Habak, a Syrian activist and cameraman, first connected while covering the Syrian civil war and stayed in touch through years of war, revolution and exile, forming a relationship that is chronicled in the documentary by drawing on 13 years of their personal videos, voice notes and other correspondence.


The film also examines the unequal relationship between international news organizations and local journalists whose work they rely on, the fraught political history between Syria and Lebanon, and how Boulos and Habak’s personal connection overcame those divisions.


“Without our journalistic relationship, [we] would have never been together. I would have never opened my heart to somebody like him,” says Boulos. “We can be any race, any gender, any religion, any background, but at the same time we’re all humans.”


Birds of War

 premiered at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival, where it won the World Cinema Documentary Special Jury Award for Journalistic Impact.

author: David Swanson
title: World BEYOND War Education Director Visits Romania, Bulgaria, and Belgium to Discuss Peace, Security, and Youth Participation
content:
By Phill Gittins, World BEYOND War, November 2026


From October 26 to November 4, 2026, World BEYOND War’s Education Director, Dr. Phill Gittins, visited Romania, Bulgaria, and Belgium to meet with peace activists, speak with students and educators, and join discussions on peace, security, and youth participation.


Romania: Chapter Members and University Students


On October 28 in Bucharest, Phill met with Hans Hedrich and George Epurescu of the

World BEYOND War Romania Chapter

. They discussed local peace and anti-war organizing and ways to stay connected.


Later that day, Phill gave a presentation and joined a discussion with an international group of master’s students at the

University of Bucharest’s Faculty of Political Science

, hosted by Associate Professor Luciana Alexandra Ghica. Drawing on WBW’s forthcoming book,

From the War System to a Global Peace System

, he explored different approaches to security, alternatives to war and militarism, and the role of civil society in building peace.


Phill Gittins with Hans Hedrich and George Epurescu of the World BEYOND War Romania Chapter in Bucharest


Phill Gittins speaking with students at the University of Bucharest.


Bulgaria: Peace Education and Practical Action


On October 30, Phill spoke at

Sofia University

 with Bulgarian and international students, doctoral researchers, and faculty members. The presentation drew further on the forthcoming book and led to a lively discussion about non-military defense, including how countries facing armed aggression might protect themselves without relying solely on military force.


Afterwards, Phill spoke with Professor Tatyana Dronzina and Dr. Denitsa Hinkova who expressed interest in possible collaboration, including a summer school for young leaders from Central and Eastern Europe. The idea is to combine peace education, dialogue, and practical training with support for participants to develop projects afterwards.


That afternoon, Phill met with Denitza Vidolova of the

Sofia Platform Foundation

 to learn about its work in civic and history education, including helping teachers address Bulgaria’s communist past and polarizing issues.


While in Sofia, Phill also caught up with

Veronika Botsova

, who served as President of Rotaract Europe during the 2023–2024 term and previously collaborated with World BEYOND War on its

Peace Education and Action for Impact (PEAI)

 programme.


Students and colleagues at Sofia University.


Phill Gittins with Denitza Vidolova of the Sofia Platform Foundation.


Phill Gittins with Veronika Botsova in Sofia.


Belgium: Youth Participation and Dialogue


The final stop was Brussels, where Phill contributed to the

Voices of Change Final Conference at the European Parliament

 on November 3. The Erasmus+-supported event, delivered by

World Scouting

 and the

Erasmus Student Network

 (ESN), brought together young people, youth organizations, civil society representatives, and policymakers to discuss democracy, participation, and peacebuilding.


In a fishbowl discussion titled

“Neutral or silent?”

, Phill considered when neutrality protects dialogue and when it becomes silence in the face of injustice. As he put it: “We are clearly not neutral about war and militarism. We have a position. But having a position does not mean closing down dialogue.”


Conversations with participants from Georgia and Ukraine raised further questions about whether non-military defense could protect societies facing armed threats. The exchanges were challenging but friendly, showing how experiences of war and insecurity shape different views of what keeps people safe.


Phill also spoke with ESN and WOSM representatives about possible contributions to future regional and international student gatherings, including peace education workshops.


Meeting Erasmus Student Network representatives.


Voices of Change Final Conference at the European Parliament.


Participants at the Voices of Change conference.


The visit was also a chance to reconnect with

Donna-Marie Fry

, a WBW Advisory Board member and longtime contributor to its education courses, and Belén Luna Sanz, who took part in a peace education program Phill led in Bolivia in 2014 and now works in digital policy.


Many thanks to everyone who hosted the visits, joined the discussions, and shared their ideas.


Phill Gittins with Donna Marie Fry in Brussels.


Phill Gittins with Belén Luna Sanz in Brussels.

author: Unknown
title: “How Has Serving Impacted You?” : Veterans of the US Military in Their Own Words
content:
What is it like to serve in the United States military? If only it were possible for those who are considering enlisting to learn the unvarnished truth. In 2019, a viral

tweet

 from the official US Army twitter account unexpectedly drew over 11,000 candid replies in the course of 48 hours. These responses offer a rare window into the real experiences of servicemembers and veterans. We present a selection of them here for the benefit of anyone who is thinking about joining the military.


This is a document of an

earlier era

 of social media, captured here before it

vanishes

. You can obtain a book collecting the first twenty-four hours of responses

here

.


Just before Memorial Day in 2019, the United States Army made a strategic blunder almost on par with invading Vietnam. They posted this inquiry on their official Twitter account:


In response, veterans and their family and friends posted thousands upon thousands of tweets recounting broken promises and broken people. They described cancer, PTSD, domestic abuse, unpaid college and housing loans, Gulf War syndrome, insomnia, sexual abuse, poverty, Agent Orange, racism, nightmare disorder, unemployment, burying loved ones, misogyny, orphaned children, burn pit syndrome, homelessness, debilitating injuries, divorce, alcoholism, disappearances, a Veterans Affairs department that was unwilling or unable to help, and suicide, suicide, suicide.


The United States military is one of the largest concentrations of power in the world. With

tens of thousands

 of missiles,

millions

 of firearms, and over

5000

 nuclear weapons—about 40% of all the nuclear weapons in the world—the US military can hold the entire world hostage.


The US military is also the largest employer in the United States,

employing

 almost 2,900,000 workers—roughly 17 out of every 2000 people. If we add private military contractors like Blackwater (250,000 workers), the employees of non-combat support companies like Halliburton who build military infrastructure, provide food, and the like (150,000-250,000), US-based war manufacturers like Lockheed Martin and Boeing (1,500,000), and

veterans

 who receive disability or pension payments (2,000,000), we find that roughly 1 out of every 50 Americans is economically dependent on US militarism.


As in all industries, without this workforce, the military would grind to a halt. It especially depends on regular transfusions of young blood—young people sold stories about adventure, duty, and upward mobility.


If we were to ask new recruits why they joined, we’d

likely

 hear a mix of narratives about gaining strength, seeing the world, paying for college, serving God and country, learning life skills, continuing a family tradition, escaping poverty or an unsafe home, obtaining housing, having fun, and protecting loved ones. Most people join the military because they think it will benefit them or because they believe they are serving a higher calling.


Some recruits get to live out their dreams. Some leave instability, danger, or deprivation for a more structured and economically stable life; some even gain a sense of belonging. If they’re lucky, they serve their time without incident, then move on to free college tuition, a no-down-payment housing loan, health insurance, and a free meal at Golden Corral once a year.


But thousands of veterans’ dreams become nightmares. The promises of recruiters, family members, and Hollywood movies offer a gamble at best—a roll of the dice that

frequently

 ends with being harmed physically, psychologically, and sexually. Military service can lead to

substance abuse

,

homelessness

, and

suicide

. It can also end in unspeakable acts of violence against others, whether those be the declared enemies of the United States, noncombatants, or veterans’ own loved ones.


It is striking how many of these responses speak of being hoodwinked out of college, housing loans, and medical care—how many describe the pain of family members lost to PTSD, alcoholism, or suicide after witnessing or committing atrocities.


American media bombards us with war propaganda. Almost every video game spreads the myth that combat makes us stronger: more powerful weapons, tougher armor, a bigger health bar, greater fortunes. Hollywood promises that the hero can weather any fight—or, if he can’t, his death will be meaningful and glorious.


Statistically speaking, the more we are exposed to combat, the more likely we are to be …

author: labor4pal
title: A fightback is building as crackdown deepens against civil liberties (Workers’ Voice)
content:
Dozens of activists are accused by the federal government of contributing to bogus “criminal conspiracies.” In Minnesota, two separate conspiracy cases accuse 54 people of participating in illegal conspiracies for participating in protest and journalistic activities. The Minnesota 15, Righteous 39, Michigan 8 (now 12), Spokane 3, and Prairieland Defendants are the most well known cases in the ongoing crackdown. All of these cases are attacks on organized labor.

The California Faculty Association and the Graduate Employee Organization at University of Michigan (GEO-AFT 3550) are facing frontal attacks on their unions by the right-wing press and FBI. Doctored video of a CFA meeting was leaked to Trump booster Bari Weiss’s Free Press in an attempt to scandalize the union with false accusations of antisemitism. The Department of Justice first charged GEO President Hiab Teshome with felonious financial crimes. Those bogus charges were dropped the same day that a grand jury subpoenaed GEO’s books, including all member lists, meeting minutes, and financial records. The union is fighting to retain basic privacy rights.

Fueled by National Security Presidential Memorandum-7, U.S. intelligence and police apparatuses are being explicitly targeted at anyone standing for basic democratic rights, immigrant communities, and racial justice. As the world drifts closer to major inter-imperialist conflict and expanding zones of overt imperialist military occupation takes hold in the semi-colonies, Western imperialisms are tightening restrictions on protest, speech, and organizing for progressive movements.

While there are many additional cases of “lawfare” and anti-protest policing, it is worth taking a moment to review two of the cases mentioned above to understand the tactics and scope of the current crackdown.

Around two dozen protesters held a noise demonstration on July 4, 2025, outside of the Prairieland Detention Center in Texas. As the protest was winding down and many of the participants had left, Alvarado Police Officer Thomas Gross sped onto the scene and almost immediately aimed his gun at a demonstrator moving away from him. Video evidence indicates that Gross discharged his weapon, something that would appear to have been covered up by the judge and prosecutors.

In response to seeing a potentially lethal attack on a protester, Marine Corps veteran Benjamin “Champagne” Song let out a warning shot into the ground away from the officers. Gross went to the hospital for superficial wounds that the government alleges resulted from being shot by Song, but video evidence released after sentencing indicates Gross was likely hit by shrapnel produced from his own weapon’s discharge.

Using the presence of guns and defensive action of Song as pretext, 22 people were ultimately indicted as part of an alleged conspiracy to attack cops and carry out an armed prison break. One person, Daniel “Des” Rolando Sanchez Estrada, was not at the protest at all. Des was convicted for “corruptly concealing a document or record” and sentenced to 30 years for possessing legally protected political materials.

After arrests, pressure and legal sabotage was mounted by the judicial system against the defendants. Many were initially held in solitary confinement, with one reporting that human feces coated their cell. U.S. District Judge Mark Pittman blocked the defendants from retaining a private attorney, meaning they had to use public defenders. author: Dominic Gutoman
title: Investigate police, doctors involved in Duterte’s ‘drug war’
content:
Forensic pathologist Dr. Raquel Fortun, also a member of the commission, presents one of the questionable certificates during the commission's truth-telling session last Friday. (Truth Commission photo)

The Truth Commission has called on the Philippine government to investigate the police officers’ misconduct and promotion and the doctors’ questionable death certificates in the course of the “drug war” campaign of former President Rodrigo Duterte.

“My son was alive when they arrested him, but they killed him. They could’ve let him live. They did not show mercy, they planted drugs and guns,” Marissa Lazaro, mother of extrajudicial killing victim Cristopher Lazaro, said in Tagalog during the commission’s truth-telling session.

The Truth Commission pointed to a failed system for investigating deaths, marked by careless police and forensic work, and little concern for victims’ families. Lazaro’s account also showed that the police officers were asking money from her, indicating a potential trail of corruption.

Cristopher, 20, and Alberto Paragas, 32, died in police operations on August 5, 2017 in Marilao, Bulacan. Police reported that the two resisted (nanlaban) after an alleged attempted holdup. Cristopher’s friends also died hours earlier in Bocaue, a separate town in Bulacan.

Lazaro added, “They asked me to sign a waiver, indicating that I consented to their illegal operation. I did not sign it. They told me: the day will come that I will seek their help. I told them, what help could you give my son? You killed him. He’s already dead.”

A similar incident happened to Marissa Quiamco, sister of Alberto, after she paid the P10,000 fee to release the cadaver of her brother. A police officer asked her and Alberto’s partner to sign a document, indicating consent for the operation but they refused to sign.

“I wish I could fight for my brother. Even my neighbors asked me to file a complaint. But I told them: we don’t have money. We don’t have the capacity or resources to get a lawyer,” Quiamco said during the truth-telling session. “I’m only earning enough to help my mother and father.”

In October, an analysis of public records by the Truth Commission recorded a pattern that commanding police officers were promoted and reassigned, instead of being subjected to criminal and administrative sanctions.

Lito Patay, who commanded Batasan police station that killed 108 people in drug operations during his term, was named chief of the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) in Central Luzon.

In Caloocan, the commission’s own records documented 284 killings in 2016, before the leadership of Chito Bersaluno in the City Police. During his watch, 105 more deaths were recorded from February to August 2017. He was removed from his post after the killing of Kian delos Santos. However, he was made police director of Bulacan Province in 2018 and promoted to the rank of brigadier general in 2022.

In 2020, human rights organizations flagged the reassignment of Debold Sinas, former chief of the Central Visayas Police Regional Office, to the National Capital Region. The Commission on Human Rights (CHR) Regional Office said back then that Sinas’ watch in Central Visayas was marred by unresolved killings linked to the illegal drugs trade and the anti-insurgency campaign “Oplan Sauron.” Duterte appointed him as the Philippine National Police Chief on November 9, 2020, serving a six-month term. A year after, he was appointed as an undersecretary of the Office of the President.

Read: [LIST] Gross human rights violations under Debold Sinas

“Any inquiry must look at promotions as closely as it looks at cash payments,” said Christopher Magno, the commission’s executive director and an expert on state violence in the Philippines. “No police officer should gain in any way from the blood of people killed outside the law.”

Former Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office (PCSO) General Manager Royina Garma, who also served as Cebu City police chief under the Duterte administration, revealed the incentivization of police officers through the “Davao Model” in a quad committee hearing of the House of Representatives in 2024.

“First is the reward if the suspect is killed. Second is the funding of planned operations. Third is the refund of operational expenses,” Garma said, stressing that the rewards started from P20,000 ($343.95) to P1 million ($17,197.50), depending on the profile of the suspects. En estos últimos días los ucranianos han tratado de intensificar sus contactos con el Sur global, lo que debe poner en alerta a las autoridades de todos nuestros países, ya que no es posible augurar nada bueno de un gobierno que apoya y estimula el nazismo, con toda su carga de racismo, supremacismo y desprecio por los pueblos no occidentales, no blancos.


El actual conflicto en Ucrania fue inducido por la OTAN, como consecuencia de su expansión hacia las fronteras rusas, violando acuerdos asumidos en 1989 entre G. Bush y M. Gorvachov. Esta es una guerra proxy de la OTAN contra Rusia a través de Ucrania.


Sin embargo, ya está claro que Occidente no podrá infligir una derrota estratégica a Rusia y que las “sanciones” occidentales han hecho más daño a Europa que a Rusia, la cual ha demostrado sus capacidades económicas, militares, políticas y diplomáticas, logrando hacer crecer su producción en todos los sectores de la industria, incluyendo el militar, manteniendo un altísimo nivel de apoyo político del pueblo ruso, incrementando su presencia en el ámbito internacional, principalmente en el BRICS, la Organización de Cooperación de Shanghai, la Unión Económica Euro Asiática y profundizando los lazos bilaterales con buena parte de las naciones africanas, asiáticas y latinoamericanas.


Mientras tanto Ucrania está sumida en un pozo sin fondo de corrupción, de ilegalidad democrática y de una dependencia absoluta de los suministros militares y financieros del Occidente colectivo. Samstag, 21.11.2026

Unterer Marktplatz, 25548 Kellinghusen

Rideshare-Tool

Jetzt einsteigen!

Warum demonstrieren wir?

Anlass für die Großdemo am 21. November ist unsere aktuelle Veröffentlichung „Töten im Takt – Die grausamste Maschine bei Tönnies“. Tönnies ist Deutschlands größter Schlachtkonzern und gilt als eines der mächtigsten Unternehmen der europäischen Fleischindustrie. Als Marktführer tötet Tönnies jedes Jahr 16 Millionen Schweine. Unsere Aufdeckung zeigt den grausamen Erstickungskampf der Tiere in der CO₂-Anlage. Die Schweine schreien vor Angst und versuchen zu fliehen.


Was wir bisher getan haben

Gewalt im Schlachthof aufgedeckt

Verstöße dokumentiert

Tönnies angezeigt

Eine große Welle an Presseberichten ausgelöst

Zahlreiche Interviews geführt

Eine politische und gesellschaftliche Debatte angestoßen

Bei der Tönnies-Zentrale in Rheda-Wiedenbrück protestiert

Hintergrundinfos

Und jetzt?

Die Gewalt im Schlachthaus geht unvermindert weiter! Wir sind wütend. Deshalb fahren wir jetzt nochmal ganz groß auf, bündeln unsere Kräfte an einem Termin und demonstrieren gemeinsam mit euch an genau dem Schlachthof, aus dem die Aufnahmen unserer Aufdeckung stammen:

Kellinghusen!


Unsere Forderung: Der Betrieb muss schließen!

Wir starten mit einer Auftaktkundgebung mit Redebeiträgen auf dem Unteren Marktplatz.

Demozug


Als großer und lauter Demozug ziehen wir mit Schildern, Bannern und Fahnen durch Kellinghusen, skandieren lautstark und setzen ein starkes Zeichen.

Die Demoroute führt uns bis zum Schlachthof. Dort gibt es weitere Redebeiträge.

Abschlusskundgebung


Gemeinsam laufen wir zurück zum Unteren Marktplatz, wo die Demo nach einer Abschlusskundgebung endet.

Content auf Social Media

 oder poste selbst unser Sharepic:


Demoregeln

1. Antispeziesistisch und abolitionistisch

Einen Ansatz, die Ausbeutung der Tiere zu reformieren und somit im Grundsatz beizubehalten, verfolgen wir nicht. Unsere Forderungen sind grundsätzlich antispeziesistisch und abolitionistisch. ARIWA lehnt alle Formen allgemeiner und gruppenbezogener Menschenfeindlichkeit (wie zum Beispiel Ableismus, Antisemitismus, Homo- und Trans*feindlichkeit, Rassismus oder Sexismus) sowie verschwörungsideologische Denkmuster ab. 5. Bitte keine Tiere mitbringen

title: SAVE THE SOUTH SUFFOLK ONE!
content:
Oh, wait… sorry. The Judge already did that in court.


John ‘Pinocchio’ Henty’s case ends in acquittal

.


Thank you to


South Suffolk Hunt Sabs


for this guest article.


A court case brought by former Essex & Suffolk Hunt huntsman John Henty against a hunt saboteur has ended in a resounding victory for the defence, with the saboteur found NOT GUILTY.


John Henty outside court.


Following allegations made to police, former Essex & Suffolk Hunt huntsman John Henty pursued a prosecution alleging abusive and threatening behaviour under Section 5 of the Public Order Act. The case followed an incident on a quiet country lane in which Henty pursued the hunt saboteurs’ vehicle, blocked it in, approached it and attempted to provoke a reaction.


What followed was a lengthy legal process based on Henty’s account of events. However, when his evidence was examined in court, serious questions arose about the credibility of that account and whether the alleged behaviour actually amounted to a criminal offence.


A case that should never have reached court?


The Judge was highly critical of the way the case had been handled by the CPS and the police officers involved, making clear that the alleged actions did not meet the legal threshold required for a criminal offence.


Both the prosecution and the defence barrister sought to discontinue the case on more than one occasion. The case was nevertheless directed to proceed. The circumstances surrounding that decision raise serious questions about why so much time and public money were spent pursuing a prosecution that ultimately failed.


Former Essex & Suffolk Hunt huntsman John Henty is now at The Ludlow Hunt.


The evidence tells a different story


Henty submitted two video clips, recorded by himself, which were played in court. The footage showed Henty pulling his vehicle alongside the hunt saboteurs’ Land Rover, getting out of his own accord and filming the encounter.


Our saboteur told Henty to ‘f*ck off’ before closing the vehicle door. Rather than disengaging, Henty continued filming and engaging with the occupants. Despite claiming under oath that he had been alarmed and distressed, the circumstances captured on his own footage told a different story.


The prosecution was unable to produce further evidence demonstrating that Henty had experienced the alarm or distress alleged.


Henty spun a yarn of lies that should never have made it to court.


The judge’s conclusion


Having heard Henty’s evidence under cross-examination and considered the footage and relevant law, the Judge concluded that:


Henty had parked his vehicle alongside the saboteurs’ vehicle of his own accord.


He had got out of his vehicle voluntarily.


He had chosen to film the encounter.


He had continued the interaction of his own accord.


He had not contacted the police immediately, instead reporting the incident to 101 approximately two hours later.


These circumstances were central to the Judge’s assessment of Henty’s claim that he had experienced fear, alarm and distress. Following Henty’s evidence and cross-examination by the prosecution and defence, the case concluded without our hunt saboteur needing to take the stand.


The verdict

:

Not guilty. Acquitted.


After all the allegations, the police involvement, the CPS proceedings and the considerable expenditure of public resources, the case ended in an acquittal. A considerable amount of time, money and public resources had been spent pursuing this matter, only for the court to reach a conclusion that raises serious questions about why the prosecution was pursued in the first place.


Hunt saboteurs will not be intimidated out of exposing illegal hunting. And they will not be silenced by allegations that cannot withstand scrutiny in court.


The South Suffolk One stands vindicated.


SAVE THE SOUTH SUFFOLK ONE!


South Suffolk Hunt Sabs remain steadfast and will not be intimidated or silenced.

author: PETA-Team
title: Neue Aufdeckung: Kamele in Marokko für Tourismus missbraucht
content:
Recherchen von PETA Asien dokumentieren immer wieder wie

Kamele

 in der marokkanischen

Tourismusindustrie

 ausgebeutet werden. Die Tiere, die für Ausritte ausgenutzt werden, werden geschlagen und ohne Schutz vor der Witterung angebunden. Sobald sie keinen Profit mehr einbringen, werden sie im Schlachthaus getötet. Erfahren Sie hier, wie es den Kamelen in Marokko geht und was Sie dagegen tun können. 


PETA Asien deckt erneut auf: Missbrauch von Kamelen in Marokko  


PETA Asien hat 2026 erneut die Misshandlung von Kamelen am Rande der Sahara in Marokko aufgedeckt, wo die Betreiber:innen sie zwingen, Tourist:innen durch die trockenen Wüstendünen zu tragen:  


Die Tiere sind außerhalb ihrer Einsätze häufig angekettet und schutzlos extremer Hitze, intensiver Sonneneinstrahlung und Sandstürmen ausgesetzt. 


Viele Kamele verbringen einen Großteil ihres Lebens isoliert und haben kaum die Möglichkeit, sich frei zu bewegen oder Sozialkontakte zu pflegen.  


Die Kamele werden meist nur dann von ihren Ketten befreit, wenn sie kurz Wasser trinken dürfen oder um weitere Tourist:innen durch die Wüste zu tragen. Ein Kamel wurde dabei beobachtet, wie es nicht nur zum Trinken, sondern auch zu einem Pfosten rannte, um sich dort zu kratzen. Es wurde jedoch zurück zu seinem Anbindeplatz gejagt.  


Tierhalter:innen schlugen Kamele wiederholt mit Peitschen, traten sie und zerrten gewaltsam an ihren Schwänzen. 


Kamele sind intelligente, soziale Wesen mit eigenen Bedürfnissen, Wünschen und Interessen. Wenn sie frei in ihrem natürlichen Lebensraum umherstreifen, leben sie in Herden und kommunizieren miteinander durch Laute und Körperbewegungen. Als Zeichen der Freundschaft blasen sich Kamele manchmal gegenseitig ins Gesicht. In der Tourismusindustrie müssen diese Tiere ein Leben lang Elend und Leid ertragen.


 PETA Asien Recherche aus dem Jahr 2025


Bereits 2025

veröffentlichte

PETA Asien

 Videomaterial, dass die Ausbeutung und Misshandlung von Kamelen in Marokko dokumentiert.

Das beunruhigende Video zeigt Kamele, die an nur wenigen Meter langen Seilen angebunden sind. Ein Betreiber wurde dabei gefilmt, wie er ein gefesseltes Kamel wiederholt mit einem langen Stock schlug, während das Tier versuchte, den Schlägen auszuweichen. Ein weiterer Betreiber erklärte den

Ermittler:innen

, dass Kamele, die bis zu 40 Jahre alt werden können, in der Regel etwa fünf Jahre lang ausgebeutet werden, bevor sie getötet oder als

Fleisch

 verkauft werden.


Globales Muster der Grausamkeit


Frühere PETA-Untersuchungen von Kamel- und Pferdebetrieben in Ägypten offenbarten ähnliche Misshandlungen: Tiere wurden blutig geschlagen, gezwungen, Menschen in brütender Hitze ohne Zugang zu Schatten oder Wasser zu tragen, und wie Müll entsorgt oder ins

Schlachthaus

 geschickt, wenn sie zu alt, krank oder verletzt waren, um noch „nützlich“ zu sein. Airbnb, booking.com, Klook, Marriott und viele andere Unternehmen erklärten sich bereit, die Werbung für Tierfahrten bei den Pyramiden von Gizeh einzustellen, nachdem sie von PETA über das Leid der Tiere informiert worden waren.


So können Sie Tieren in der Tourismusindustrie helfen


Tourist:innen, die für Kamelritte bezahlen, halten diese herzlose, unmenschliche Industrie am Laufen. Wenn Sie einen Urlaub planen, vermeiden Sie Angebote mit Tieren und entscheiden Sie sich für tierfreundliche Alternativen. Unterstützen Sie unsere Petition, um das Leid der Kamele und Pferde bei den ägyptischen Pyramiden zu stoppen.  


		Jetzt unterschreiben!


The post

Neue Aufdeckung: Kamele in Marokko für Tourismus missbraucht

 appeared first on

PETA Deutschland e.V.

.

author: hsa_oryx
title: OCTOBER ROUND UP
content:
First conviction under Hunting with Dogs (Scotland) Act 2023


October kicked off with

Glasgow Hunt Sabs

 reporting that Claire Bellamy, ex-huntswoman and former Master of the Lauderdale Hunt, was found guilty under the Hunting with Dogs (Scotland) Act 2023. Footage which was obtained by sabs shows hounds chasing a fox outside the area covered by a licence that had been granted by NatureScot, and was described by the judge as “

gut wrenching

.” This is the first ever conviction under the new Scottish legislation and you can learn more about the legislation in Scotland and what led to Claire’s conviction

here.


Claire Bellamy found guilty of deliberately hunting a fox with dogs in January 2025.

Image: Glasgow Hunt Sabs


Drone theft


On the 3

rd

 of October Dorset Borders Sabs reported that their drone had been stolen by The Cattistock Hunt as they hunted in Corscombe, Dorchester. The last image visible on the drone was a known member of the hunt running towards it in a field. The incident has been reported to the police and thanks to the generosity of supporters

Dorset Borders Sabs

 raised enough funds to replace the drone.


What do you do when you receive a CPW? If you’re a fox hunt then you break it as soon as possible of course


It didn’t take the Four Burrow Hunt long to break their Community Protection Warning (CPW) which had just been freshly issued by Devon and Cornwall Police. On the 10

th

 of October the hunt was caught breaking condition 7 of the CPW, by failing to give police 24 hours’ notice of their meet. As they had failed to give the details of the meet this means they won’t have provided a map of their “trail” meaning they will have broken more conditions that just number 7. It remains to be seen what action the police will take.

Read our recent article about CPW’s.


Four Burrow Hunt were issued with a CPW after years of trespass and livestock worrying.

Image:


Kernow Sabs, Monitors and Animal Rights Team-Cornwall


Stag hunting horror continues


The horror of stag hunting has continued to escalate in the south west. On the 12

th

 of October the Quantock Staghounds hunted a stag towards the A39 between Nether Stowey and Holford. This is a stretch of road where the hunt are continually causing chaos and putting people’s lives in danger.


This particular incident resulted in a

hunted stag running across the road and colliding with a car.

 A witness described how the terrified stag “

was flipped over the top of the car. Its leg kicked out smashing the rear nearside window. The Stag landed heavily on the verge.”

 Luckily the woman driving and her small child were not hurt but were badly shaken up.


The cruelty doesn’t end there. Two weeks later

North Dorset Hunt Sabs

 reported that the Quantock Staghounds had once again inflicted sickening suffering and pain on a stag. This particular large stag had a visibly infected wound on his side and it is also suspected he had a broken leg. These injuries unfortunately indicate that it is likely the stag that was hit by the car. Despite these injuries the hunt continued to torture him, subjecting him to a chase through thick gorse which no doubt would have caused him unbearable pain.


A stag hunted and terrorised by the Quantock Staghounds.

Credit: North Dorset Hunt Sabs


On the 22

nd

 of October hunt master of the Quantock Staghounds, Christopher Gibbons and huntsman Martin Watts, appeared at Taunton Magistrates Court. Gibbons is facing two counts of hunting a wild mammal under the Hunting Act, and Watts is facing one relating to the barbaric five-hour chase and ultimate

killing of a stag on the 23

rd

 of April 2026

. Both have pleaded not guilty and the case has been adjourned until the 18

th

 of January 2027 for a case management hearing; no trial date has been set. In the meantime, the Quantock Staghounds are continuing to commit abhorrent levels of animal cruelty whilst putting the safety of the general public at great risk.


This stag was tortured for five hours and ultimately killed on the 23

rd

 of April by the Quantock Staghounds.

 Huntsman and hunt master have both pleaded not guilty to charges under the Hunting Act.

Credit:


Mendip Hunt Sabs


They’re blatantly hunting foxes


Amidst the CPW’s, convictions, court hearings, road chaos and trespassing, foxes are still being chased, like the one pictured below.


Beds and Bucks Hunt Sabs

 along with

Peterborough Hunt Sabs

author: L214
title: Enquête abattoir Cooperl
content:
L214 publie une enquête sur l’étourdissement des cochons au CO₂ dans l’un des plus gros abattoirs de France : l’abattoir Cooperl de Montfort-sur-Meu, en Ille-et-Vilaine (Bretagne).

Les images, commentées par l'écrivaine Marie Darrieussecq, montrent la cruauté de cette méthode d'étourdissement dont les instances scientifiques ont établi qu’elle est source de peur, de détresse et de souffrance.

Plus de trente vétérinaires signent un appel publié ce jour pour demander l’interdiction du gazage au CO₂ des cochons. L214 se joint à cette demande et entame un recours contre l’État pour faire interdire cette pratique. L’enseigne de supermarchés Carrefour fait fabriquer par son partenaire Cooperl ses produits à base de viande de porc sous ses marques distributeurs, notamment sa marque Filière Qualité Carrefour. L’association demande à Carrefour de refuser le gazage des cochons et de signer le Plant Protein Pact.

Le musicien Moby apporte son soutien et appelle à signer la pétition.

Chaque heure d’abattage, plus de 800 cochons sont gazés au CO₂ à l’abattoir Cooperl de Montfort-sur-Meu, en Bretagne. Plongés dans une fosse à haute concentration en CO₂, les cochons ont la sensation de se noyer : ils hurlent, paniquent, cherchent désespérément à fuir. Il leur faut entre 21 et 60 secondes pour perdre conscience…

Ce n’est ni instantané, ni sans souffrance. Les instances scientifiques européenne (EFSA) et britannique (AWC) l’affirment depuis 20 ans : cette méthode provoque douleur, peur et détresse respiratoire. Le Royaume-Uni envisage même d’y renoncer, et plus de trente vétérinaires demandent son interdiction.

Pourtant, l’abattoir Cooperl de Montfort-sur-Meu a investi en 2024 environ 5 millions d'euros dans cet équipement qui permet d’abattre un nombre gigantesque d’animaux, de conquérir de nouveaux marchés, d’augmenter les cadences et la productivité. L’enseigne Carrefour fait fabriquer par son partenaire Cooperl des produits à base de cochons gazés sous ses marques, dont la Filière Qualité Carrefour, tout en se disant « pionnier sur le bien-être animal »…

À l’État français : interdire le gazage au CO₂ des cochons ;

À Carrefour : ne plus s’approvisionner en produits issus de cochons gazés et participer à un changement collectif en s'engageant dans le Plant Protein Pact, pour prendre part à une réduction de moitié du nombre d’animaux tués d’ici 2030.

Plus nous serons nombreux et nombreuses, plus il sera difficile pour les responsables de fermer les yeux. Signez et partagez : les cochons ne peuvent pas parler pour eux-mêmes, mais nous, oui.

Contre la souffrance des animaux, agissez à nos côtés avec un don.

title: DEM Party emphasises priority tasks of new period
content:
The DEM Party Council began its second meeting following the congress by commemorating Tuncer Sağlam and Nesrin Aslan.


According to the final statement, the meeting included a comprehensive assessment of political, economic and social developments in Turkey, the Middle East and the world.


The statement said that, guided by the political vision set out at the congress and an awareness of its historical responsibilities, the Council had reached the following conclusions in order to determine the course of struggle for the period ahead:


Solidarity is our fundamental principle


1. The world is going through a period in which people's aspirations for peace, equality, freedom and democracy are confronting governments' policies of war, violence and hegemony. In response to the poverty, unemployment and inequality deepened by the capitalist system, youth, labour and popular movements stretching from France to Serbia and from Latin America to Europe are demonstrating the possibilities of a democratic and egalitarian way of life. Solidarity with struggles against exploitation, oppression, discrimination and lawlessness is our fundamental principle.


In the Middle East, policies of war directed against Iran, conflicts extending from Palestine to Lebanon and from Syria to Yemen, and efforts to establish regional alliances threaten the will and democratic future of the peoples of the region. Rather than becoming part of these policies, Turkey should assume responsibility for regional peace, equality among peoples and democratic solutions. We oppose the government's orientation towards the Mecca Pact, the Badr Agreement and its new relationships with regional powers, as these carry the risk of aligning Turkey with policies of war and hegemony.


The future of a multilingual, multi-faith and multicultural Middle East cannot be built through military alliances and sectarian policies, but through the equality and free will of its peoples. Recognition of the national, cultural and democratic rights of all peoples in the region is indispensable.


Kurda must come together on common ground


2. Overcoming political divisions within the Kurdistan Regional Government and bringing Kurdish political forces together is of historic importance for the unity of the Kurdish people, their shared future and the protection of their achievements. Political differences must not be allowed to weaken the people's collective will. We call on all Kurdish political forces to overcome their divisions through dialogue and come together on common ground for the unity of the Kurdish people.


Political and legal steps must be taken in the second phase of the process


3. The Peace and Democratic Society Process represents a historic opportunity for Turkey's democratic future. For developments aimed at ending conflict and violence as methods of resolving disputes to lead to lasting peace, democratic political channels must be expanded and all sections of society must be able to participate. The process concerns the shared future of society as a whole, not merely the parties involved, and also places responsibility on pro-democracy forces.


Political and legal steps for the second phase must be taken without delay. It is essential to implement the requirements of the legislation adopted by the Grand National Assembly of Turkey (TBMM), establish legal safeguards suited to the needs of the process, and resolve fundamental issues, particularly the right to hope and the status of Mr Abdullah Öcalan.


Ending the appointment of trustees in place of elected local authorities, recognising the will of the people, implementing the rulings of the Constitutional Court (AYM) and the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR), and guaranteeing the life and health rights of sick prisoners are indispensable requirements for democratisation.


Peace is not simply the silencing of weapons; it means confronting the truth, establishing equal citizenship, securing rights and freedoms, ensuring justice and building a democratic society. A democratic and peaceful resolution of the Kurdish question is one of the fundamental conditions for Turkey's transformation into a democratic and social republic. Our party remains determined to maintain its constructive and responsible approach in order to ensure the success of this historic opportunity.

author: Julia Conley
title: Fossil Fuel Giants Have Sued States for Over $443 Billion Under Trade Deals
content:
Critics say the companies are weaponizing provisions to siphon money from public budgets that are already stretched.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Ahead of an official side event at the United Nations Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Türkiye, campaigners on Thursday released an analysis of UN data regarding secretive deals within trade agreements aimed at protecting the profits of corporations, including fossil fuel giants, which have now claimed at least $443 billion from the legal provisions.

Investor-state dispute settlements (ISDS), which allow corporations to sue governments over their investments and profit losses as the result of laws and regulations, have increasingly been used by the fossil fuel industry as countries have started taking action to regulate planet-heating oil and gas emissions, according to data from the UN Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD).

The data was analyzed by the British campaign group Global Justice Now and the German research organization PowerShift, which found that based on 987 publicly disclosed ISDS cases, corporate investors have demanded a total of $1.177 trillion up to 2025.

That represents a 37.5% increase, or $321 billion more, from the amount investors were attempting to claim at the end of 2023.

$1.177 trillion is nearly equivalent to the total global climate finance needs, including mitigation costs, for 2021-22, said the campaigners.

The total compensation demanded by fossil fuel investors, $443.8 billion, “is equivalent to the estimated minimum amount of economic losses developing countries will face due to climate change in 2030,” said Global Justice Now and PowerShift.

In fossil fuel cases, the amount demanded rose by $80 billion, or 22%, compared to 2023.

Fabian Flues, investment policy lead at PowerShift, pointed out that by “weaponizing” ISDS, fossil fuel giants are siphoning “money from public budgets that are already stretched,” and Nick Dearden, director of Global Justice Now, compared the ISDS payouts to “the owners of enslaved people being compensated for their grotesque harms following abolition in the early 19th century.”

“We know fossil fuel corporations are making a fortune out of global crises, hitting ordinary people hard,” said Dearden. “But they are also using obscure international agreements to bully governments out of responding and drain money from the public sector. It’s obscene that the very corporations which have created the climate crisis are demanding eye-watering payouts when governments take much needed climate action.”

This week, US company ExxonMobil launched a legal challenge to the European Union’s Net Zero Industry Act, under which the company is required to pay for carbon storage.

The law would saddle Exxon with “unrealistic timelines,” the company said in a statement.

A UK-based mining company and its Singapore-based majority shareholder also sued the UK government last year for £300 million ($398 million) after officials blocked their “unviable” coal mine planned for Cumbria.

“This legal challenge is a last, desperate attempt by investors to make some money out of a project which belonged in the last century,” Niall Toru, a senior lawyer at Friends of the Earth, told Land and Climate Review in May.

According to Global Justice Now and PowerShift, the total amount of compensation awarded to corporate investors through ISDS cases reached $123 billion last year, with fossil fuel investors receiving “the lion’s share of $85.9 billion, representing almost 70% of all payouts to investors.”

$123 billion is “equivalent to the entire bilateral development aid given by [Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development] countries in 2025,” said the campaigners.

The groups are among those calling on leaders at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) to agree to a coordinated phase-out of ISDS.

Next Monday, Global Justice Now and the Netherlands-based group Both ENDS are organizing an official side event in Antalya featuring Vanuatu Climate Minister Ralph Regenvanu, representatives from communities at the center of ISDS disputes, and a senior government official from Australia, which announced a new policy in 2022 of excluding ISDS mechanisms from future trade deals.

“Governments need to stop this heist and cancel the international agreements that enable fossil fuel investors to sue over …

author: Nina Garcia Steel
title: Crossing Dimensions of Pain Without Losing My Soul
content:
A

s I sit here in my—as I like to call it—Oasis in the Desert, looking out my window at the morning clouds gloriously dancing to the tune the songbirds sing every morning is simply a treasure. I can smile at the sun and sway with the wind as it tickles my senses. I enjoy this morning view as I sip a cup of sweet herbal tea and take in the rays of light.


There was a time when such treasures were absent in my mind. I was living with undeniable pain that I could not explain, except in my poetry.


Photo by Nina Garcia Steel


It’s my heart that aches the most.


The feeling of nerves tearing and bones slowly breaking.


Flares of fire running through my veins.


The words that everyone took as metaphorical were literal words of agony from trauma that started decades earlier. It would take over half a century to discover the root cause of the autoimmune conditions that developed, the near dementia scares. At one point, I was having severe neurological attacks where I lost control of my limbs entirely, making them feel as though they were being tossed around like a rag doll. I picked three alcoholic husbands and stayed in abusive relationships. Little did I know that all of this was coming from the same place:

unprocessed trauma

.


It took me by surprise too. I had been making decisions about who I chose to be my mate based on what I thought was normal from what I experienced as a child. I had suffered sexual abuse more than once, starting when I was only 7 at the hands of a friend’s oldest brother, then an uncle who was visiting, with the worst culprit being my own father. What does a horrific experience like that do to the mind of an innocent child? Nobody was ever prosecuted, my therapy was abruptly stopped, and nothing was done. Left without justice or support, I was left to navigate the aftermath entirely on my own. This meant those early patterns quietly and unknowingly dictated my choices for years.


Decades later, the trauma manifested itself as depression. The connection wasn’t obvious because nobody asked the core question: What happened in your childhood?


So many individuals struggle with trauma that they cannot even name, for we are told, even by medical professionals, that we must focus on our future and that going backward is not in their school of thought. However, trauma is the poisonous seed that grows weeds of unnecessary pain that need to be destroyed at the root.


I walked with pride for so many years, challenging the status quo despite what had happened. I buried it without realizing that everything always comes back if not properly addressed. The pain of betrayal is doubly sharp when there’s unprocessed trauma in the background. It is unfortunate that the questions that could have shaped my treatment were not asked.


I always did things differently, even as early as 6 years old when I was selected to teach a kindergartener English, showing a precocious initiative and drive to bridge gaps long before I understood what systemic obstacles even were. I remember thinking that it was important for my student, Alicia, to learn hopscotch as that would make it easier for her to integrate with the other children. I was an ESL assistant from third to sixth grade. Selling shiny rocks door-to-door for ice-cream money at age 6, writing formal letters in Spanish to my grandfather at age 8. At just 14 years old, I served as the inventory buyer for our family shoe store. I was entrusted to travel on buying trips with an adult and curate the shoes for our inventory.


Learning the mechanics of commerce, spatial merchandising and inventory selection at such a young age taught me how to analyze systems, spot value, and exercise practical strategy long before I ever had to apply those skills to my own survival. At 15, that same drive led me to approach my high school principal with a proposal to redesign the school uniform. I saw how the existing uniforms lacked functionality and aesthetic timelessness, so I designed an updated, structurally timeless uniform that my school adopted. I was already practicing the art of seeing what needed change, organizing a solution, and taking decisive action.


I dared not dwell on the horror of the abuse I had experienced, not realizing that my body would keep score. At that stage, blocking the pain was pure survival. I hadn’t yet allowed my mind to acknowledge the true scope of what had happened — confronting it all at once would have destroyed me, so I compartmentalized …

title: Varto Ekoloji Platformu’ndan, Doğu Anadolu Kalkınma Ajansı’nın toplantı planına tepki
content:
Varto Ekoloji Platformu Varto kültür Merkezinde, Doğu Anadolu Kalkınma Ajansı tarafından düzenlenmesi planlanan etkinliğe tepki gösterdi. Daha önce Muş’ta halktan ve ekoloji örgütlerinden gizlenerek yapılan toplantıda, daha sonra jeotermal güzellemesi yapıldığının ortaya çıkması üzerine, benzer bir etkinliğin de Varto da yapılması tepki çekti. Platform tarafından paylaşılan açıklamada, Varto halkının, toprağını ve suyunu hedef alan, halkın yararına olmayan sömürü projelerine karşı 8 aydan fazladır iradesini direnerek ve mücadele ederek net bir şekilde gösterdiği vurgulandı.

Açıklamada, Varto halkının mücadelesine rağmen düzenlenmesi planlanan toplantıya karşı, “Varto Kültür Merkezi’nde sözde bilim insanı İskender Dölek’in katılımıyla gerçekleştirilmesi planlanan toplantı, halkın aylardır sürdürdüğü bu kararlı direnişi kırma ve doğamızı yıkıma uğratacak projeleri meşrulaştırma çabasıdır. Halka ait kamusal alanların, Varto’nun geleceğini karartmak isteyenlerin propaganda alanı haline getirilmesini kesinlikle kabul etmiyoruz. Bilim; şirketlerin fonlarıyla hareket edenlerin değil, halkın ve doğanın hakikatini savunanların yanındadır” ifadelerine yer verildi.

Açıklamanın devamında, şu ifadelere yer verildi:

“Bu doğrultuda Varto Ekoloji Platformu olarak açık tavrımızdır:

Fonlu ve Şirket Odaklı Anlayışa Soruyoruz:

Sermaye grupları ve maden/enerji şirketleri tarafından fonlanan, talan projelerine zemin hazırlayan bu sözde bilgilendirme toplantılarını hangi çıkarlar karşılığında yürütüyorsunuz?”

STK, kurum ve muhtarlara çağrı yapılan açıklamada, “Varto halkının 8 aydır ilmek ilmek büyüttüğü direniş iradesine sahip çıkın. Şirket fonlarıyla hazırlanan bu meşrulaştırma toplantısına kesinlikle katılmayın, boykot edin” çağrısı yapıldı.

Kamusal mekan vurgusu yapılan açıklamada, “Varto halkının ortak malı olan alanların, halkın onaylamadığı sömürü projelerine tahsis edilmesini reddediyoruz. Varto halkı toprağına, suyuna ve yaşam alanlarına sahip çıkmaya; bu sömürü projelerine karşı mücadelesini kararlılıkla sürdürmeye devam edecektir” denildi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: 500,000 hectares of Mindanao forest lands up for privatization
content:
The Musuan Peak in Bukidnon. Photo by Franck Dick Rosete/Bulatlat

More than 500,000 hectares of public forest lands in Mindanao are up for investment, a recent report from the national government revealed, raising concerns among Indigenous peoples.

Joselin Marcus Fragada, Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) Undersecretary for field operations and line bureaus, said during this year’s Mindanao Development Forum held in Davao City on October 28 that 500,011 hectares of Mindanao forest lands—excluding in the Bangsamoro region—have been delineated for private investments related to agroforestry, industrial timber and wood processing, and pasture management.

Thirty-five percent of the total lands belong to the Caraga region, followed by the Davao region with 28.8 percent—reportedly considered two of the country’s richest areas in terms of natural resources.

Moreover, on top of these lands, the agency also reported that 132,896 hectares of forest lands in Mindanao were qualified for clean energy projects.

Sabokahan Youth, a group of young Lumad, expressed strong opposition to DENR’s plan. Apart from possibilities that it may affect ancestral domains of Indigenous communities and may result in the increase of land disputes, the group stressed that privatizing forest areas may lead to environmental destruction.

“We challenge the DENR to be sincere in serving the people instead of destroying the environment,” the group said in a statement, also decrying the Mindanao Development Authority’s plan of exploring options for Mindanao to supply production inputs, including raw minerals, the United States-led Pax Silica initiative if it becomes operational.

Read: Critical minerals policy framework linked to Pax Silica?

The said DENR program will be governed under the Sustainable Forest Land Management Agreement (SFLMA), a production sharing deal between the agency and a qualified applicant to undertake sustainable forest management under a renewable 25-year contract.

DENR Administrative Order No. 2025-22, or the rules and regulations governing SFLMA, shall cover forest lands outside protected areas that are suitable and available for development and utilization.

One of the requirements to be obtained by an applicant is a certificate of non-overlap (CNO), a certification issued by the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples (NCIP) attesting that a subject area does not overlap with any ancestral domain.

Fragada said the national government needs the private sector for the state to provide better programs in the country’s timberland and forest land areas.

Kalikasan People’s Network for the Environment, in an earlier statement, denounced the SFLMA policy, describing it as a blatant handover of the nation’s forests to profit-driven corporations.

“[It] only deepens the threat to Indigenous and rural poor communities, especially in Mindanao, where intensified Lumad killings are already linked to resource plunder and militarized land grabs,” it added.

Special Archives: Lumad Killings

For the environmental group, such a policy, without a genuine national industrialization that could process the country’s resources for the benefit of the Filipinos, only deepens exploitation and the nation’s dependence on foreign markets. (RVO)

author: groundxero
title: 544 Scientists and Researchers Stand with Siang Valley Anti-Dam Movement; Demand Halt to Mega Project and Release of Detained Activists
content:
“We stand with the people of the Siang Valley in their struggle to protect their river, their lands, their rights and the ability to determine their future. We recognise that the people who call this valley home must have the primary say in determining its future.”


 


Groundxero

 Desk


 


In a strong show of solidarity with the indigenous Adi communities resisting the proposed 11,000 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh, a group of 544 scientists, researchers, and concerned citizens working in the fields of nature, wildlife, society and the environment has called on the Union and state governments to immediately halt all pre-feasibility activities, withdraw additional security forces from the valley and release anti-dam protesters detained and arrested under the stringent Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA).


 


The statement, issued on November 9, 2026, comes amid growing resistance in the Siang Valley to the proposed mega-dam and reports of intensified security deployment, restrictions on people’s movement, arrests and the use of force against protesters.


 


The signatories, many of whom have worked in Arunachal Pradesh and the Eastern Himalayas, describe the Siang Valley as an ecologically irreplaceable landscape of immense biodiversity, cultural significance and traditional knowledge. Referring to an earlier statement by 114 scientists issued on June 9, 2025, they point out that 48 new species and 140 new distribution records have been documented in the valley in the past 15 years alone.


 


The statement warns that large-scale construction in an ecologically fragile and highly seismically active river system could have irreversible consequences. It emphasises that the Siang River, its forests and surrounding mountains sustain not only rich biodiversity but also the livelihoods, cultural identity and traditional knowledge systems of indigenous Adi communities.


 


The scientists express particular concern over the Arunachal Pradesh government’s continued efforts to push ahead with the project’s Pre-Feasibility Report (PFR) despite sustained opposition from affected communities. They condemned the militarisation of this otherwise peaceful region, restrictions on movement, arrests and detentions of local anti-dam activists, and the use of tear gas and force against protesters. They also denounce the alleged harassment and intimidation of lawyers, journalists and others standing in solidarity of the movement.


 


Invoking the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP), the signatories assert that the project must not proceed without the free, prior and informed consent of the affected indigenous communities, whose lands, livelihoods, cultural heritage and relationship with the Siang are at stake. They also stressed on the constitutional guarantees of freedom of speech, expression and peaceful assembly.


 


The statement calls on the Arunachal Pradesh and Union governments to stop all PFR-related activities, withdraw additional armed forces from the region, release those detained for participating in the movement, and initiate an open and meaningful dialogue with the affected communities.


 


The signatories affirm that the people who have protected and sustained the Siang Valley for generations must have the primary say in determining its future.


 


The full statement along with the list of signatories is published below:


 


November 9, 2026


 


We, a group of scientists, researchers, conservation practitioners and concerned citizens, many of whom have worked in Arunachal Pradesh and in the Eastern Himalaya, stand in unequivocal solidarity with the people of the Siang Valley in their opposition to the proposed 11,000 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP).


 


The Siang Valley is not merely a site for a proposed mega-infrastructure project. The Siang River, its forests and the surrounding mountains sustain extraordinary biodiversity, livelihoods, traditional knowledge systems and the cultural identity of indigenous Adi communities.


 


A statement issued by a collective of 114 scientists on 9th of June 2025, noted that the Siang is a rich living landscape of immense ecological, cultural and biological significance. In the past 15 years alone, there have been 48 new species described, as well as 140 new distribution records from the valley.

author: Nelly Madegwa
title: Pregnancy in a Warming Africa
content:
At 8:30 a.m., Stella is usually already at the Kakamega Forest dispensary in Kakamega County, western Kenya, for her antenatal care (ANC) appointment. Seven months pregnant, she has learnt to organise her household around the rising heat, doing most of her chores when temperatures are lower.


The clinic is 2.5 kilometres away, a distance she walks. Arriving early allows her to complete her check-ups and begin the journey home before the sun becomes unbearable.


Her routine reflects a change that Doreen Atamba, a community health promoter who has supported expectant mothers for the past ten years, has observed among women attending the facility. Increasingly, expectant mothers arrive between 8 a.m. and 10 a.m., with fewer coming after 10 a.m. By late morning, attendance drops considerably.


Atamba says the heat is affecting not only when women seek antenatal care but also their comfort and well-being at home. Some expectant mothers complain that intense temperatures make everyday activities difficult and disrupt their sleep.


“Some of them tell me they are really struggling with the heat, even at night when they are trying to sleep,” she says.


To help them cope, Atamba encourages pregnant women to wear loose-fitting clothing, drink plenty of water, avoid unnecessary exposure to extreme heat, rest frequently and seek relief in cooler places, especially shaded areas.


These everyday adjustments are taking place amid rising temperatures and growing concern about the effects of climate change on maternal and newborn health.


Across Africa, experts in Kenya, South Africa, Senegal and Nigeria are increasingly concerned about how climate-related extremes are affecting pregnant women and newborns. Extreme heat can cause dehydration and physical strain, while drought, flooding, food insecurity and disrupted healthcare services can compound the risks. Experts say the consequences depend not only on the weather but also on women’s living and working conditions, access to water and nutrition, and the ability of health facilities to provide safe care.


Heat and pregnancy


Pregnancy places additional demands on the body. During extreme heat, dehydration and the effort required to regulate body temperature can put additional strain on the heart and circulatory system. Researchers are still investigating how this stress may affect the placenta and developing baby.


Ijeoma Solarin, a senior researcher at Wits Planetary Health Research, and Kimberly McAlpine, a medical student and PhD researcher at Wits University, point to growing evidence associating high temperatures with preterm birth, stillbirth, low birth weight and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.


A 2025

study

 by Carrie Ngongo and colleagues, analysing 22.7 million births in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, found that each 1°C increase in temperature above 34°C was associated with an additional 2.3 stillbirths per 1,000 births and 27.3 maternal deaths per 100,000 live births.


A separate

study

 at a Johannesburg hospital linked high temperatures early in pregnancy to approximately 1.8 times the risk of severe hypertensive disorders, including pre-eclampsia and eclampsia.


Research

 involving pregnant subsistence farmers in The Gambia has also documented signs of fetal distress during hot weather, including unusual changes in the baby’s heart rate and increased resistance to blood flow through the umbilical cord, which supplies oxygen and nutrients from the placenta.


The scale of concern extends beyond individual studies. A

Wellcome-commissioned poll

 of 1,001 healthcare professionals in Australia, Brazil, India, the United Kingdom and Zimbabwe found that 98 per cent had cared for a pregnant woman whose health they believed had been adversely affected by extreme heat. Meanwhile, 99 per cent reported caring for a baby whose health they believed had been adversely affected by extreme heat.


These findings reflect healthcare professionals’ reported experiences and perceptions, rather than estimates of the proportion of pregnant women or babies experiencing medically confirmed heat-related harm. Nevertheless, they highlight concerns among health workers about the effects of extreme heat on mothers and babies.

author: Anne Marxze Umil
title: IMF, WB cause misery for marginalized communities
content:
The Counterdocket exposed the harms caused by the IMF-WB.


BANGKOK – For 80 years, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank (WB) brought suffering to many communities in the Global South.


On October 15, their stories were heard at the Counterdocket in Bangkok, Thailand where the two Breton Woods institutions also held their annual meeting from October 12 to 18.  


Dubbed as Our Voices Count! A Counterdocket, it brought together movements to challenge extractive systems and demand greater accountability from the IMF-WB. The Counterdocket exposed the harms caused by the IMF-WB. From the Support to Parcelization of Lands for Individual Titling (SPLIT) project of the WB Group in the Philippines to Lithium mining in Argentina, these testimonies became public records of the IMF-WB’s effects on communities. 


“This counterdocket is an act of historical and political reassertion,” said Joms Salvador, regional coordinator of the Asia Pacific Forum on Women Law and Development (APWLD) during the opening on October 15. “The communities sitting in this room are not beneficiaries of course waiting for charity, nor are they subjects to be studied. You are the plaintiffs. You are the witnesses. And you are the judges of a system that has failed humanly. And through the voices of community leaders, feminist economists, legal scholars, and human rights defenders across all these sessions throughout the day, we are building an irrefutable record of systemic accountability.” 


“Its jurisdiction is not grounded in formal legal authority, but in the right of communities to document, testify, question and demand accountability for decisions that shape their lives,” said Zeph Repollo, Southeast Asia regional director at Just Associates (JASS), a feminist movement-building organization. 


(Photo courtesy of Asia Pacific Forum on Women Law and Development)


She added, “It is an expression of communities’ self determination and their right to be heard, particularly in a context where existing accountability mechanisms have proven largely ineffective in addressing the consequences of IFI (international financing institutions) actions for economic, social, cultural, and environmental rights.” 


The Counterdocket focused on five connected themes examining how economic policies, development projects, and global power structures affected the communities in the Global South. The testimonies presented covered a range of projects and issues spanned across South Asia, South East Asia, Africa and Latin America. 


Some of the cases heard at the Counterdocket included the Sentani Airport and Transformation of Buyaka Ancestral Land case in West Papua 


IMF-WB effects on Filipinos lives 


At the Counterdocket, Ana Marie Mijares, 54, a farmer from Kabankalan, Negros Occidental narrated the militarization they experienced in the government’s implementation of SPLIT, a project of the Department of Agrarian Reform and the World Bank Group. 


According to the project proponent, the main objective of SPLIT is to improve the land tenure or the rights of the farmers to the land they cultivate and to provide individual titles to farmers under collective certificate of land ownership award (CLOA). 


Their community is composed mainly of farmer-beneficiaries and former sugar farmworkers organized through Kauswagan sang Bino para sa Buhi kag Hilway nga Palangabuhian (Kabuhi-an)  and Kauswagan sang Mamumugon, Mangunguma sa Bino (KASMMABI) in Barangay Orong, Kabankalan City, Negros Occidental.


The community manages around 198 hectares of land awarded through the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program in 1998 under a collective Certificate of Land Ownership Award (CLOA). The original beneficiaries were former hacienda sugarcane workers, with additional Agrarian Reform Beneficiaries (ARBs) later included through a petition for the inclusion of qualified ARBs in the landholding. The community now involves around 168 farming families.


Ana Marie Mijares (middle) with other delegates at the Counterdocket. (Photo courtesy of Asia Pacific Forum on Women Law and Development)


After years of struggle for land, the farmers developed their own way of managing the property. Each family cultivates an individual portion of around 1.5 hectares, while at least 15 hectares are maintained as common or collective land for collective production.

author: Slingshot robot #1
title: 5 – Call to ceremony: Red Butte and the protection of sacred lands
content:
By two comrades based in Oakland, CA

“Wii’i Gdwiisa [we-e gud-we-suh], known in english as Red Butte, is a sacred mountain just south of the Grand Canyon. It is the birthplace of the Havasupai people. In 1974, uranium was discovered on the Havasupai reservation. Despite the tribe’s attempts to prevent mining on their sacred lands, the u.s. government approved mining permits and the land was stolen (again). There is a long history of violence in the so-called american southwest committed against indigenous people and land by the nuclear industry. This is a story of that legacy and the uranium mine currently operating at the northern base of Red Butte. This is also a story of the steadfast resistance by the people born from these lands and those who fight alongside them. Wii’i Gdwiisa is still alive, still breathing. Her people ask us to live and fight in solidarity with her and all sacred land/water under attack by the settler colonial capitalist regime.”

On the weekend of May 14th–18th 2026, networks of land defenders called a gathering to defend Red Butte against uranium mining. We gathered some comrades to make the journey and as we left Oakland, we didn’t realize how transformative the trip would be. On the journey back home, we decided to pull over to pray and honor the sunrise the way we had been taught at the gathering, and we knew our lives and organizing would be forever changed by Red Butte.

When we arrived at Wii’i Gdwiisa after two days of travel, comrades were setting up camp at the southern base of the mountain. Our Indigenous comrades invited us to greet the land, give an offering, share our lineages and intentions, and ask permission to camp. We listened to the wind and rocks for answers and proceeded only once the land responded. Ceremony was at the center of this gathering, grounding us in an ongoing conversation with the land itself as we planned our actions in defense of Red Butte.

The gathering was autonomously organized and guided by Indigenous organizers with established protocols. People were invited to take whatever action they were called to, rather than relying on direction from specific leaders. The autonomous strategy was apparent in moments of confusion and disorganization, but allowed us to nimbly shift programming in response to emergent situations like radioactively contaminated desert winds and police repression. It also created opportunities for everyone to contribute what they could and grow into roles that needed doing, like bathroom duty, shelter construction, political education, vibes, radioactive decontamination, or cooking in a fully-functional desert kitchen serving three hot meals to 150 people every day.

Two sacred fires, one for Wii’i Gdwiisa and one for Dookó’oslííd (known in english as the San Francisco Peaks), were the heartbeat of the camp. We burned medicine and other offerings in their flames which burned uninterrupted throughout the gathering, we shared stories and meals around their circle, and we sang and danced in their warmth at night. We were taught to gather and cut wood with clear minds and good intentions. Fire-tenders stayed up every night to ensure the fires didn’t go out. As we kept watch over the fire, we also kept watch over the safety of the camp. Other practices, like the daily sunrise ceremonies and a ceremonial sheep slaughter led by Diné comrades, similarly intertwined spiritual consciousness and soulful embodied connection to Red Butte with the meeting of basic needs like sleeping and eating. The rituals were hard work, which taught us to be good guests and showed the necessity of strong spiritual practice in sustaining a lifelong militant commitment to fighting for land.

We were invited to Red Butte by Havasupai elders, who cannot themselves return to the birthplace of their tribe because the radioactive contamination is too big of a threat to the tribe’s survival. They wanted us to learn about uranium mining and make a public show of support for the tribe’s fight. After taking the first day to set up, the following two days were full of teach-ins, workshops, discussions, and planning for the elders’ call to action. We thank those who shared their knowledge with us, including groups like Haul No! and Stop T.H.E.M., as well as indigenous experts of the local land and academic experts of history and hydrology.
