author: groundxero
title: দুনিয়া কাঁপানো শরৎকাল
content:
এরকম এক শরৎকাল প্রত্যক্ষ করার পর এক রকমের আশা জাগে – বসন্ত আসতে হয়তো বেশি দেরী হবে না।


 


দেবারতি


গুপ্ত

  


 


এ এক অন্য শরৎকাল এসে হাজির হয়েছে দুনিয়া জুড়ে। লেট ক্যাপিটালিজমের নখ দাঁত যেভাবে প্রকট হয়ে উঠেছে গত দুই দশকে তাতে সাধারণ মানুষের নাভিশ্বাস উঠতে শুরু করেছে। মিলেনিয়াল প্রজন্ম এই পরিস্থিতি একভাবে মোকাবিলা করেছে। তাদের যৌবনে তবু কিছু চাকরি ছিল মন ভোলানোর উপাদান ছিল। কোভিড পরবর্তী কালে যে প্রজন্ম যৌবনে পা দিয়েছে তারা পেয়েছে এক অবাক পৃথিবী। একদিকে সমাজ মাধ্যমের বিভ্রান্তিকর দুনিয়া আরেকদিকে নতুন হাজির হওয়া কৃত্রিম বুদ্ধিমত্তা। এইসবের মধ্যে দুনিয়াজোরা সরকারি শিক্ষা ব্যবস্থা, স্বাস্থ্য পরিষেবা আর কর্মসংস্থানের চূড়ান্ত বেহাল অবস্থা।


 


বছর দুই আগে থেকেই সার্বিয়ার ছাত্ররা বিক্ষোভ শুরু করেছিল। নোভি সাদ রেইল স্টেশনের ছাত ভেঙে ১৬ জনের মৃত্যু হওয়ায় ছাত্রদের বিরোধিতা শুরু হয়। ওই কান্ড নিছক দুর্ঘটনা বলে চাপা দেবার চক্রান্ত সহজে মেনে নেয় নি সার্বিয়ার ছাত্ররা। তারা আন্দোলন শুরু করে। সেই আন্দোলন দীর্ঘ ১৪ বছর ধরে ক্ষমতায় থাকা আলেক্সান্ডার ভুচিচকে সম্প্রতি গদিচ্যুত করেছে।


 


২৬ অক্টোবর, অর্থাৎ সার্বিয়ার ওই ঐতিহাসিক দিনে বেলগ্রেড থেকে এক সফটওয়্যার ইঞ্জিনিয়ার লাজার পেত্রোভিচ ‘কফি হাউস এক্সপেরিয়েন্স’ এর লাইভ পডকাস্টে এসেছিলেন। এই মুহূর্তে কলকাতা শহরে যেখানে প্রতিদিন ফ্যাসিজমের উপস্থিতি হাড়ে হাড়ে টের পাচ্ছি সেইখানে বসে সার্বিয়ার পার্লামেন্টের সামনে দাঁড়িয়ে উচ্ছ্বসিত লাজারকে দেখতে পাওয়া, নিঃসন্দেহে খুব আশাব্যঞ্জক ঘটনা। মজার কথা হল দক্ষিণপন্থী ভুচিচের এস এন এস (সার্বিয়ান প্রগ্রেসিভ পার্টি) দলের বিরোধী যে রাজনৈতিক দলগুলো – গ্রিন লেফট পার্টি বা ডেমক্রেটিক পার্টি এরাও ছাত্রদের দলের কাছে পাত্তা পায় নি। ক্ষমতাসীন বা তথাকথিত বিরোধী দুই পক্ষের প্রতিই গভীর অনাস্থা থেকে Student List বা Students Are Winning দলটি তৈরি হয়েছিল। লাজারকে জিগ্যেস করেছিলাম যে ছাত্র আর সার্বিয়ার সুশীল সমাজের যে প্রতিনিধিদের নিয়ে ওরা ক্ষমতায় এল তাদের রাজনৈতিক আদর্শ কি? লাজার জানালো ওদের গত দু বছরের লড়াই কোন নির্দিষ্ট রাজনৈতিক আদর্শের ভিত্তিতে গড়ে ওঠে নি। তাদের দেশের সংকট যেখানে পৌঁছেছিল তাতে শিক্ষা, স্বাস্থ্য আর নিরাপত্তার মতো মৌলিক অধিকার নিয়ে তাদের লড়াই করতে হয়েছে। লাজারের দেশের শাসনব্যবস্থা তথা রাজনীতি কোনদিকে এগোয় তা বোঝার জন্য আমরা নিশ্চই অধীর আগ্রহে তাকিয়ে থাকবো সার্বিয়ার দিকে।


 


এবার মুখ ফেরানো যাক বিপ্লবের পীঠস্থান ফ্রান্সের দিকে। সেখানেও ছাত্রদের নেতৃত্বে বিরোধিতা শুরু হয়েছে।


 


প্রায় দু’মাস হতে চলল ফ্রান্সে ছাত্র আন্দোলন চলছে। প্রাথমিক ভাবে যেটা শুরু হয়েছিল প্যারিসের এক শহরতলি এলাকার উচ্চ বিদ্যালয় বা Lycée-র ছাত্র-ছাত্রীদের মাধ্যমে, তা পরে আরও ব্যাপক ভূমিকা গ্রহণ করেছিল। শিক্ষক-শিক্ষিকারা, অধ্যাপক-অধ্যাপিকারা, স্কুল ছাড়াও কলেজ-বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের ছাত্র-ছাত্রীরা, তাদের অভিভাবকেরাও মিছিলে নিয়মিত সক্রিয় অংশ নিচ্ছিলেন। হাই স্কুল ছাত্র-ছাত্রীদের মূল দাবী ছিল সরকারি স্কুল গুলোর পরিকাঠামোর উন্নতি,  কারণ সরকারি স্কুলগুলোয় যথেষ্ট শিক্ষক নেই, ফলে একেকটা ক্লাসে একজন শিক্ষকের দায়িত্বে অনেক বেশি ছাত্র। স্কুল বিল্ডিং এর অবস্থা ক্রমশ খারাপ হয়ে পড়ছে। অতিরিক্ত গরমে বা অতিরিক্ত ঠান্ডায় সেই সব ঘরে ক্লাস করা খুব মুশকিল হয়ে পড়ছে। গত বাজেট সেশনে শিক্ষা ক্ষেত্রে বাজেট অনেক কমানো হয়েছে। ফলে এই সবকিছু নিয়েই ছাত্ররা বিক্ষুব্ধ। সম্প্রতি সরকার এদের কিছু কিছু দাবি মেনে নিয়েছে কিন্তু তবুও আন্দোলন থামেনি। কারণ ছাত্ররা বলছে এটা যথেষ্ট নয়। যা সমস্যা রয়েছে আরও গভীরে গিয়ে তার সমাধান করতে হবে। ফলে স্কুল কলেজ ব্লক করা অব্যাহত রয়েছেl এই ব্লক করার একটা নাম তারা দিয়েছে – ব্লকাস (Blocus)


 


কথা হচ্ছিল ফ্রান্সে বসবাসকারী অধ্যাপক সোমঋতা ভট্টাচার্যর সঙ্গে। সোমঋতা কঁ-নর্ম্যান্ডি ইউনিভার্সিটিতে (Université de Caen-Normandie) ইংরিজি পড়ান। অকে জিগ্যেস করেছিলাম, ম‍্যাক্রোঁর সেন্ট্রিস্ট সরকারের বিরুদ্ধে যদি আন্দোলন জারি থাকে তাহলে কি তা লা পেনের দক্ষিণপন্থী দলকে জোরদার করবে? না কি বামপন্থী জাঁ লুক মেলেশঁদলেরও সম্ভাবনা তৈরি করতে পারে?


 


সোমঋতা আন্দোলনের বিস্তারের কথা জানালো। প্রতিবাদী ছাত্র-ছাত্রীদের সঙ্গে শ্রমিকশ্রেণী যাঁরা ইয়েলো ভেস্ট (gillet jaune) মুভমেন্টে অংশ নিয়েছিলেন, অবসর প্রাপ্ত মানুষ যাঁরা কিছু দিন আগে অবস্র গ্রহণের বয়স বৃদ্ধির বিরুদ্ধে প্রতিবাদে অংশ নিয়েছিলেন, তাঁরা সকলে একে একে জড়ো হচ্ছেন। কারণ দ্রব্যমূল্য বৃদ্ধি, মানুষের ক্রয়ক্ষমতা কমে যাওয়ার সঙ্কট একটা ভয়াবহ আকার নিয়েছে। তবে আশার কথা এই যে, ছাত্র আন্দোলনে কিন্তু মেলেশঁর সমর্থক বেশি দেখা যাচ্ছে। নিয়মিত ছাত্রদের পাশে থেকেছেন মেলেশঁ, তাদের প্রতিবাদে অংশ নিয়েছেন। অন্যদিকে ছাত্রেরা স্পষ্ট ভাবে মারিন লো পেন এবং তাঁর অতি-দক্ষিণপন্থী দলের সমালোচনা করছে এবং প্রতিবাদী ছাত্ররা তাদের বিরোধী মিছিলে এমন কিছু পোস্টার নিয়েও এসেছে যেখানে পরিষ্কার লেখা রয়েছে, দক্ষিণপন্থী দলদের তারা কোনও ভাবেই সমর্থন করছে না এবং অতি-দক্ষিণপন্থীদের বিভেদ, বৈষম্যমূলক কার্যকলাপের সম্পূর্ণ বিরোধিতা করছে এবং ভবিষ্যতেও করে যাবে। অর্থাৎ সার্বিয়ার মতো ছাত্র বিক্ষোভ থেকে বিদ্রোহ ছড়িয়ে পড়েছে নানান ক্ষেত্রে। তবে ফ্রান্সে রাজনৈতিক আদর্শ …

author: Unknown
title: Difendersi, organizzarsi, avere fiducia nella classe – Intervista a Raul Zibechi
content:
Pubblichiamo la sbobinatura, leggermente editata per chiarezza e fluidità del testo, di un’intervista con Raul Zibechi realizzata da alcuni compagni di

Radio Blackout

, trasmessa durante il programma informativo e ripubblicata sul sito della radio come

podcast dal titolo

 «Guerra, estrattivismo e prospettive per i movimenti sociali in Latino-America: una conversazione con Raul Zibechi»

.


Raúl Zibechi è un giornalista, scrittore e militante uruguaiano. Si è formato politicamente nella sinistra rivoluzionaria uruguaiana degli anni Sessanta e Settanta. Durante la dittatura ha conosciuto l’esilio, in Argentina e poi in Spagna. Rientrato in Uruguay, scrive da decenni per il settimanale Brecha e per La Jornada. È tra le voci più lucide del pensiero autonomo latinoamericano. Il suo lavoro ruota intorno ai processi di autonomia popolare, ai movimenti sociali, alla lunga esperienza zapatista e alle lotte indigene e contadine.


Nel continente latino-americano assistiamo da anni ad una progressiva emersione di governi di estrema destra, che da alcuni anni sembra abbiano sancito la fine del “ciclo progressista” che aveva caratterizzato il decennio precedente. Partendo da questa constatazione, vorremmo chiederti qual è oggi la situazione politica e sociale in America Latina. Come interpretare, da una prospettiva latinoamericana, la fine del ciclo progressista e l’inizio di un ciclo fascista e neoliberale? Quali classi sociali ed interessi si scontrano?


RZ

: Grazie mille per le domande. Dunque: oggi l’America Latina attraversa una deriva autoritaria, un percorso che definirei come una scomposizione della società. Su questo credo valga la pena fare un parallelo con l’Europa, e con la Francia in particolare. Della Francia possiamo dire che da anni stia attraversando un processo di “putrefazione” della società: in America Latina, io direi che siamo dentro un processo di scomposizione, di disarticolazione sociale.


Questa scomposizione si manifesta come uno scontro permanente tra diversi settori sociali. Da una parte ci sono le classi superiori, quell’1% che controlla lo Stato, il capitale finanziario e le banche, ed anche le classi medio-alte. Dall’altra ci sono i settori e le classi popolari, che le classi medio-alte individuano come loro nemico: i poveri urbani, i contadini, gli indigeni, i neri. Non dimentichiamo che in America Latina indigeni, neri e meticci rappresentano il 30-40% della popolazione. Contro questi settori si sta combattendo una guerra non dichiarata, non ufficiale, ma con moltissimi morti, come vediamo in Messico e in Brasile. Detto questo, non si tratta di uno scontro tra due “modelli” di società, perché bisogna ammettere che l’unica forza in campo ad avere un reale progetto sociale è la destra autoritaria e neoliberale. È un progetto sociale pensato per il solo 30% della popolazione, in cui il restante 70% è considerato “scartabile”, eliminabile. Un progetto di controllo autoritario che, per dirla con Giorgio Agamben, vuole trasformare l’immensa maggioranza della popolazione negli inquilini perenni di un enorme campo di concentramento, cioè le favelas, le periferie urbane, le comunità nere e quelle indigene, da cui non possano uscire e dentro cui vengano periodicamente attaccati. Il progetto sociale delle classi dominanti è questo: estrattivismo e controllo militare sulla popolazione “in eccesso”, ed infatti è la militarizzazione il cuore della proposta della destra.


Il progressismo, invece, oggi non ha un progetto sociale che sia davvero alternativo. Cerca di limitare i danni provocati dal modello neoliberale, ma non ha né la volontà né la capacità di uscirne. Per questo dico che non si scontrano due modelli, ma al massimo due idee diverse su come gestire la società. Certo, il Brasile di Lula sarà meno autoritario di quello di Bolsonaro, ma il controllo reale rimane nelle mani delle classi alte, e né l’autoritarismo né il militarismo scompaiono. Qua bisognerebbe fare un ragionamento su quello che in America Latina sono il governo ed il potere, che sono due cose diverse. Ma ci torneremo più tardi. Comunque, il punto importante è che oltre l’America Latina, in tutto il mondo le sinistre non riescono a esprimere un progetto politico capace di contrapporsi davvero alle destre. Questo è un problema molto, molto serio.


Che ruolo ha avuto in questi anni l’estrattivismo? Dal nostro punto di vista è uno dei fattori che più hanno messo in crisi il modello progressista. Il progressismo non è riuscito a …

author: Kerry Smith
title: Socialist Alliance: Funding cuts to Villamanta throw people with disability on scrap heap
content:
Brenden Grull, Socialist Alliance spokesperson and candidate for Geelong, has called for funding cuts to Villamanta, Geelong’s Disability Rights Legal Service, to be reversed.

The community-based service, which is housed in Geelong West but works across Victoria, fights for the rights of people with disability-related justice issues. It has been operating since 1990.

The Department of Health and Ageing said on November 10 that it would be cutting approximately 30% of Villamanta’s total funding and around 50% of its core funding.

“It is almost unbelievable that as the demand for disability advocacy increases and in defiance of the Disability Royal Commission’s recommendations to recognise independent advocacy as a vital safeguard for people with disability that Villamanta’s funds are being cut so significantly,” Grull told Green Left.

“I understand that the decision will have an immediate impact; it will lead to substantial job losses. I presume that this is part of the federal government’s cuts to NDIS services.

“It is particularly shocking when independent reviews have recognised that Villamanta is a leader in best-practice disability advocacy and community legal support.”

Grull said the cuts will “only cause more pain and suffering for clients and workers”. He said as cost of living pressures rise for everyone, these cuts show federal Labor’s “diminishing commitment” to community-based organisations.

“Labor’s preference is for dodgy providers from the private sector.”

Grull said Socialist Alliance backs Villamanta’s campaign to get the funding cuts reversed and to protect access to independent disability advocacy.

“We support the reintroduction of publicly-funded disability services to fix gaps in the National Disability Insurance Scheme. Villamanta has our 100% support and we will be doing everything in our power to help restore its funding.”

author: Chiara Joos
title: Das Recht auf sexuelle Selbstbestimmung
content:
Zwangssterilisation ist verboten. Dennoch erfahren Frauen mit Behinderungen häufig Druck von Angehörigen, Ärzt*innen oder Betreuer*innen, sich sterilisieren zu lassen.

Weißt du, wie viele Menschen ich begleitet habe, die darunter gelitten haben, dass sie sterilisiert wurden?“, fragte mich eine Beraterin am Telefon. Sie schult Menschen mit Behinderungen in Selbstbestimmung. Es war eines von hundert Gesprächen, die meine Kollegin Ramona Arzberger und ich geführt haben, um zur Verhütungspraxis bei Menschen mit Behinderungen zu recherchieren. Nach fast einem Jahr ist daraus der Film „Hauptsache, du kriegst kein Kind“ unseres Magazins „andererseits“ entstanden. Er begleitet mehrere Frauen in Deutschland und Österreich, die mit Lernschwierigkeiten leben und auf Unterstützung angewiesen sind. Drei von ihnen sind sterilisiert. Keine entschied allein. Elf Prozent der Frauen in deutschen Einrichtungen geben an, sterilisiert zu sein, so der Forschungsbericht zu Gewalt und Gewaltschutz in Einrichtungen der Behindertenhilfe des deutschen Bundesministeriums für Arbeit und Soziales von 2024. In Österreich waren es zuletzt 17 Prozent. In Deutschland habe fast die Hälfte der Betroffenen den Eingriff nicht von sich aus gewollt, heißt es in dem Bericht. In Österreich taucht in Befragungen dasselbe auf: Eltern, Ärzt*innen und Betreuer*innen hätten auf die Frauen eingewirkt. „Ich will auch mitmachen!“, platzte die Stimme von Hannelore Trtil ins Telefon, noch ehe meine Kollegin erfuhr, wer da sprach. Die 66-Jährige hatte unseren Flyer gesehen, der Betroffene erreichen sollte. In den 1980er-Jahren wurde sie in Wien „unterbunden“, ein anderes Wort für sterilisiert. „Die haben alle gesagt, man darf keine Kinder kriegen. Das habe ich nicht richtig gefunden. Und das habe ich nicht gewollt“, sagt sie im Film. Heute verbringt sie oft Zeit mit Kindern. Ihre OP-Akte hat das Krankenhaus vor etwa zehn Jahren vernichtet, nach Ablauf der Frist für Schadenersatz. Sie wird nie erfahren, welche Art von Sterilisation bei ihr gemacht wurde. Hannelore sagt auch, sie habe nie Sex gehabt, aus dem ein Kind hätte entstehen können. Diesen Satz haben wir in unseren Recherchen nicht nur von ihr gehört. Thea, die in Wirklichkeit anders heißt, wurde 2025 sterilisiert, in einem Alter, in dem manche noch nicht an Kinder denken. author: daniel
title: Ableistisches journalistisches Versagen
content: Dieser wurde aber weitgehend totgeschwiegen. Es gab kaum Presseberichte. Selbst über die Besetzung eines Bundesministeriums berichtete einzig die Frankfurter Rundschau. Journalist*innen schreiben lieber über Einzelschicksale. Mitleid-erweckende Berichte generieren online Klicks und gefallen Leser*innen. Die Berichte bleiben oberflächlich und die systemischen und politischen Hintergründe werden nicht beleuchtet. Betroffene als Objekte einer bequemen Berichtserstattung. Sobald Betroffene als Akteur*innen auftreten und das System, das sie behindert, anprangern, werden sie unsichtbar gemacht. Die Redaktionen stehen offenbar zu dieser ableistischen Linie. Der Lüneburger Behindertenbeirat kritisierte die Nicht-Berichtserstattung der Landeszeitung (LZ) über eine Kundgebung am europäischen Protesttag für die Gleichstellung von Menschen mit Behinderung. Die Redaktion antwortete am 22. Mai 2026 wie folgt: „Anm. d. Red.: Am Protesttag selbst hat die LZ tatsächlich nicht berichtet. Wir stellen hingegen regelmäßig Schicksale von Menschen mit Einschränkungen in den Mittelpunkt von Geschichten – unabhängig von Protest- oder Gedenktagen. So haben wir beispielsweise am 9. Mai von der 16-jährigen Lotti berichtet, die trotz Unterstützungsbedarf ihren Traumberuf lernen will.“ Selbst die verwendete Sprache ist hier ableistisch. Das Wort „Behinderung“ wird gemieden, obwohl dies kein Schimpfwort ist, sondern eine neutrale Eigenschaft. Das ist ein journalistisches Versagen. Die Graswurzelrevolution wird dagegen über die Proteste und ihre Hintergründe ausführlich in der GWR 514 berichten. Seid auf den Schwerpunkt der Dezemberausgabe gespannt!

author: Sarah Hughes
title: Members Alarmed by End-Run around Democracy at Buffalo Health Care Local
content:
Things had been tense for some time inside the leadership of Communications Workers (CWA) Local 1168, a 4,800-member health care union based near Buffalo, New York. Still, it was a high-functioning local with a busy calendar of events, stewards handling grievances, organizers pursuing leads, and leaders organizing at work.


So it was a surprise to members in June when their parent union, CWA, put the local into trusteeship, at the request of the local’s president and seven of the nineteen executive board members.


Trusteeship meant the union’s bylaws and elected leaders were suspended, and most of its work temporarily ground to a halt. The appointed Director of Organizing and Mobilizing Mary Nowocien and elected Vice President Patrick Weisansal II found themselves locked out of their group chats, email, and union hall, and facing an internal union prosecution.


A staffer of CWA District 1, Erin Spaulding, was assigned as trustee—tasked with maintaining the functioning of the local, setting up and overseeing judicial processes for the charges against officers, and making a plan to return the union to local control.


Nowocien and Weisansal saw the sudden trusteeship as an escalation of a long-running conflict and a deliberate undermining of the upcoming union elections. Weisansal had just announced his intention to run against incumbent President Cori Gambini.


Now the elections are on hold until the trials are over, whenever that is. And lately, the employer has been taking advantage of the turmoil in the union.


While the allegations are serious, members are concerned that the trusteeship was a nuclear option for an internal financial matter and that it has torn apart relationships at the local, weakened opposition to management’s schemes and denied democratic processes to an active, engaged union membership.


ALLEGED TIMECARD ISSUES


The trusteeship filing lists the cause as “serious allegations of financial misconduct” from officers and “dueling charges” between leaders.


Gambini and Executive Vice President Robert Andruszko had accused Nowocien and Weisansal of defrauding the local of thousands of dollars, by getting paid by both the union and their employer for the same hours worked, and by falsifying records. These issues came to light during a timecard audit in the fall of 2025 by their employer, Kaleida Health.


Nowocien and Weisansal acknowledged there were significant errors on old timecards and paychecks, but said it was the product of the employer’s faulty timekeeping and payroll system, and human error. The majority of other officers also had issues, they pointed out, but only some were being singled out for discipline by the local and the employer.


Spaulding, the trustee, interviewed all the suspended officers and allowed the majority to return to their paid positions—with the exception of Nowocien, Weisansal, and three others not facing any charges: the Communications and Political Directors and one of the Area Vice Presidents. Also fired were two longtime staff organizers, on the grounds that there was no work for them to do, according to one, Ann Converso, who had recently helped organize a new unit of substance use disorder counselors and was gearing up for their first contract fight.


Many current leaders on both sides of this schism were part of a reform caucus in Local 1168, the Caucus of Rank-and-File Healthcare Employees (CORHE), which dissolved when they won their positions in 2020.


Since winning, Gambini and a few others have butted heads with Weisansal, Nowocien, and others over how to tackle problems. The latter camp frequently organized their facility—Buffalo General Hospital, the union’s largest unit—to push back against management’s changes and violations. Gambini and leaders aligned with her argued that that wasn’t the right approach—that they had to pick their fights and not overextend the membership, according to Weisansal.


One Buffalo General steward, who asked to not be named, said members were appalled that the trustee had removed elected officers. “If our employer treated one of our members in a similar fashion,” the steward said, “union leadership would rally around them and fight to return them to their position!”


Spaulding wrote in a public FAQ posted on the local’s social media that the temporary administration “is not intended to be punitive or find guilt against any individual in the Local. It is intended to stabilize the Local while issues are …

author: Solarpunk Magazine
title: Solarpunk Horror, Lunarpunk Submissions, and 2027 Magazine Submissions
content:
We’ve got some exciting announcements to share! There’s a brand-new lunarpunk anthology seeking submissions, our special horror-themed issue of Solarpunk Magazine is available for preorder, we’re going to start publishing solarpunk novellas and novels, and our complete 2027 submissions schedule is now up on our website’s submissions page.

So whether you’re a reader looking for your next great story or a writer dreaming up better futures, here’s what’s coming.

Submission Window: November 1 – December 31, 2026

Android Press is preparing to venture into the shadows with What Blooms in Darkness: A Lunarpunk Anthology, edited by our co-editor-in-chief, Justine Norton-Kertson, and scheduled for publication in autumn 2027.

Lunarpunk shares solarpunk’s commitment to ecological regeneration, social justice, community, and liberatory futures, while exploring the possibilities that emerge in darkness, mystery, privacy, dreams, and the hidden corners of our world.

What Blooms in Darkness asks some fascinating questions: What kinds of communities thrive beyond the reach of surveillance? What knowledge survives underground? What forms of liberation become possible when people are free to remain unseen?

Android Press is seeking stories about everything from nocturnal ecosystems and underground communities to secret mutual-aid networks, hidden cultures, rituals, and resistance movements. The anthology welcomes imaginative interpretations of lunarpunk, especially stories that challenge the assumption that darkness is inherently dangerous or frightening.

Genre: Lunarpunk, climate fiction, and related speculative fiction

Eligibility: Original, unpublished fiction by human authors worldwide

Expected publication: Autumn 2027

Whether you’re a writer or a reader, you can easily sign up to get a notification when the anthology’s crowdfunder launches in March 2027!

We’ve spent years exploring what better futures might look like. Now we’re inviting some monsters into the garden. We’re thrilled to reveal the cover and complete table of contents for Solarpunk Magazine Issue #30, our special Solarpunk Horror issue, arriving November 10, 2026!

Horror and solarpunk might seem like an unusual combination, but we think they have a lot to say to each other. What happens when the ghosts of ecological destruction refuse to stay buried? What kinds of monsters might haunt societies struggling to heal centuries of exploitation? And how do things like fear, grief, survival, and resistance fit into our visions of better futures?

This extra large special issue brings together fiction, poetry, essays, and artwork that explore the darker edges of solarpunk imagination. We’re especially excited about the lineup of writers and artists contributing to this issue.

“The Unrooted Sea” by Seiba Rosario

“Bottles, Bones, Skein” by Marisca Pichette

“A Sweetness On The Breeze” by John Leahy

“Blood of the Town, Veins of the Earth” by Katharine Tyndall

“The Ordinary Was Extraordinary All Along: A reflection on loss, appreciation, and radical hope from Gaza” by Aya Al-Hattab

“Reemergence of the Past” by Victoria Black

We’re incredibly grateful to all the contributors who helped bring this experiment in solarpunk horror to life.

Issue #30 releases November 10, 2026, and is available for preorder now for $6.

We also have two special themed issues planned for 2027!

author: Tam Saavedra
title: WEI and UN Women Co-Launches Guide for Disability-Inclusive
content:
Across Asia and the Pacific, 350 million women and girls with disabilities navigate conflict, crisis, and climate instability. While they are frontline peacebuilders, community leaders, and human rights defenders, they remain systematically excluded from formal peace and security decision-making.

To break down these barriers, Women Enabled International (WEI) and the UN Women Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific have officially launched a landmark publication today: the Guidance Note on Disability-Inclusive National Action Plans on Women, Peace and Security in Asia and the Pacific. Released ahead of the annual UN Security Council high-level debate in New York, this first-of-its-kind guide provides a practical, policy-oriented blueprint for governments, policymakers, and civil society.

Read the full Guidance Note on Disability-Inclusive NAPs on WPS in Asia and the Pacific

Historically, women with disabilities in peace policies have been viewed narrowly as victims or passive recipients of protection. Co-drafted through consultations with 26 women and gender-diverse people with disabilities, in collaboration with Women Enabled International and the UN Women Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific, this guide directly challenges that narrative. It grounds its framework in a human rights model of disability and the core movement principle: “Nothing about us without us”.

As WEI Executive Director Maryangel García-Ramos Guadiana stated during the launch:

“The true value of this Guidance Note is that it exists, not as a siloed document, but as a means to ensure we, as feminist disabled change-makers, are not left out of the agenda, but we are the ones who get to set the agenda.”

UN Women Regional Director for Asia and the Pacific, Christine Arab, added:

“National Action Plans on WPS that include everyone lead to peace that lasts.”

The publication was shaped by participatory research, drawing on focus groups and surveys with 26 grassroots leaders with diverse disabilities across the region. It addresses critical ground-level hurdles—including digital exclusion, inaccessible evacuation infrastructure, and ableism in mainstream spaces—ensuring that the voices of women, girls and gender-diverse people with disabilities form the foundation of the guidance.

The publication urges stakeholders to align National Action Plans (NAPs) with international standards—including the CRPD, CEDAW, and UN Security Council Resolution 2475—across all four WPS pillars:

Participation: Reserve seats for organizations of persons with disabilities (OPDs)—especially women-led OPDs—on NAP steering committees with full accessibility support.

Participation: Reserve seats for organizations of persons with disabilities (OPDs)—especially women-led OPDs—on NAP steering committees with full accessibility support.

Prevention: Recognize women and gender-diverse people with disabilities as active peacebuilders and integrate intersectional early-warning indicators.

Prevention: Recognize women and gender-diverse people with disabilities as active peacebuilders and integrate intersectional early-warning indicators.

Protection: Address unique forms of violence (such as caregiver abuse or institutionalization) and guarantee accessible shelters and evacuation procedures.

Protection: Address unique forms of violence (such as caregiver abuse or institutionalization) and guarantee accessible shelters and evacuation procedures.

Relief & Recovery: Ensure transitional justice mechanisms, reparations, and post-conflict upskilling actively include women with disabilities.

Relief & Recovery: Ensure transitional justice mechanisms, reparations, and post-conflict upskilling actively include women with disabilities.

The guide also features a practical Disability-Inclusive WPS NAP Checklist to help stakeholders evaluate progress at every stage of policy implementation.

This Guidance Note was made possible with the generous support of the Government of the Republic of Korea (through the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family) as part of the project “Promoting Leadership of Future Generation Peacebuilders and Change-makers in Asia and the Pacific”, and of the Australian Government under the Regional Framework Towards Peaceful, Inclusive Societies (2023–2027).

author: James Moore
title: Be More Human: Why Mental Health Care is Broken and What We Can Do to Fix It: An Interview with Sir Norman Lamb
content:
H

ello, this is James and welcome to the Mad in America podcast. This week, we are asking why people with mental health conditions die 15-20 years earlier than people without. Why does the UK spend £100 million every year placing patients far from home? How did the question, ‘What matters to you?’ transform mental health care in Norway? Can mental healthcare be more compassionate?


Sir Norman Lamb asks these questions, and more, in his book

Be More Human

, published by Jessica Kingsley Publishers. Sir Norman is a former Health Minister, an NHS trust chair, and a dedicated mental health campaigner who was knighted in 2019 for his public and political service. He has seen the cracks in the system up close. In his book, he sets out to answer these questions, and many others, uncovering the reasons why our mental health services are failing. He shares eye-opening stories from patients who have been let down, but also inspiring tales from trailblazers who are shaking things up with creative, community-first solutions.


In this interview, we talk about how his personal and professional experiences led to him wanting to lift the lid on the UK’s mental health system. We also discuss how personal accounts of mistreatment and abuse motivated him to think differently about the human element so often missing from mental healthcare. Finally, we discuss novel, community-based alternatives that offer dignity, compassion and hope.


The transcript below has been edited for length and clarity. Listen to the audio of the interview here.


James Moore: Sir Norman, welcome. Thank you so much for joining me for the Mad in America podcast. It’s an honour to get to talk to you and to delve into your recently published book,

Be More Human

, published by Jessica Kingsley Publishers in August this year.


Before we kick off, I have to say that upon reading the book, I found that it’s one of those books that stays with you long after you finish it. We’ll come on to talk about some of the details, but the personal stories shared, the lived experience accounts, particularly resonate. Welcome, first of all.


Norman Lamb:

 Thank you, James. You can drop the Sir bit. I’m happy just to be Norman, but it’s really good to talk to you; great that we’ve got this opportunity.


Moore: First, I’d like to talk a little bit about you and your entry into this world. You’re someone with wide-ranging experience across government. You’ve been a Liberal Democrat member of parliament for Norfolk. You’ve held positions in science and technology and business and skills departments. 

More recently, you’ve spent time in the Department of Health and Social Care and also, perhaps very importantly, been Chair of mental health services at South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust.


How was it that those experiences came together to you wanting to put a spotlight on mental health services and how they can be made more compassionate?


Lamb:

 Yes, it’s been an interesting journey, James, because if you scroll back to the late ’90s, early 2000s, I hadn’t really focused much on mental health. It hadn’t touched me in any particular way. Then I was elected to parliament in 2001, and as a member of parliament in North Norfolk, I wanted to be available to constituents to take up their concerns. I became aware of a lot of people coming to see me with their own stories about the mental health system and how, in their terms, they felt it was failing them in various ways: awful waiting lists, awful use of coercion and institutionalisation. Those stories leave a mark on you.


Then we were hit personally in our own family. Our oldest son, Archie, when he was 15, was diagnosed with obsessive-compulsive disorder. We managed to get a referral to the Mental Health Trust at a moment when we were fairly desperate. He was in quite a bad way, and we were told that we would have to wait up to six months for anything to happen.


When you’re a family in despair and really anxious about a child, being told you’ve got to wait up to six months is sort of hopeless, really. I’m acutely conscious that for many people nowadays, it could be a year waiting. We did what any family would do if they’re able to. We paid for care, and in a way, there’s the injustice because most people can’t do that. They are literally just left waiting.


I sort of concluded that a service that leaves people waiting so long when they’re desperate is not really a service at all in any meaningful sense, and …

author: Marion Brown
title: A Decade of the Rise and Rise of “Functional Neurological Disorder” (FND)
content:
“FND occurs when the brain has difficulty sending and receiving signals properly, even though scans like MRI or CT appear normal. It affects movement, sensation, speech, cognition, and other functions. Symptoms are genuine, involuntary, and can be disabling.”


—

NIH website


M

ore and more people are being diagnosed with ‘functional neurological disorder’ (FND). FND is essentially a term for ‘unexplained’ symptoms—including severely disabling symptoms such as movement disorders, blackouts and so-called ‘non-epileptic seizures’—and which doctors say has no clear cause. I began to notice about 10 years ago that these ‘unexplained’ symptoms were the same symptoms as those experienced by some people when taking prescribed drugs for ‘depression’, ‘anxiety’, ‘stress’, etc. and especially when trying to reduce or come off these psychiatric drugs.


I began to meet more and more people with the FND diagnosis who were also experiencing withdrawal effects after stopping antidepressants, benzodiazepines, and other psychiatric drugs—but no doctors seemed to connect the two. I have now come to think that the diagnosis of FND is essentially a way to dismiss adverse effects and withdrawal symptoms—so that doctors can continue to say that psychiatric drugs have no such effects because these effects are diagnosed as something else, even while admitting that they can’t explain what that something else is.


Background


I had trained over some years and became qualified as a

Human Givens Practitioner

 in 2011, and subsequently worked as a private Human Givens practitioner/psychotherapist in Helensburgh, Scotland. This work brought me into contact with many people who, it turned out, were struggling with the effects of having taken medicines prescribed usually by their primary care physician for ‘depression’, ‘anxiety’, ‘insomnia’ etc. This led on to the co-founding of a local ‘motley-crew’ patient self-help group, Recovery and Renewal, in 2013.


Initially we met locally to offer companionship and free non-drug wellness support—and also to ask collectively for formal National Health Service (NHS) support for people who were struggling with adverse and withdrawal effects of these very commonly prescribed drugs. Our efforts were mostly met with fobbing off by local GPs and by official NHS and Scottish Health service bodies.


My lay-person research campaign began as an attempt to formally raise concerns with prescribers about the apparently overlooked adverse and withdrawal effects of antidepressants and benzodiazepines—which were and are (especially antidepressants) commonly prescribed in primary care settings. People who had come together through our Recovery and Renewal group (which later become

a wide-reaching Facebook Group

), were (and are) fellow researchers and campaigners. We are now mainly active on X @recover2renew.


Questioning ‘Unexplained Symptoms’


We began questioning the diagnosis of Medically Unexplained Symptoms (MUS) and Functional Neurological Disorders (FND) in 2016—as it was apparent by then that these mysterious disabling conditions (of ‘unknown aetiology’) were appearing in people’s medical records and that these ‘conditions’ (listed in the DSM) clearly shared many symptoms with antidepressant (and benzodiazepine) side effects and/or withdrawal effects.


I came across a book,

ABC of Medically Unexplained Symptoms

 (2013) and was startled to find chapters written by the (now internationally well-known) FND ‘experts’ Jon Stone and Alan Carson in Scotland—chapters in particular which seemed to refer to the very symptoms that people were experiencing as a consequence of taking (and/or trying to withdraw from) antidepressants & benzodiazepines.


Being also based in Scotland, this was particularly pertinent to the people in our local group, with

Stone

 and

Carson

 having close connections with (and funding from) the Scottish Government and Scotland’s National Health Service. It became apparent that ‘Medically Unexplained Symptoms’ (a DSM diagnosis) seemed to be becoming more often diagnosed as ‘Functional Neurological Symptoms’ (FND).


My own first article was published by Mad in America in December 2016:

“An Outsider’s Observation: Medically Unexplained Somatic Symptoms in General Practice

Le 31 octobre, c'est Halloween – la fête des morts. Généralement ils reviennent exiger des bonbons ou des sorts. Le 17 octobre, le gouvernement a choisi les sorts. Résultat : on vient de quitter l'époque contemporaine et, depuis, Bismillah, c'est les ténèbres. Mais ces ténèbres, elles sont super drôles.


Jamais autant de créatures multiformes n'avaient déferlé dans nos insurrections. Il nous a fallu analyser cet étrange phénomène. Alors on a invité deux experts des ténèbres joyeuses : le philosophe Norman Ajari et l'essayiste Pacôme Thiellement. La brèche entre les mondes vient de s'ouvrir, elle n'est pas près de se refermer. title: ziq - Anarchie ist
content:

Anarchie ist ein fortlaufender Prozess zur Demontage von Autorität.

Anarchie ist die unerbittliche Verneinung von Herrschaftsstrukturen, das Bestreben, sich kleine Bereiche des Lebens frei von Ausbeutung und Leid zu schaffen.

Anarchie ist der kompromisslose Vorstoß gegen Unterdrückung und die lautstarke Forderung nach Autonomie und Selbstbestimmung, die Ablehnung aller Klassen, Institutionen und Dogmen, die geschaffen wurden, um Menschen zu beherrschen.

Anarchie ist vor allem eine Praxis, nicht eine Theorie. Es geht darum, aktiv daran zu arbeiten, autoritäre Verhältnisse zu beenden, wo immer sie existieren, und nicht-autoritäre Alternativen aufzubauen. Es geht nicht darum, eine Lebensweise für einen imaginären Ort, eine imaginäre Zeit und imaginäre Menschen vorzuschreiben. Es geht um reale Menschen und die Bewältigung realer Probleme.

Anarchie ist eine lebendige und atmende Praxis, die wir in unser tägliches Leben einbauen. Eine persönliche Haltung gegen die Herrschaft, die alle unsere Entscheidungen beeinflusst und so den Verlauf unserer Existenz prägt.

Es gibt kein Endziel für Anarchie. Sie ist ein fortwährender, nicht enden wollender Kampf gegen hierarchische Strukturen und die Autoritätspersonen, die im Luxus an der Spitze dieser Strukturen sitzen.

Anarchie ist der Wunsch nach Freiheit von Tyrannei. Anarchie sind unzählige Generationen verschiedener Menschen mit dem Drang, freier zu sein als sie es unter den Systemen sind, die sie gewaltsam regieren.

Anarchie ist die Ablehnung der Regierung, der Staaten, der Grenzen, des Kapitals, des Patriarchats, des Gender-Essenzialismus, der Sklaverei, der Ideologie, der Rechten, der Linken, des Klerus, der Demokratie, des Privateigentums, der Technokratie, der Kernfamilie, des Humanismus, des Imperialismus, der Gefängnisse, der Fabriken, der Gründerväter, der Bürokratie, der Ethnokratie, der Heteronormativität, der Idole, der Tradition, der Polizeiarbeit, der Neuronormativität, des Ökozids, der Zivilisation und jeder anderen Form von Autorität.

Anarchie ist Gemeinschaftsgärten, Umsonstläden, Graffiti, 3D-gedruckte Waffen, FKK, vegane Potlucks [1], Hausbesetzungen, Lebensmittelwälder, Sabotage von Pipelines, freie Software, die Befreiung von Kühen, Ladendiebstahl, das Sichern von Saatgut alter Kulturpflanzen, die Bildung autonomer Zonen, Attentate auf Tyrannen, Guerilla-Gärtnern, Zines schreiben, Regenwasser auffangen, Wahlurnen verbrennen, Biodiversität, Abschaffung der Whiteness, Hacken, Aquaponik, Musik machen, Upcycling, Polizeistationen abfackeln und Wildblumen in der ganzen Landschaft säen.

Anarchist*innen sind jene Personen, die sich weigern, von irgendjemandem oder irgendetwas regiert, beherrscht oder dominiert zu werden. Anarchist*innen sind wütende, verbitterte, verlorene, ängstliche, desillusionierte, gewalttätige, friedliche, mutige, idealistische, mitreißende, furchtlose Träumende.

Ein*e Anarchist*in steht allein gegen die riesige Flut der Autorität, die in alle Richtungen ansteigt. Anarchist*innen verbinden sich mit jeder geschundenen, geknechteten Seele im gemeinsamen Angriff gegen die rücksichtslosen Systeme, die uns entmachten und entfremden sollen.

Anarchie ist geprägt von endlosen Widersprüchen, existenzieller Angst und unerträglichen inneren Konflikten, und doch ergibt Anarchie für jede Person, die entsetzt oder wütend ist über die groben Ungerechtigkeiten, die diesen kleinen blauen Planeten verschlingen, einen perfekten Sinn. Anarchie ist für jede Person, die ein Leben in Würde anstrebt.

Anarchie ist ein unmögliches, absonderliches, aber für unser Überleben notwendiges Streben.

author: Archipelago Anarchist Archive
title: Archipelago Anarchist Archive, Perpustakaan Anarkis, and Anarsip: Jurnal Arsip & Perpustakaan Anti-otoritarian (A Brief Introduction)
content:
Initiatives in anarchist archiving, librarianship, and journals of archives & libraries in Indonesia

The Archipelago Anarchist Archive (AAA) is an informal, alternative archives and library initiative established in 2024 with the aim of preserving and distributing anti-authoritarian materials. AAA is driven by a number of anarchist archivists and librarians from various cities in Indonesia.

The materials that AAA focuses on are those produced in, and related to, the archipelago (known as Indonesia), whether in Indonesian or in non-Indonesian languages. These materials can take the form of texts, photographs, audio, video, and so on. All of AAA's digital archive collections can be accessed through the Internet Archive.

Link to the Archipelago Anarchist Archive collection: https://archive.org/details/@archipelago-anti-authoritarian-archive

Perpustakaan Anarkis (Anarchist Library) is an preservation and distribution project for anti-authoritarian materials based on plain text. Plain text was chosen because it makes it easier for authors and translators to distribute their work, easier for publishers to reproduce it, and easier for those who wish to archive it[1]. Perpustakaan Anarkis understands anti-authoritarianism in a flexible manner, though not without limits. Therefore, it can be said that Perpustakaan Anarkis accepts and includes both anarchist materials (from all tendencies, except anarcho-capitalism and anarcho-nationalism) and materials that can enrich anarchism, such as avant-garde(ism) that challenges not only the boundaries of art but also the state and centralized power, libertarian Marxism, autonomism, democratic confederalism, and so on. In addition, Perpustakaan Anarkis also accepts and includes reportage from the front lines (confrontation) and the home front (care) of flashpoints of popular struggle and resistance, labor strikes, and so on.

Because in anarchism, decentralization and prefiguration are important. And by practicing decentralization and prefiguration, we (and us all) no longer need to wait to act and be overly dependent on a single central point.

Besides anarcho-capitalism and anarcho-nationalism, Perpustakaan Anarkis is also not intended for authoritarian Marxists, misanthropic individuals, extractive technologism (automation that subordinates), avant-garde(ism) that leads to fascism, and other authoritarian tendencies and centralized power.

[1] Authors and translators can distribute their works without the hassle of layout, editing, cover design, and other technical work. Conversely, publishers no longer need to go through the trouble of dealing with writing and translation. And archivists—in addition to finding archiving easier—will receive various versions of the work.

Link to the Perpustakaan Anarkis collection: https://id.anarchistlibraries.net/special/index

Anarsip: Jurnal Arsip & Perpustakaan Anti-otoritarian (Anarsip: Journal of Anti-authoritarian Archives & Libraries) (published periodically, every 6 months) is a space for theorizing–practicing–theorizing–practicing anarchist archives and librarianship. Because we believe that anarchist archives and librarianship should not stop at merely the definition of "managed by, and archiving materials of, anarchist(s) and/or anti-authoritarian [movements and ideas]," but also means using methods, practicing ways of working, and thinking in an anarchist and/or anti-authoritarian manner. If the Situationist International said "to be avant-garde is to move in step with reality" (Internationale Situationiste #8); then we say "to be anarchist archiving and librarianship is to move in step with reality and anarchism."

Link to follow the developments of Anarsip: https://id.anarchistlibraries.net/special/anarsip-jurnal-arsip-perpustakaan-anti-otoritarian

Archipelago Anarchist Archive (AAA) adalah inisiatif pengarsipan dan perpustakaan informal nan alternatif yang didirikan pada tahun 2024 dengan tujuan mempreservasi sekaligus mendistribusi materi-materi anti-otoritarian. AAA digerakkan oleh sejumlah arsiparis dan pustakawan anarkis yang berasal dari berbagai kota di Indonesia.

Adapun materi-materi yang menjadi fokus dari AAA adalah materi-materi yang diproduksi di, dan yang berkaitan dengan, wilayah kepulauan (yang kini disebut sebagai Indonesia) baik itu yang berbahasa Indonesia maupun yang berbahasa non-indonesia. author: Indo
title: On “Sultat al-Majalis”
content:
Rather interesting text on the Arab Council Communist group “Sultat al-Majalis” formed by Lafif Lakhdar and Mustapha Khayati. Originally published in "Al-Hewar Al-Mutamadin, Issue 8699, 6th May 2026”. Can be found here.

The Arab Communist Grouping, which published the magazine Sultat al-Majalis (The Power of Workers’ Councils), was a revolutionary organization that adopted the ideas of council communism, drawing inspiration from the experiences of workers’ councils in Europe. The group was active in the early 1970s and consisted of intellectuals and workers of Maghrebi (North African) origin living in France. Its members were influenced by the events of May 1968 in France and by the left-wing critique of the existing socialist regimes of the time.

The group focused on the idea that revolution should be led by workers’ councils elected directly by the workers themselves. It rejected the traditional Leninist party model and centralized bureaucratic authority. It regarded Soviet communism, as well as its Chinese Maoist counterpart, as systems that had nothing to do with socialism. In its view, both were forms of state capitalism, owned and controlled by a new class known as the bureaucracy, which, like the bourgeoisie, was hostile to the working class and its independent movement.

The organization also launched a scathing critique of existing Arab regimes, whether self-proclaimed progressive or conservative, as well as all Palestinian organizations and the very idea of a Palestinian revolution, insofar as it remained detached from an all-encompassing Arab revolution aimed at overthrowing the existing state structures across the various Arab countries.

The first and only issue of Sultat al-Majalis was published in January 1974. Its purpose was to promote awareness of the self-organization of workers and peasants, free from the tutelage of political parties. The magazine included translations of texts by leading international theorists of council communism, articles analyzing the Arab-Israeli conflict from a class-based perspective that rejected nationalism, and studies of Arab labor movements.

Despite its limited organizational base, the group had a notable intellectual influence in independent left-wing circles and helped introduce concepts of workers’ self-management. It remains one of the distinctive experiments in the history of the Arab Left, representing an attempt to offer a third alternative outside the frameworks of Arab nationalism and official communism aligned with Moscow.

The group operated clandestinely, which meant that some of its contributors wrote under pseudonyms while others remained behind the scenes. Its initial core included young university graduates from Beirut who had been influenced by the global New Left movement but chose to work under the umbrella of the group in order to distinguish themselves from the official communist parties and the Organization of Communist Action in Lebanon.

The relationship between Lafif Lakhdar (1934–2013) and Mustapha Khayati was central to the establishment of this tendency. In his writings, Lafif Lakhdar confirmed that he and Mustapha Khayati had overseen the publication of Sultat al-Majalis.

Mustapha Khayati was a Tunisian activist and intellectual, a prominent member of the Situationist International in France, and the author of the famous pamphlet On the Poverty of Student Life. Khayati brought Situationist thought and the critique of the “Society of the Spectacle” into the Arab context, an influence that was reflected in the pages of Sultat al-Majalis.

Lafif Lakhdar was a radical left-wing Tunisian intellectual and one of the most outspoken critics of state capitalism in the Soviet Union and the Arab regimes. He argued that the genuine alternative lay in the “power of workers’ councils,” exercising self-management. This position formed the central ideological identity of the group.

The magazine served as a platform through which Khayati and Lakhdar translated unorthodox Marxist texts and analyzed Arab conflicts from an internationalist perspective.

Regarding the joint activities of three members of the group in early 1970, before its formal establishment, the Palestinian journalist Bilal al-Hassan wrote the following in an article discussing the book Nayef Hawatmeh Speaks, published in Beirut in 1997:

Must We Lie to Please the Critics?

Social Conditions and Character.

Anarchists, Wise and Otherwise.

We find ourselves in a world of conflicting ideas, and every person who has individuality enough developed to be more, in human life, than a domestic animal or lifeless machine, must align himself with others who hold the same opinions, whether he will or not, and then he is in the view of others, and perhaps in his own view, labeled with the name of the idea he holds. So we find that nearly every person is labeled, and some persons have a number of labels.

Finding that we must be something—must hold to certain ideas and work for certain ends—if we work at all, or amount to any more in human life than an ox, or an ax, it very naturally follows that we will adopt and work for the prevalence of such ideas as will bring us the greatest happiness, now or bye and bye. That is why I am an Anarchist. I am convinced that to work for the realization of the Anarchist ideal will bring me more satisfaction than an adherence to, or working for, any other ideal would bring me.

But every one should be able and willing to give a reason for the “faith that is within him,” and I will try and do so.

I find myself in a world of sunshine and shade; of joy and sorrow; of happiness and woe. All around me I see fellow beings; beings that are constituted very much as I am, have similar desires, hopes and aspirations. I find that they are constantly trying to gratify these desires; to realize their hopes and attain to that for which they aspire. I find further that they can do these things only by exploiting inorganic nature, and by assisting each other. I find that as things are now, these beings instead of mutually assisting each other are constantly striving to injure each other, not because they take delight in the suffering of a fellow, but because they see no other way of satisfying their desires and aspirations. They think this state of affairs wrong, and are constantly clamoring for a change, but have not yet learned the great fundamental fact of human solidarity—of our interdependence.

Long have the various members of the human family sought to adjust themselves to environment, and of late have begun to endeavor to adjust the environment to suit themselves. All mankind craves for freedom, but most of the people have sought to gain freedom by subjugating others, or by restricting all alike. They have not learned that they cannot be free while they are holding others, or while they seek to restrict the freedom of others. No one desires to be injured, and yet no one can be secure from injury as long as he injures others. We all wish to be free from injury. I crave for freedom. I see that others want the same condition, and I know that my freedom can be made secure only by the freedom of all others. I know of no other ideal but Anarchy that, if really would secure freedom to me and to all others, therefore I am an Anarchist.

content:

Переведено для

Источник

 Сегодня революционная борьба страдает от недостатка способностей на индивидуальном, организационном и социальном уровнях. Нашим крупнейшим социальным движениям, как и нашим самым страстным индивидуальным усилиям необходим милитантский импульс, способный стратегически соединять разрозненные действия. Милитантность позволяет массовым движениям испытывать обоснованную гордость и ощущать свою причастность к наиболее успешным революционным действиям. Она также даёт активному меньшинству чёткую цель и место в формировании социальной силы. Однако стойкая милитантность — это акт свободы, но сегодня большинство людей оказываются «втянуты» в неё не из сознательного выбора, а в силу обстоятельств. Мы, люди, борющиеся за социальную революцию, хотим иметь возможность самим решать, как развивать нашу милитантность. Мы требуем возможности сознательно участвовать в милитантской практике, поскольку так революционный потенциал наших движений будет обеспечен свободой людей.


 И всё же, даже при наличии свободы выбрать милитантскую деятельность остаётся вопрос:


 Куда революционерам направить свои усилия, чтобы их деятельность была связана с той реальностью, в которой в конечном счёте будет жить народ, пробуждала в людях чувство субъектности в Истории и принятие ответственности за этичность своих действий в настоящем?


 Наш ответ следует искать во взрослом образовании, которое представляет собой особенно благоприятную почву для долгосрочного участия в судьбе народных движений. Людям всегда будет необходимо учиться. Поэтому мы предлагаем создать, поддерживать и защищать революционное образовательное направление, которое станет местом встречи и обмена опытом для людей, стремящихся учиться и учить других, — в том числе членов сообщества, активистов, организаторов, диссидентов и милитантов.


 Стремление учиться, которое обычно связывают с молодёжью, новичками, студентами и теми, кому недостаёт опыта, не следует отвергать как стихийную форму организации. Нередко люди, «научившись», переходят к «действиям»: применяют полученные знания, но покидают пространство обучения, в котором они развивали свои способности, не заботясь о том, чтобы сохранить прочную связь с его методами и целями.


 Однако мы настаиваем на том, что это пространство нуждается в целенаправленной защите, если оно должно оказывать долговременное влияние на социальные преобразования. Прежде всего, защита этого пространства со временем будет способствовать коллективному становлению милитантов, которые смогут использовать общий образовательный опыт как основу для единой стратегии и политической программы. Кроме того, сохранение этого пространства будет способствовать пониманию значимости милитантов в социальной борьбе и осознанию того, насколько милитантность необходима для успеха революционных движений.


 Стремление учиться должно выполнять две функции: с одной стороны, служить пространством, где люди получают инструменты и обретают сообщество, необходимые для становления милитантами; с другой — знакомить более широкое сообщество с понятием милитантности и её теорией. Таким образом, наша цель едина, но включает два самостоятельных аспекта, которые необходимо развивать одновременно:


 Мы должны создать образовательное пространство для становления милитантов, а наше регулярное участие в его жизни должно обеспечивать надёжные пути как к милитантской деятельности, так и обратно — к образованию.


 Таким образом, стремление учиться станет пространством, где люди с большим и меньшим опытом смогут встречаться и учиться друг у друга.


 При столь ясных целях нас, несомненно, будут оценивать по нашим же критериям — приверженности делу и стойкости. Ясное определение того, что представляет собой стремление учиться, сможет воплотиться в жизнь лишь благодаря нашей приверженности ему, а его эффективность можно будет оценить лишь по тому, насколько долго оно сохраняется и насколько верно остаётся своим целям.

En svensk förf. Fredrik Lindholm, har någon gång år 1909 "gjort" en skrift om anarkismen, vari han åtagit sig att framställa anarkismens uppgifter. Skriftens huvudsakliga innehåll har blivit ett upprepande av de kungamord och tsarmord, som anarkisterna anklagats för, och i vissa fall väl även utfört.

Den omfattar en period då despotismen, liksom nu i många länder, intog högsätet, då folket var helt rättslöst, då anarkisterna och andra motståndare till stats- och utsugningsmonopolen, behandlades som förbrytare och fördrevs ur landet. Ofta fanns det blott en utväg att väcka uppmärksamhet för dessa ohyggliga förhållanden: Bombens detonation.

Bomben var avsedd eller träffade en herre som i sitt dagliga liv, kanske tanklöst, undertecknat hundratals dödsdomar och förvisningar, som framställde sig vara i kompani med gud, innehade kontroll över alla kanaler till det existerande rättsväsendet, befallde över polis och militär, följaktligen utövade ensam härskarmakt eller representerande sådan makt.

Jag anser mig inte i detta sammanhang ha någon befogenhet att diskutera huruvida det var rätt eller inte. Det skulle bli en alltför vidlyftig avhandling, att framställa vad man talar för och emot i ett sammanhang som detta. Våldet har alltid karaktäriserats som ultima ratio, en sista utväg.

I anarkismens politiska och sociala tankevärld har våldet ingen plats. Såväl de politiska som sociala uttrycksformerna skapar en miljö och atmosfär, som avlägsnar ifrån våldet och främjar inbördes hjälp. Dessa förändringar bygger anarkisterna inte på en sinnets förändring som grundlag, men på fakta som att möjligheterna för det sociala välståndets fördelning uppnåtts och herraväldets och förtryckets förverkligande avlägsnats.

Den fulländning som anarkismens samhällsideal företräder bygger på orsakernas upphävande, orsakerna till våldsmentaliteten.

De invändningar som göras, bygga på helt andra förutsättningar. Den ägande som fruktar för att tjuvar och rånare skola tillägna sig hans egendom, vinkar indignerat bort pratet om att våldet skulle bli överflödigt, noggrant förbiseende att människorna under kommunistiskt-anarkistiska samhällsformer inte ha någon anledning att stjäla eller med våld försvara sig mot stöld.

Militären, som tränat in sin yrkesmentalitet och den fanatiske chauvinisten komma med sina argument! Skola vi inte försvara oss mot utländska fiender?

Här är en fråga som redan nuet borde taga klar ställning till. Finns det någon mening i att försvara sig mot utländska fiender? Vad är det man kan och vill försvara? Marken, naturen, sjöarna, kan inte försvaras, kan inte erövras. Under ett krig kan man däremot förstöra dem. Ja, måste förstöra. Fransmän och belgare förstörde stora delar av sina egna områden, direkt, när tyskarna trängde fram under världskriget, förstörde för att inte tyskarna skulle få nytta av det. Franska och belgiska sprängämnen och volymkulor träffade fransk och belgisk natur - och förstörde kanske lika mycket som "fienden", tyskarna, förstörde.

Krigets mekanisering är ett kapitel som vilar tungt på vågen när det gäller att mäta våldets uppgift i nuet. Förr, när en hord människor dreva mot varandra med pikar och muskedunder, var det hela ett farligt äventyr, som begränsades av vapnens räckvidd. Nu finnes det inte längre någon sådan begränsning. Brand-, gift- och spränggaser ha förverkat varje tanke på "försvar" och mobiliserat angreppstanken som enda möjlighet i en våldskonflikt mellan staterna. De långskjutande kanonerna understryka denna utveckling. Ett krig blir blott ett fruktansvärt förgörande av allt levande.

Enda synpunkten som talar för att med krigets våld lösa de mellanfolkliga konflikterna, är den, att vapenfabrikerna och sprängämnestillverkarna behöva experimentera och måste ha stora dividender.

title: Killing King Abacus - Notizen zu einer neuen Analyse der Institutionen der Herrschaft
content:

Es ist kaum 65 Jahre her, da war es absolut üblich, in der anarchistischen Literatur Analysen der Institutionen zu lesen, in denen sich die verschiedenen Formen der Herrschaft manifestierten. Wenn man beispielsweise über die Unterdrückung der Frauen schrieb, dann wurden die Familie und die Ehe untersucht und bloßgestellt. Wenn die Unterdrückung von Vergnügen und der Freude des Lebens zur Diskussion stand, dann wurden Religion und Gesetz ins Visier genommen. Der institutionelle Rahmen, in dem sich diese Gesellschaft abspielt wurde als Quelle der Ausbeutung, Herrschaft und Entfremdung wahrgenommen.

Es scheint so, als wäre dieser institutionelle Rahmen in jüngerer Zeit größtenteils vergessen worden zu sein. Von den verschiedenen Institutionen, in die unser entfremdetes kreatives Potenzial zu unserem Nachteil akkumuliert wurde, scheinen nur noch der Staat und das Kapital (und gelegentlich die Technologie) in einem bedeutenden Ausmaß Erwähnung zu finden und selbst diese werden häufig mehr als Geisteszustände, denn als konkrete soziale Institutionen behandelt. So entdecken wir beispielsweise, dass Anarchist*innen gegen Staatlichkeit (was auch immer das sein soll) sind, anstatt gegen den Staat. Auf diese Weise kann etwa ein Bookchin behaupten, gegen Staatlichkeit zu sein, während er den altertümlichen griechischen Stadt-Staat als Modell für seine demokratisierte Version der „Anarchie“ bewirbt.

Jede andere Form der Unterdrückung wird ebenfalls zu einem „-ismus“ (Rassismus, Sexismus, usw.) oder schlimmerem (Homophobie impliziert beispielsweise eine psychologische Störung, die einer Behandlung bedarf, anstatt einer sozialen Repression, die nach Revolte verlangt). Natürlich verleugnen wir nicht die Realitäten der Ideologien der Bigotterie und ihrer Durchdringung der Gedanken und Gefühle der Ausgebeuteten und Unterdrückten. Aber ohne ein Verständnis des institutionellen Rahmens der Unterdrückung und Herrschaft ist es nicht möglich zu verstehen, wie die herrschende Klasse diese Ideologien dazu nutzt, diejenigen zu spalten, die sie ausbeutet.

Selbst die anscheinend Radikalsten (weil ihre Rhetorik am extremsten ist) innerhalb des anarchistischen Millieus entgehen dem nicht. Die von primitivistischen und antizivilisatorischen Kreisen kommende Kritik richtet ihre verbalen Angriffe allzu häufig gegen eine nebulöse, schlecht definierte Zivilisation. Gewiss klingt „Für die Zerstörung der Zivilisation“ radikal. Meiner eigenen Definition gemäß stimme ich damit sogar überein. Aber meiner Definition nach ist Zivilisation nicht irgendeine nebulöse, weitestgehend mentale Kategorie, die dem Rationalismus oder dem westlichen Denken oder welcher unerwünschten Denkweise auch immer entspringt; sie ist ein Netzwerk konkreter sozialer Institutionen, die ich in meinem Alltag konfrontiere: Staat, Wirtschaft, Religion, die Familie, technologische Systeme, und so weiter, allesamt sehr reale Entitäten, die nicht von Gedankenspielen beseitigt werden werden.

Und genau hier tappt die derzeitige Tendenz in eine Falle. Wenn eine Analyse des institutionellen Rahmens der Unterdrückung, Ausbeutung, Herrschaft und Entfremdung vergessen wird, dann tritt Therapie an die Stelle von Revolution. Wir sind dann gezwungen, uns mit den pathetischen, weinerlichen Geständnissen eines Chris Crass zu beschäftigen oder auch der schlechten Popkultur-Psychologie der Autor*innen des Textes „Stick it to the Manarchy“ (wobei schon der Gebrauch eines Begriffs wie „manarchy“ ein sicheres Zeichen dafür ist, dass jemand nichts hörenswertes zu sagen hat), die versuchen ihren „Sexismus“, „Rassismus“, „Homophobie“ und „Klassismus“ abzulegen, die nicht länger irgendwelche Ideologien der Bigotterie sind, sondern niedere mentale Krankheiten, unter denen die selbsternannten „Privilegierten“ aller Klassen leiden.

Jede*r ernsthafte revolutionäre Anarchist*in muss sehen, dass das nur eine weitere List der Feiglinge und jener ist, die ein Interesse an der Aufrechterhaltung der herrschenden Ordnung haben, die eigentliche Entscheidung darüber, auf wessen Seite sie im Kampf gegen diese Gesellschaft stehen, aufzuschieben. Diejenigen von uns, die es mit der Zerstörung der gegenwärtigen Welt ernst meinen, um unsere Leben selbst zu gestalten, haben keine Zeit für diese selbstgerechten Gedankenspielereien, die so sehr an Selbsthilfegruppen erinnern („Mein Name ist … …

author: rezgar2
title: نحو أممية يسارية رقمية في مواجهة الرأسمالية الرقمية، اليسار الرقمي في زمن الخوارزميات
content:
إن المعركة حول التكنولوجيا هي أيضاً معركة حول الملكية والسلطة والوعي ومستقبل البشرية. ومع اتساع دور الفضاء الرقمي بوصفه إحدى الساحات الرئيسية للصراع الطبقي، يمكن للأممية اليسارية الرقمية أن تصبح نقطة انطلاق لتجديد العمل الأممي عموماً. ويتمثل التحدي اليوم في البناء على التشخيص بأدوات جماعية للمواجهة، وفي تطوير التعاون العملي القائم بين قوى اليسار وتوسيعه، ليكمل المواقف والبيانات التضامنية بعمل مشترك أكثر تنظيماً واستمرارية، وفي التوجه التدريجي من منصات الاحتكارات إلى بدائل مستقلة وديمقراطية. وبذلك يمكن أن تتحول إمكانات الثورة الرقمية من امتياز تستأثر به حفنة من الشركات والدول الكبرى إلى مكسب عام يخدم الإنسان وتحرره.

صدر حديثاً كتاب «نحو أممية يسارية رقمية في مواجهة الرأسمالية الرقمية، اليسار الرقمي في زمن الخوارزميات» نصوص ودراسات وبرنامج عمل حول اليسار الرقمي والأممية اليسارية الرقمية، من إعدادي وتأليفي، وهو متاح إلكترونياً ومجاناً.

يشهد العالم ثورة رقمية متسارعة تعيد تشكيل الاقتصاد والعمل والسياسة والوعي الإنساني. وفي الوقت الذي تفتح فيه هذه الثورة إمكانات هائلة للتقدم والتحرر البشري وتجاوز الفقر والأمراض، تتركز ملكية أدواتها ومواردها الأساسية في أيدي حفنة من الاحتكارات الرأسمالية المدعومة من الدول الكبرى. وفي المقابل، تتسع الاحتجاجات الجماهيرية والشبابية في كثير من بلدان العالم، مستفيدة من الأدوات الرقمية في التنظيم والتعبئة، ومؤكدة أن الظروف الموضوعية لتجاوز الرأسمالية قائمة.

ومن هذا التناقض تنبع الحاجة إلى مسار متكامل يبدأ بفهم الرأسمالية الرقمية، ويمر بإغناء تجربة اليسار فكرياً وتنظيمياً بما يواكب التطورات الراهنة، وصولاً إلى بناء أممية يسارية رقمية قادرة على التأثير.

تتيح الثورة الرقمية تقليص ساعات العمل، وتطوير الخدمات الصحية والتعليمية، وتحرير الإنسان من الأعمال المرهقة والمتكررة. غير أن هذه الإمكانات تتطور في إطار علاقات إنتاج رأسمالية، تستحوذ فيها الاحتكارات على القسم الأكبر من مكاسب التقدم التكنولوجي.

فالخوارزميات والمنصات الرقمية ليست محايدة اجتماعياً أو طبقياً، إذ تتأثر بعلاقات الملكية والتمويل والإدارة. وتتجاوز هذه الهيمنة حدود الاقتصاد إلى تشكيل الوعي وتوسيع المراقبة وتوظيف التكنولوجيا في القتل والحروب، ويزيد تقارب بعض قوى اليمين المتطرف مع الاحتكارات التكنولوجية من مخاطر الفاشية الرقمية.

وأمام هذا الواقع، يبرز السؤال الجوهري: كيف يقاوم اليسار الرأسمالية في طورها الرقمي المتقدم، ويفتح الطريق نحو بديل اشتراكي إنساني أكثر عدلاً، محلياً وعالمياً؟ وكيف يجدد نفسه ويطورها ليكون قادراً على ذلك؟

فقد أصبحت الرأسمالية الرقمية قوة عابرة للحدود، بينما يبقى جزء كبير من العمل اليساري الرقمي محصوراً داخل الأطر الوطنية، ويعاني ضعف التنسيق الرقمي الأممي. وتكشف التجارب الحديثة حجم الخطر الذي يواجهه اليسار في هذا الميدان.

ففي البرازيل، وخلال سباق رئاسي بالغ التقارب عام 2026 بين لولا دا سيلفا ومرشح اليمين المتطرف فلافيو بولسونارو، اتهم لولا وحزبه شركة ميتا بتقليص انتشار منشوراته لمصلحة خصمه. وتدخلت المحكمة الانتخابية العليا وألزمت الشركة بتقديم توضيحات، ونشرت صحيفة «فولها دي ساو باولو» مراسلات داخلية يقر فيها موظفون في الشركة بأن قيود المنصة أضرت بحسابات لولا، فيما تحدثت ميتا عن «أعطال تقنية». ورغم ذلك، حسمت التعبئة الجماهيرية جولة الإعادة لصالح لولا.

وفي ألمانيا، وظّف إيلون ماسك منصته «إكس» لدعم حزب «البديل من أجل ألمانيا» اليميني المتطرف قبيل انتخابات فبراير 2025، عبر مقالات التأييد وبثّ حوار مباشر مع زعيمته أليس فايدل، فيما رصدت دراسات انحياز خوارزميات المنصة لصالح محتوى الحزب. وفي كولومبيا، وبعد جولة إعادة حسمت لمرشح اليمين المتطرف بفارق نحو نقطة مئوية واحدة، اتهم الرئيس غوستافو بيترو شركة سايبر إسرائيلية بنشر نصف مليون حساب آلي زائف للتلاعب بالناخبين، وطعن في سلامة برمجيات الفرز وانحياز المنصات الرقمية لليمين المتطرف. ومهما انتهى إليه التحقيق، فإن انتقال الطعن في انتخابات بلد بأكمله إلى ميدان الخوارزميات والحسابات الآلية يكشف طبيعة المرحلة التي نعيشها.

أما المثال الأوضح فجاء من المحكمة الجنائية الدولية. فبعد أن أصدر قضاتها مذكرات توقيف بحق مسؤولين إسرائيليين بتهم ارتكاب جرائم حرب في غزة، فرضت الإدارة الأمريكية عقوبات على عدد من قضاتها ومسؤوليها، فأغلقت شركات أمريكية حساباتهم المصرفية والرقمية. وإذا كانت الرأسمالية مستعدة لفعل ذلك بمحكمة دولية تضم أكثر من مئة وعشرين دولة عضواً، فماذا ستفعل بمشروع يساري يصبح مؤثراً ويسعى إلى كسر هيمنتها، ويتجاوز الخطوط الحمراء التي رسمتها؟

وتمتد هذه الهيمنة إلى الحياة اليومية للناشطات والناشطين، عبر عقوبات رقمية تفرضها المنصات على من يفضح جرائم الحرب الإسرائيلية وانتهاكات دول أخرى، أو يطرح خطاباً يسارياً جذرياً. وتبدأ هذه العقوبات بالتضييق وتقليص الانتشار والتهميش، وتصل إلى حذف المحتوى وإغلاق الحسابات. وقد وثقت منظمات حقوق الإنسان الدولية هذه الممارسات وأدانتها، ومنها تقرير «هيومن رايتس ووتش» عن الرقابة الممنهجة على المحتوى الفلسطيني في منصات ميتا. ويدفع هذا القمع الرقمي كثيراً من الناشطات والناشطين إلى رقابة ذاتية طوعية، فيعدلون خطابهم ويتجنبون قضايا بعينها خوفاً من الحظر …

author: Unknown
title: We Have Fed You All for a Thousand Years
content:
Title

: We Have Fed You All for a Thousand Years

Subtitle

: Travels of a Protest Poem

Source

: KSL: Bulletin of the Kate Sharpley Library No. 122, October 2026


A Humble Reminder : To the Propertied Classes


 (Slightly altered from Rudyard Kipling’s Ode in praise of English Enterprise.)


 We have fed you all for a thousand years,

 And you hail us still unfed,

 Though there’s never a pound of all your pounds

 But marks the workers’ dead;

 We have yielded our best to give you rest,

 And you lie on a crimson wool,

 For if blood be the price of England’s wealth,

 Good God, we ha’ paid in full.


 There’s never a mine blown skyward now

 But we’re buried alive for you;

 There’s never a wreck drifts shoreward now

 But it’s we are the ghastly crew;

 Go, reckon our dead by the forges red,

 And the factories where we spin;

 If blood be the price of England’s wealth,

 Good God, we ha’ paid it in.


 We have fed you all for a thousand years,

 For that was our doom, you know,

 From the days when you chained us in your fields

 To the strike of a week ago;

 You have eaten our lives and our babes and wives,

 And we’re told it’s your legal share;

 But if blood be the price of England’s wealth,

 Good God, we ha’ bought it fair.


 N.


 


 In September 1893 the London anarchist newspaper

Freedom : A Journal of Anarchist Communism

 published a poem called ‘A Humble Reminder : To the Propertied Classes’, credited to ‘N.’

[1]

 It’s an anti-capitalist protest, lamenting the ‘workers’ dead’ whose deaths enriched those ‘propertied classes’. It rails at the rich ‘We have fed you all for a thousand years, / And you hail us still unfed’. I do not know who ‘N.’ was, though they seem to be connected to the

Freedom

 milieu.

Freedom

 had published another poem by them, ‘The Pet Voter’, in August 1892.

[2]

 Max Nettlau used the same initial when writing in

Freedom

 in June 1891; the Fabian socialist Edith Nesbit had a poem ‘A Word For The Children’ in

Freedom

 in February 1891 (‘The right to give help is your own, / The right to claim it theirs.’) Neither seems a convincing candidate for the authorship of this poem.


The Kipling connection


 ‘N.’ introduced their poem by saying it was ‘slightly altered from Rudyard Kipling’s Ode in praise of English Enterprise.’ That’s a reference to Kipling’s ‘Song of the Dead’ published four months earlier in

The English Illustrated Magazine

 (May 1893). ‘N.’s address to the propertied classes ‘For if blood be the price of England’s wealth, / Good God, we ha’ paid in full’ rewrites Kipling’s address to the sea ‘If blood be the price of admiralty, / Lord God, we ha’ paid in full!’.

[3]

 The ‘Humble Reminder’ changes Kipling’s poem – but leans heavily upon it. Mark Leier said ‘strictly speaking the poem is not a parody of Kipling’s poem but a re-working of the words based on the original verse and meter.’

[4]

 It reminds me of Utah Philips’ comment on IWW songmaking: ‘The Wobblies liked to steal the hymn tunes ‘cos they were pretty and change the words so they made more sense.’

[5]


 The connection to Kipling persisted. He was credited in many of the reprints (inevitable, perhaps, given that the author remained unknown and their debt to Kipling was clear). There were even articles discussing what it would mean if the poem were by Kipling.

[6]


Reprinted and recited


 Once printed, it was always possible for the poem to reappear, and this one spread beyond the anarchist press, becoming a standard of labour movement papers. The title often changed, varying from ‘The Cry of Toil’ to ‘The Capitalist’. Just as the connection to Kipling is sometimes there and sometimes not, the text varies between the poetic ‘ha’’ to the everyday ‘have’.


 Apparently a version was published in Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania in 1895.

[7]

 The Portland anarchist newspaper

The Firebrand

 reprinted the poem (anonymously) as ‘The Workers Outcry’ in 1897.

[8]

 Changes had been made to Americanise the text: instead of pounds the third line talks of ‘there’s never a dollar of all your wealth’.


 Sometimes you can read about the poem’s life off the printed page. In May 1897 Miss Olive Keep recited ‘We have fed you all for a thousand years’ at a gathering of the Socialist Labor Party.

[9]

. In August 1899,

The Carpenter

, a union journal for ‘Carpenters, Stair Builders, Machine Wood Workers, Planing Mill Men, and Kindred Interests’ reprinted the ‘Firebrand version’ (with credit) …

title: Anonym - Die Systeme der Organisation
content:
