Es drängt uns, eine Frage von eminenter Wichtigkeit und folgenschwerer Bedeutung unter das Secirmesser der Kritik zu bringen, die Organisationsfrage nämlich. Es ist dieser Gegenstand von weit grösserer Wichtigkeit und Tragweite, als es bei einer flüchtigen Betrachtung den Schein haben mag: denn die Organisation ist das wichtigste Werkzeug des obschwebenden geistigen Riesenkampfes, und ist von grosser Wichtigkeit, ob eben dieses Instrument scharf und spitzig oder schartig und stumpf ist: die Organisation kann aber auch, wenn sie tauglich geformt wird, zur wirksamen Triebkraft, zum zweckdienlichen Sauerteige für die künftige Kulturform werden, sowie andererseits zum Geiste, der beschworen wurde und sich nicht zähmen lässt, wie der von Goethe’s Zauberlehrling.

Dem Wesen nach unterscheiden wir zwei Systeme der Organisation, und zwar den Centralismus und den Föderalismus. Beide sollen nun untersucht werden.

Was zunächst den Centralismus anbelangt, so ist derselbe nichts Anderes wie ein misslungener Abklatsch des despotischen oder absoluten Regierungssystems und zeigt uns, dass nicht allein der Affe, sondern auch der Mensch den Nachahmungstrieb besitzt.

Die Despotie zeigt uns den Centralismus in seiner vollendetsten und ausgebildetsten Form.

Caligula und Nero, Philipp der Zweite von Spanien und Richard III. von England, sowie Ludwig XI. von Frankreich: sie Alle waren Centralisten, die unser Augenmerk fesseln, denn sie waren gross, wenn auch als Tyrannen, wenn auch im Schlechten, sie ragen über die Mittelmässigkeit hoch empor: sie waren Verbrecher an der Menschenwürde, aber sie waren es voll Kraft und Mut, voll Kühnheit und Energie. Was sind aber die Tyrännchen, die sich die Arbeiter durch den Centralismus erzeugen, indem sie sich von Mauldreschern bethören lassen? Erbärmliche Jammergestalten im Vergleiche mit jenen Titanen, deren Andenken glühenden Hass in unserer Seele weckt? Sie sind armselige Zwerge, Liliputaner, und thun wohl daran, sich spreizen und viel und laut von der Redner-Tribüne herunter zu deklamiren und zu kreischen, denn sonst würde man sie gar nicht wahrnehmen. Sie zu verachten, wäre zu viel Ehre für sie, nein, ein mitleidiges Bedauern ist Alles, was ihnen zugewendet werden kann. Sie sind der Vergessenheit geweiht und haben dereinst zwecklos gelebt: das alleinige Ziel ihres Strebens ist das Wohlleben, und dafür treten sie das Heiligste, Erhabenste, die himmlische, ewige Idee in den Kot: sie unterscheiden sich in nichts von einem Mastschwein, das auf nichts denkt wie auf vielen und guten Mais und einen trefflichen Stall, nur erstreben sie beides in einer anderen Form. Ärmliche, kleinliche Menschlein! – Und sie wären vielleicht fähig, ihr ephemeres Sein an die ewige unvergängliche Kette von Ursachen und Wirkungen, Grund und Folge zu knüpfen und ewig zu sein im Erlösungswerk der Menschheit durch ihr fruchtbringendes Wirken, sie wären vielleicht befähigt zu schaffen, so dass sie darin das reinste Glück, ein Gefühl von Seligkeit empfänden im Glücke und Paradieses-Sein Aller, dass sie für künftige Generationen anzubahnen helfen würden.

Der Centralismus vernichtet die individuelle Selbstständigkeit und Freiheit vollständig, wie wir es im despotischen Staat antreffen. Hier ist der Wille des Autokraten Gesetz, dort der Wille des Parteigötzen, den man auf das Piedestal emporhob: der Druck ist ärger noch als im despotischen Staat, denn in einem solchen soll nur eine gesetzwidrige Handlung gerichtet werden; die Spitze der centralistischen Pyramide aber richtet nicht allein die Handlungen, sondern sogar die Meinungen, sie erforscht Herz und Nieren der Menschen wie Jehova, und es sollte auch der Wille solcher Parteigötzen unter Donner und Blitz zeitweilig verkündet werden, wenigstens hätte das Colophonium stärkeren Absatz und die Spängler fänden bei der Anfertigung von Donnerblechen vielleicht lohnende Arbeit.

Treffend bezeichnet ein Engländer den Centralismus, indem er sagt: “Stelle ein Schaf vor die andern und Du hast die Herde fertig.” Ja wohl, eine Herde ist es und weiter nichts, und diese Herde geht hin, wohin der Hammel sie führt, und wenn er in einen Sumpf hineinplumpst, so wandern Alle in den Morast, und thatsächlich stecken gegenwärtig die Bekenner der alleinseligmachenden Sozialdemokratie mit ihrer achtundvierziger Theorie im Schlamme der Reformpolitik und leiden an …

author: Berliner Bündnis gegen Waffenproduktion
title: Demo: Kamikazedrohnen ausm Wedding? Rheinmetall stoppen!
content:
Seit Monaten baut Rheinmetall das ehemalige Pierburg-Werk beim Humboldt­hain, in dem bislang Autoteile produziert wurden, auf Rüstungsproduktion um.


Wie Rheinmetall verkündete, läuft am Berliner Standort bereits jetzt die serielle Produktion von Gefechtsköpfen für sogenannte »Loitering Munition« – auch Kamikazedrohnen genannt. Ab 2027 sollen im Weddinger Werk zudem jährlich rund 120.000 Geschossmäntel für 155-Millimeter-Artilleriemunition hergestellt werden. Diese Stahlmäntel sind 42 Kilogramm schwer und 80 Zentimeter lang. Bei Detonation zerspringt der Stahlkörper in 13.000 tödliche Splitter.


Was bringt uns das? Krieg und unermessliches Leid. Was bringt es Rheinmetall? Unermesslichen Profit! Die Waffen von Rheinmetall töten in aller Welt: in Palästina, in Kurdistan, im Jemen. Während die Gewinne des Konzerns wachsen, erleben Beschäftigte in der Rüstungs- und Automobilindustrie Druck, Umstrukturierungen und Unsicherheit.


Aufrüstung hat uns nie vor Kriegen und ihren elenden Folgen bewahrt – ganz im Gegenteil. Kriege nützen den Reichen, wir liefern die Leichen. Wenn wir Frieden wollen, müssen wir den Kapitalismus überwinden und eine solidarische Welt aufbauen.


Die Gruppe Peacefully against Genocide ruft vom 15. bis 22. November erneut zu einer Aktionswoche gegen Rheinmetall im Wedding auf. Schließen wir uns an!

author: Qassam Muaddi
title: Palestinian Opinions Are Divided as Elections Are Now Postponed Until 2027
content:
Although some in Gaza welcomed the prospect of elections, many are looking for solutions to more urgent problems.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

On October 10, Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas issued a presidential decree postponing the legislative and presidential elections from November 2026, the original scheduled date, until September 2027.

Amid obstacles imposed by the Israeli occupation, the postponement was justified by a need to create appropriate political, security, and on-the-ground conditions for free, fair, and inclusive elections.

According to the official Palestinian news agency WAFA, the decree aims to allow for comprehensive national dialogue to strengthen Palestinian unity, preserve Palestinian territory, safeguard the political system, address challenges that the electoral process is facing, and ensure the participation of Palestinians in Jerusalem, the West Bank, and the Gaza Strip while protecting their political and constitutional rights.

While some expected the postponement, in light of the cancellation of Palestinian elections in 2021, it nevertheless came as a surprise to observers.

In the Gaza Strip, reactions to the decision have been divided. Some consider it to be in the national interest, arguing that the current conditions in Gaza do not permit elections. Others believe that postponing the vote, after more than 20 years without elections, undermines the national democratic process and marginalizes the role of Gaza’s residents in determining their political future.

Fadi al-Sheikh Youssef, head of a youth-led electoral list that had been preparing to contest the elections, described the postponement as an unjust and direct denial of the Palestinian people’s democratic right.

“The elections should have continued after nearly 20 years of freezing the democratic process in Palestine,” he said. “If the Israeli occupation has imposed obstacles, the elections should have become a political battle fought by all parties against the occupation. This electoral process should have been a new opportunity to expose the occupation to the world and reveal the falsity of its claims about democratic practices and its supposed respect for freedom of expression and Palestinians’ right to political participation.”

He added that the postponement appeared to reflect an agreement among political parties to reproduce the same political landscape.

“Unfortunately, we see this postponement as part of an effort by the parties to recreate the same political scene. Even the justification of national consensus does not reflect the real wishes of the Palestinian people. If there had truly been national consensus, it should have been achieved over the past 20 years, not now, as the political landscape is being reshaped through a democratic process,” he said.

Al-Sheikh Youssef described the decision as deeply unjust and ill-suited to the current political landscape, arguing that it excluded new groups and political actors seeking to enter the arena and defend what remains of people’s dignity.

In a statement, Hamas said it viewed the decision to postpone the elections until next year as a step in the right direction, given the absence of the political, security, and on-the-ground conditions necessary for free and fair elections throughout the occupied Palestinian territories, including Jerusalem.

Hamas said the postponement should lead to comprehensive, serious and productive national dialogue. It also expressed its readiness to participate in discussions aimed at reaching clear and binding agreements for all parties, including mechanisms to reorganize Palestinian political institutions, particularly the Palestinian National Council and the Palestinian Legislative Council.

Furthermore, some Palestinian political analysts and academics offered a broader assessment of the political calculations behind the postponement and its potential consequences for the Palestinian political system.

Political analyst Adel Shadid told Mondoweiss that “despite the Palestinian demands and European pressure on the Palestinian Authority to hold elections, the PA are afraid of elections, because they know its officials know that there are real possibilities of losing, and despite that, I was surprised by the postponement of elections.”

title: Ücret artışı olmadan daha uzun çalışma dayatan Mercedes-Benz, Almanya'da yeni yatırımları durdurdu
content:
Mercedes-Benz, iş gücü maliyetlerini düşürmek için işçi temsilcileriyle yürüttüğü görüşmelerde ilerleme sağlanamaması üzerine Almanya’daki tesislerine yönelik yeni yatırımları durdurdu. Şirket yönetiminin, ülkedeki bazı fabrikaların kapatılmasını da değerlendirdiği belirtildi. İnsan Kaynakları Direktörü Britta Seeger, Reuters’ın gördüğü şirket içi söyleşide yakın zamanda anlaşma beklemediklerini ve hangi tesislerin mevcut maliyetlerle işletilebileceğini incelemeye başladıklarını söyledi.

Görüşmelerde haftalık çalışma süresinin ücret artışı olmadan 35 saatten 40 saate çıkarılması gündeme geldi. Yönetim ayrıca kâr payı, tatil ve Noel ödemeleri gibi ek ödemeleri de görüşmeye açmak istiyor. Çalışan temsilcileri ve IG Metall sendikası ise 35 saatlik çalışma haftasını temel bir kazanım olarak görüyor ve bu dayatmaları reddediyor.

Üretim Direktörü Michael Schiebe, maliyetler düşürülemezse Almanya’da bir otomobil montaj fabrikası ile bir parça üretim tesisinin kapanabileceğini daha önce belirtmişti. Şirketin Sindelfingen, Rastatt ve Bremen’de montaj fabrikaları bulunuyor. Schiebe, anlaşma sağlanamazsa yeni modellerin yalnızca yurt dışında üretileceğini söyledi.

Schiebe’ye göre Almanya’daki üretim tesislerinde saatlik iş gücü maliyeti, bazı durumlarda Doğu Avrupa’daki tesislerin beş katına ulaşıyor. Macaristan’daki fabrikasını genişleten şirket, gümrük vergilerini, zayıflayan talebi, fiyat baskısını ve özellikle Çinli üreticilerin rekabetini de gerekçe gösteriyor. Mercedes-Benz’in binek otomobil biriminin satış kârlılığı ocak-eylül döneminde yüzde 3,3’e geriledi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Jillian Kestler-D’Amours
title: Refugee Groups Sue to Stop Canada From Handing Over Asylum Seekers to ICE
content:
The lawsuit says handing asylum seekers over to the abuse-perpetrating US is a violation of Canada’s constitution.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Canada is violating its own constitution by turning asylum seekers away at the border with the United States, where they face serious threats under U.S. President Donald Trump, Canadian legal experts and rights advocates say.

Amnesty International Canada, the Canadian Council for Refugees, and the Canadian Council of Churches are in court this week to challenge a decades-old pact that allows Canadian officials to summarily send most refugees back at the U.S. border.

People rallied in Toronto and Montreal, the two largest cities in Canada, on Monday to show support for the case and call on the Canadian government to rip up the Safe Third Country Agreement (STCA).

In Montreal, dozens of protesters held posters that read, “Canada must protect, not send back” and “Humanity has no borders.”

“If Canadians don’t feel safe in the United States, we can be sure that refugees aren’t safe either,” Lauren Lallemand, co-executive director of the Canadian Council for Refugees, told the crowd.

“The asylum system in the U.S. is failing, and those who flee in search of safety deserve to be protected.”

The Safe Third Country Agreement, which came into force in 2004, is premised on the idea that Canada and the U.S. each offer people access to a robust refugee protection system.

In practice, it means that asylum seekers can seek protection in the first country they arrive in, but not both: someone in the U.S. cannot apply for asylum in Canada, or vice versa.

For years, the restriction applied to asylum claims made at official crossings along the border.

But if people entered Canada irregularly between ports of entry (via farmers’ fields or rural roads, for example), they could circumvent the pact — and as Trump began to crack down on immigration during his first term, tens of thousands of people made dangerous crossings into Canada to request protection.

In 2023, amid public and political pressure to crack down on immigration, Prime Minister Justin Trudeau and President Joe Biden closed the loophole, extending the Safe Third Country Agreement to the entire 5,525-mile border.

Now, only people who meet specific conditions — such as unaccompanied minors or individuals with relatives who are already in Canada — are exempt from being turned away under the Safe Third Country Agreement.

The lawsuit being heard in Federal Court in Toronto this week argues that the Safe Third Country Agreement violates equality rights under Section 15 of Canada’s constitution, known as the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms.

According to the complainants, that’s because the pact disproportionately harms racialized asylum seekers, including women fleeing gender-based violence, children, and members of the LGBTQ+ community.

Julia Sande, a lawyer at Amnesty International Canada, explained that Section 15 applies to everyone who is physically in the country, including refugee claimants.

“Canada cannot deport people to face torture, harm [and] persecution in another country,” she said. “It would be a violation of their Charter rights, even if it’s another country doing the harm, because it’s Canada’s decision to send them out … [and] to put them in [harm’s way] when harm is reasonably foreseeable.”

While conditions for asylum seekers and refugees in the U.S. have been concerning for a long time, Sande said the situation has deteriorated dramatically under the administration of U.S. President Donald Trump.

She pointed to the expansion of immigration detention as one example. “Things are obviously extremely urgent and extremely harmful,” she said.

“We all act in horror at what’s unfolding in the United States. You hear Canadian citizens talking about being afraid to go there, being afraid of ICE.”

“We all act in horror at what’s unfolding in the United States. You hear Canadian citizens talking about being afraid to go there, being afraid of ICE,” she told Truthout.

“I have a hard time believing that you could find anyone here who would say, ‘Yeah I’d really like my government to hand a child over to ICE to be thrown in detention … and ultimately sent back to a country where they fled gang violence.’”

author: The Canadian Press
title: Shelter-in-place advisory issued near Squamish, B.C., due to flooding from heavy rain
content:
A shelter-in-place advisory has been issued north of Vancouver, where roads have flooded due to dam run-off triggered by storms that have drenched parts of southern British Columbia with more than 300 millimetres of rain in 48 hours.


The rains that are forecast to ease Thursday before a weaker system arrives Friday have also forced evacuation orders for parts of Vancouver Island, the Lil’wat First Nation in the central Interior, and parts of the Village of Pemberton, about 150 kilometres north of Vancouver.


The entire Village of Pemberton is under an evacuation alert, while the District of Squamish about 90 kilometres to the south has told residents of Paradise Valley to shelter in place after dam discharge swamped local roads.


British Columbia’s emergency information system says residents in areas including Sunwolf Lodge and Cheekye Ranch should stay indoors if they can.


The District of Squamish says in a statement that the spill level from the Cheakamus Dam at Daisy Lake peaked at approximately 5 a.m. and was expected to decrease slowly throughout the day.


The district says the spill level decrease was to create room in the reservoir for another upcoming storm, as well as to eventually allow for roads to be re-opened.


It says a rainfall warning ended this morning and that heavy rain is no longer expected through Friday.


It also says river levels are expected to peak Thursday and begin to drop as rainfall from the storm works its way through the river system.


A string of weather systems has slammed southwestern B.C since last week, with 306 millimetres of rain falling at Port Mellon in the Howe Sound region since Tuesday.


The Village of Pemberton’s evacuation order covers properties on Airport Road, including the community’s airport, wastewater treatment facility, wildland fire management base and a public golf course due to flooding and “high-risk river levels.”


The B.C. Ministry of Transportation’s DriveBC website says Highway 99 east of Pemberton has been shut in both directions.


The Lilʼwat Nation has also expanded an evacuation order and alert for the area from Kwetsa7 along the Lillooet River corridor to Lillooet Lake.


Elsewhere, the Strathcona Regional District issued a water conservation notice for the village of Sayward on the northeast coast of Vancouver Island, as high flows in Newcastle Creek led to extra sediment in the water.


An evacuation order due to flooding and landslide risks remains in place for about 30 properties in the village of Zeballos on northwest Vancouver Island.


While rains have eased in parts of the province including Metro Vancouver, orange rainfall warnings remain in place for west and inland Vancouver Island, indicating severe storms that are likely to cause significant damage and disruption.


“A strong frontal system over the area will weaken today. Rain will continue to ease as the front weakens,” Environment Canada said Thursday.


A less-severe yellow rainfall warning is active for the Sunshine Coast and parts of east Vancouver Island.


Environment Canada says several locations reported more than 100 millimetres of rain in the last 48 hours, including Kennedy Lake on Vancouver Island (248 mm), Port Alberni (123 mm), Porteau Cove on the Sea to Sky Highway (140 mm), Whistler (138 mm), and Squamish (134 mm).

title: Democratic Party Factions Are Competing to Define What Is Possible Right Now
content:
David Sirota points out that a billionaire-backed group is now convening in Denver to try to sculpt the party’s agenda.

author: Doug Bock Clark
title: A Tool Built by Election Deniers Said These Voters Were Dead — They Aren’t
content:
After the midterm, a GOP election board member in Georgia challenged dozens of ballots using a controversial data tool.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Ahead of the midterms, conservative election activists discussed plans to wield a powerful new weapon in the war against fraud: a data tool built by one of their own that could identify suspicious voters and help with contesting their ballots.

The system was put to the test this week in Forsyth County, Georgia, where a member of the county’s election board provided other officials with what he suggested was evidence of wrongdoing: four allegedly dead voters.

But it turns out all four are alive and well, ProPublica determined. The board rejected the attempt to challenge their ballots.

The effort, though, shows that even after last week’s blue wave, those who believe the 2020 election was stolen have continued to relentlessly search for ways to contest Republican losses. In Georgia, Democrats swept statewide offices.

The board member who initiated the Forsyth County challenge, Max Clavijo, is a member of the Election Integrity Network, a group led by conservative lawyer Cleta Mitchell that works to restrict voting and tighten election laws and rules. Mitchell worked closely with Donald Trump in his attempt to overturn his defeat in the 2020 election and, since he retook the presidency, has been central to his push to assert greater federal control over voting.

In the run-up to the midterms, on right-wing media and on private organizing calls, EIN participants outlined plans to search voter rolls with a software tool known as ELLY’s Election Monitor and contest ballots the tool deemed suspicious.

ELLY was developed by EIN member Rick Richards. It aggregates public data from state voter files, federal change-of-address records, tax documents, obituaries, property websites like Zillow and other sources. In Georgia, State Election Board members and top staffers have urged counties to use the tool to search their voter rolls for signs of fraud.

Richards talked about ELLY’s national potential on a podcast in late September, on which right-wing media personalities and activists touted its capacity to help GOP candidates contest their defeats. “We can prove the fraud that’s gone on in every state,” one commentator said. “This data will be able to set up challenges to those who lose.”

The following month, on a private call with EIN members and other conservative activists, Richards promised to provide data from more than 3,000 counties to “citizen monitors” and GOP candidates to try to prove fraud, according to a recording reviewed by ProPublica.

In an interview, Richards told ProPublica that he gave Clavijo data on Forsyth County at Clavijo’s request. He said in a subsequent email that their actions were meant to inform the board and remain confidential. Clavijo didn’t respond to questions from ProPublica.

Richards refused to answer questions about whether Clavijo’s effort was part of a wider EIN campaign to contest votes cast in the midterms.

“That’s irrelevant,” he said. “The data is the data. People can use it for what they want to.”

Mitchell, EIN’s leader, didn’t respond to questions about the group’s plans related to ELLY, either in Georgia or nationally.

In the months since some on Georgia’s State Election Board started promoting ELLY’s use, its accuracy has been much debated. The tool doesn’t have access to personal identifiers such as voters’ Social Security or driver’s license numbers or full dates of birth, which increases the potential for mismatches involving people with the same names.

Voting rights groups have called ELLY error-prone. The Cherokee County election director complained to the state board after the tool falsely flagged a county board member’s spouse as dead.

State Election Board members and Richards have defended ELLY. Accusations that the data is unreliable were “horse hockey,” Richards told ProPublica, explaining this was “a Southern colloquialism for B.S.”

Late last week, according to several people familiar with the matter, Clavijo circulated documents to board members and Forsyth County’s election director. Based on data from ELLY, Clavijo questioned whether the names of more than 22,000 people on the county’s voter roll were correct and disputed the eligibility of 69 voters. In addition to four he claimed were deceased, he alleged others had moved out of the …

title: CHP seçmeni AKP'ye MHP seçmeninden çok güveniyor
content: Yöneylem Sosyal Araştırmalar Merkezi’nin Türkiye Siyaset Paneli Ekim 2026 araştırması, seçmenlerin fon krizine yaklaşımını, ülke yönetimine ilişkin değerlendirmelerini ve oy tercihlerindeki değişimi ortaya koydu. Araştırma, 21–28 Ekim 2026 tarihlerinde 81 il ve 12 istatistiki bölgede 2 bin 400 panelistle bilgisayar destekli telefon görüşmesi (CATI) yöntemiyle gerçekleştirildi. Yöneylem, araştırmanın Türkiye geneli sonuçları için yüzde 95 güven düzeyinde hata payını ±2 yüzde puan olarak açıkladı.Bulgular, bazı AKP’li siyasetçilerin fon krizinden haksız kazanç sağladığı iddialarını inandırıcı bulanların, AKP ve MHP seçmenleri arasında da önemli bir kesim oluşturduğunu gösteriyor. Araştırmaya katılanların yüzde 50,6’sı fon kriziyle ilgili gelişmeleri “yakından”, yüzde 24,7’si “biraz” takip ettiğini belirtti. Böylece gelişmeleri takip edenlerin toplamı yüzde 75,3 oldu. Katılımcıların yüzde 12,6’sı krizi hiç duymadığını, yüzde 11,6’sı ise yalnızca duyduğunu söyledi. Yüzde 0,5’lik kesim soruyu yanıtsız bıraktı. Fon krizini takip etme oranı parti tercihlerine göre farklılaştı. Gelişmeleri biraz veya yakından takip edenlerin toplamı İYİ Parti seçmenlerinde yüzde 95,9, Yeni Parti seçmenlerinde yüzde 91,3, MHP seçmenlerinde yüzde 86,8 ve DEM Parti seçmenlerinde yüzde 86,3 olarak ölçüldü. Aynı oran AKP seçmenlerinde yüzde 59,2, CHP seçmenlerinde yüzde 57 oldu Bazı AKP’li siyasetçilerin fon krizinden haksız kazanç sağladığı iddialarını katılımcıların yüzde 45,4’ü “çok inandırıcı”, yüzde 26,4’ü “inandırıcı” buldu. İddiaları inandırıcı bulanların toplamı yüzde 71,8’e ulaşırken, yüzde 9,6’lık kesim “pek inandırıcı değil” veya “hiç inandırıcı değil” yanıtını verdi. Katılımcıların yüzde 9’u değerlendirme yapacak kadar bilgisi olmadığını belirtti. Söz konusu iddiaları inandırıcı veya çok inandırıcı bulanların oranı AKP seçmenlerinde yüzde 47,6, MHP seçmenlerinde yüzde 74,6 oldu. Bu oran Yeni Parti seçmenlerinde yüzde 90,7, İYİ Parti seçmenlerinde yüzde 91 ve DEM Parti seçmenlerinde yüzde 88,5 olarak kaydedildi. CHP seçmenlerinde ise yüzde 62,4’te kaldı. Değerlendirme yapacak kadar bilgisi olmadığını söyleyenlerin oranı CHP seçmenlerinde yüzde 16,5, AKP seçmenlerinde yüzde 14,5 olarak ölçüldü. “Sizce Türkiye nasıl yönetilmektedir?” sorusuna katılımcıların yüzde 55,7’si “kötü yönetilmektedir” yanıtını verdi. Ülkenin iyi yönetildiğini düşünenlerin oranı yüzde 21,5 olurken, yüzde 21,8’lik kesim “ne iyi ne kötü yönetilmektedir” seçeneğini işaretledi. Katılımcıların yüzde 1’i ise bilmediğini belirtti. Türkiye’nin iyi yönetildiğini söyleyenlerin oranı AKP seçmenlerinde yüzde 65, MHP seçmenlerinde yüzde 49,6 oldu. Kötü yönetildiğini düşünenlerin oranı ise Yeni Parti seçmenlerinde yüzde 89,2, İYİ Parti seçmenlerinde yüzde 87,8, DEM Parti seçmenlerinde yüzde 87,1 ve CHP seçmenlerinde yüzde 73,6’ya ulaştı. AKP seçmenlerinin yüzde 8,3’ü ve MHP seçmenlerinin yüzde 10,7’si de ülkenin kötü yönetildiğini belirtti. Katılımcıların yüzde 16’sı son bir ayda oy vermeyi düşündüğü partiyi değiştirdiğini, yüzde 83,2’si ise tercihinin değişmediğini söyledi. Tercihini değiştirenlerin yüzde 31,1’i önceki ay AKP’ye, yüzde 26,1’i CHP’ye, yüzde 7,6’sı Yeni Parti’ye ve yüzde 6,7’si MHP’ye oy vermeyi düşündüğünü belirtti. Bu dağılım, tercih değiştiren grubun önceki yönelimini gösteriyor; partilerin kendi seçmenleri içindeki kayıp oranlarını veya net oy değişimini ortaya koymuyor. Oy tercihini değiştirme gerekçelerinde “ekonomi, geçim ve istihdam” yüzde 21,5 ile ilk sırada yer aldı. Bunu yüzde 11,7 ile “yolsuzluk, fon krizi ve usulsüzlük”, yüzde 10,3 ile “parti içi gelişmeler, liderlik ve kayyım”, yüzde 9,1 ile “parti politikaları, söylemler ve tutumlar” izledi. Fon krizi diğer iki konuyla aynı başlıkta değerlendirildiği için, yalnızca bu krizin tercih değişimindeki payı verilerden ayrıştırılamıyor. Hane içindeki siyasi tercihlere ilişkin soruda katılımcıların yüzde 57,9’u herkesin aynı partiye oy vermeyi düşündüğünü söyledi. Yüzde 16,6’sı hanede farklı partileri tercih edenlerin bulunduğunu, yüzde 3,6’sı ise tercihi belli olanların yanında kararsız veya oy kullanmayı düşünmeyen kişilerin de yaşadığını belirtti. Hanedeki hiç kimsenin tercihinin belli olmadığını söyleyenlerin oranı yüzde 8,7, hiçbirinin oy kullanmayı düşünmediğini belirtenlerin oranı yüzde 5,5 oldu. Yüzde 7,7’lik kesim diğer hane üyelerinin tercihini bilmediğini söyledi. İkinci parti tercihleri, Yeni Parti’nin farklı muhalefet partilerinin seçmenleri arasında alternatif olarak görüldüğüne işaret etti …

author: Daron Letts
title: Nunavut earns second-highest score from leading credit rating agency
content:
The Government of Nunavut received the second-highest possible credit score from Moody’s Ratings, a leading New York-based international credit rating agency.


The Aa1 rating was granted because the Canadian government financially backs the territory, according to the company’s report.


“This rating is an important milestone for Nunavut and reflects the strength of our financial position,” said Premier John Main, who is also finance minister, in a news release issued Monday.

“It recognizes our government’s responsible financial management and the stability provided by our relationship with the Government of Canada.”


The company’s ratings system ranges from Aaa, the highest, to C, the lowest. 


Although Nunavut’s own-source revenue was only 17 per cent of total revenue in 2025-26, reflecting a narrow tax base due to its small population, the report concluded that there is “a high likelihood that the Government of Canada would provide extraordinary support should Nunavut face acute liquidity stress.”


Federal transfers account for approximately 80 per cent of the territory’s revenue, which bridges the gap between high expenditure needs and limited revenue capacity, the report states.


From 2018 through 2025, the government’s annual credit ratings were provided by Chicago-based DBRS Morningstar.


In 2025, that agency awarded the territory a rating of “AA stable trend,” which was an upgrade from the 2024 rating of “AA (low) stable trend.”


Both those scores fall within the second-highest level of the company’s rating structure.


Prior to that, Nunavut maintained an Aa1 rating from Moody’s Ratings from 2012 through 2017, according to the Moody’s Ratings website.

author: Chris Walker
title: House Democrats Vow to Investigate White House Despite Trump Admin Threats
content:
The counsel to the president claimed that recent statements by Democrats “may cross the line into blatant criminality.”

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

The White House has sent a threatening letter to House Democrats, warning that lawmakers could face repercussions if they open investigations into the Trump administration once they take control of Congress.

The letter, sent by Will Scharf in his official role as counsel to the president, was delivered just days after President Donald Trump demanded investigations into Democrats who stated that they were planning inquiries into the administration in the wake of the “blue wave” in this month’s midterm elections. Trump falsely called those statements “illegal” and “criminal.”

Scharf’s letter, first revealed by Punchbowl News, was sent to Rep. Robert Garcia (D-California) on Monday, according to the date on the letter, though the House Oversight Committee said midweek that it had not yet received an actual copy of the document. Garcia, currently the ranking member of the committee, is likely to become its chair after Democrats take control of the House in January.

Citing several Election Night social media posts by Democrats — including comments from Garcia urging the administration to “lawyer up” — Scharf claimed that there are “foundational” constitutional limits “on congressional investigations and subpoenas,” and accused incoming Democrats of having personal reasons for planning inquiries into the White House.

“We are monitoring the abusive and capricious threats that are now proliferating from Democrat legislators who seek to abuse the legislative process to intimidate and to interfere with the lawful functioning of government,” Scharf said.

The comments by Democrats “may cross the line into blatant criminality,” Scharf added, though he provided no basis for that claim.

The letter is highly unusual — while past presidents have criticized subpoenas and inquiries into their actions, the ability of the House Oversight Committee to conduct such investigations has long been considered a basic function of its work, and Supreme Court precedent has protected those powers. The statements by both Scharf and Trump are also hypocritical, given that Trump’s predecessor, former President Joe Biden, faced investigations by Republicans into his executive branch actions, including into his family members.

Garcia suggested that the letter indicates the administration has “something to hide.” He added:

The Trump administration continues to weaponize the government with threats of unconstitutional attacks on Congress. … [We] will not be deterred by baseless threats from a weaponized DOJ or from the president’s lawyers.

House Democratic leader Rep. Hakeem Jeffries (D-New York), who is poised to become the next Speaker of the House, also criticized Scharf’s letter, describing it as “outrageous” and “factually inaccurate…in terms of the Constitution.”

Peter M. Shane, constitutional legal scholar and adjunct professor at NYU School of Law, agreed that the letter contained false claims about the limits of congressional oversight.

“Our Constitution protects legislators from the threat of criminal prosecution while performing official duties as an essential bulwark to repel executive overreach and defend checks and balances,” Shane told The New York Times. “Congressional oversight and the issuance of subpoenas by definition cannot be the focus of legitimate criminal prosecution. It may be that an occasional subpoena may be quashed as outside the committee’s jurisdiction or for some other reason, but that is not a criminal offense.”

Donations are down for Truthout at a time when media is under immense pressure. Google’s AI search has driven our traffic down by 15 percent, Trump is arresting journalists, and many independent media organizations face heartbreaking cutbacks and closures.

At the same time, movement media is vital in the fight against Trump’s authoritarian reign. Our mandate to tell the truth, share strategies for resistance, and speak against fascism is ever more urgent in this deluge of political censorship and misinformation. Yet, we are struggling to meet our publishing costs when our work is so urgently needed.

We are fundraising right now for those basic operating expenses — we need $44,000 in the next 7 days. If you can support Truthout …

title: Ayşe Berktay: Women's direct participation is essential to peace
content:
Writer Ayşe Berktay, who participated in peace initiatives organized by women during previous resolution processes and met with women in many cities, spoke to ANF about the Peace and Democratic Society Process and the role women should play in it.


Ayşe Berktay recalled the work carried out by women's movements during the 2013–2015 resolution process, stressing that women should not merely support peace but must also be directly involved in decision-making mechanisms.


Ayşe Berktay emphasized the importance of building social support for peace, stating that the process cannot be reduced to negotiations between political actors. She stressed that the Kurdish freedom movement, particularly women, would not allow such an approach and said that women's organized will must be brought to the forefront to achieve a democratic solution.


'Women must participate as decision-makers at every stage of peace processes'


Ayşe Berktay stated that the 2013–2015 resolution process did not begin suddenly and should be understood as part of the search for a political solution to the Kurdish question that emerged in 2009.


She said that efforts to achieve peace could be traced further back to 2005 and even 1993, highlighting the importance of joint work between the Kurdish women's movement and feminist and socialist women from Turkey.


Ayşe Berktay said: "It is both possible and necessary to trace the process that emerged in July 2009 under the name 'Democratic Opening' further back to 2005 and, when viewed as a whole, as far back as 1993.


In the years around 2009, as the possibility of peace began to be felt, both the Kurdish women's movement and socialist and feminist women's movements in Turkey began coming together, holding discussions and organizing in solidarity against repression to spread the message, aspiration and language of peace.


The Democratic Free Women's Movement (DÖKH) inviting a large group of women to Amed (Diyarbakır) for discussions was critical in this regard. Ankara followed, then Berçelan-Taksim and the Peace Points. The Women's Initiative for Peace (BIKG) emerged from these joint efforts.


The Democratic Free Women's Movement was important in establishing a more structured platform for feminist and socialist women to meet, discuss, build relationships and work together.


These preparations formed the foundation and background for the activities carried out during the 2013–2015 process. Women examined peace experiences around the world and shared their findings with the public. The relationship between violence against women, militarism and war was addressed.


The need for women to participate as equal decision-makers at every stage of the peace process was constantly kept on the agenda. Women established various commissions and produced reports, activities and materials concerning different aspects of the process.


Following the Paris Massacre, there was a powerful collective commitment both to Sara, Rojbîn and Ronahî (Sakine Cansız, Fidan Doğan and Leyla Şaylemez, the three Kurdish women activists assassinated in Paris on 9 January 2013) and, through them, to the resolution process itself.”


'The importance of women's work became evident a decade ago'


Ayşe Berktay recalled that a woman representing the Kurdish women's movement joined the delegation when visits to Imralı began. She also stated that women from Turkey established the Women's Freedom Assembly (KÖM) to develop their collective voice and will.


Ayşe Berktay said that women's organizations prepared reports on the peace process through the commissions they established and carried out activities in different cities.


She said: "Efforts were made to establish an organized structure capable of bringing women's collective will to the negotiating table through commissions and reports. Throughout this process, both the Women's Initiative for Peace and the Women's Freedom Assembly worked tirelessly.


Women carried out work through monitoring commissions and truth commissions in Lice, Varto, Dersim, Suruç and along the Kobanê border. The importance and urgency of expanding this work became evident."


'

Women must participate in decision-making mechanisms'


Ayşe Berktay stated that raising the demand for peace and supporting the process were important but insufficient on their own. She stressed that women must participate directly in discussions about how peace will be built and in the mechanisms where decisions are made.

title: “Shared Stories, Free Cinema”: 6th Rojava Film Festival opens on Friday
content:
The 6th International Rojava Film Festival will open on Friday, November 13, with the screening of “Heval Kekê Min” by Haşim Aydemir. Under the theme “Çîrokên Hevpar, Sînemaya Azad” (Shared Stories, Free Cinema), the festival will bring filmmakers from various countries together with audiences in Rojava through November 20. Alongside feature films and documentaries, the program includes discussions on the social significance of cinema, collective filmmaking and the conditions for independent cultural production.


The main venue will be the Mihemed Şêxo Center in Qamişlo, where the film screenings will take place. Workshops, expert discussions and panel discussions will be held at the TEV-ÇAND, Sine Jin and Hunergeha Welat cultural centers. A special focus will be the “Ji Rojava” (From Rojava) section, featuring five productions from the region. The program will also include Kurdish-language short films, international feature films and documentaries.


Opening with music, dance and “Heval Kekê Min”


Friday’s opening ceremony will begin at 5:00 p.m. at the Mihemed Şêxo Center. MA Music will provide the musical program, while Narin Dance will present a dance performance. At 7:00 p.m., the opening film “Heval Kekê Min,” directed by Haşim Aydemir, will be screened.


The accompanying program of professional events will begin on Saturday, November 14. From 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. at Sine Jin, documentary filmmaker and editor Sasha Ayoub will introduce the work of Stories Film Lab. The program supports independent filmmakers in Syria in developing their projects. Films produced through the lab will also be screened during the event.


Film screenings will begin at 11:00 a.m. with “The Country Judge.” Other selections include the Kurdish-language short films “House of the Moon” and “Dorpêç,” as well as the documentary “The Wedding of the Pirs.”


From 3:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. at TEV-ÇAND, cinematographer Cemil Kızıldağ will lead a workshop on the visual language of cinema. The session will explore the creative possibilities of visual composition and cinematic storytelling.


Filmmaking practice and stories from Rojava


On Sunday, November 15, two multi-day workshops will begin. Cinematographer and lighting designer Jafar Amin Al-Betar will provide theoretical foundations and practical training in film lighting at Hunergeha Welat from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. The workshop will continue on November 16 and 17. Meanwhile, documentary filmmaker Guevara Namer will lead a workshop at Sine Jin focusing on the documentary filmmaking process and her experiences in international film production. The second part of her workshop will take place on November 16.


The “Ji Rojava” section will also begin that day. “Rêwiyên Ser Riya Agir” will be screened at 11:00 a.m., followed by “Keziyên Berxwedanê” at 11:50 a.m.


At 3:00 p.m., director Sêvînaz Evdikê, known for her film “Berbû,” will introduce the Nûjîyan Women’s Film Festival at TEV-ÇAND. At the same time, the documentary “Kî me ez?” will be screened at the Mihemed Şêxo Center.


The evening program will feature two more documentaries: “04.17 Adıyaman” at 6:00 p.m., followed by “Pêlên Kurdan” at 7:10 p.m. Both screenings will be followed by discussions with the audience.


Ten years of collective filmmaking in Rojava


On Monday, November 16, the experiences of the Rojava Film Commune will take center stage alongside the film screenings. “To Fetch a Pail of Water” will be screened at 11:00 a.m., followed by the documentary “Under the Flags the Sun” at 3:00 p.m.


From 3:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m., a panel discussion on the collective filmmaking practices of the Rojava Film Commune will take place at TEV-ÇAND. Since its establishment in 2015, the commune has been developing collectively organized approaches to filmmaking.


Moderated by Mirzan Bekir, the discussion will bring together founding members Diyar Hesso and Şêro Hindê and sound designer Coni Docolomansky, who worked on the films “Kobanê” and “Berbû.” The discussion will focus on experiences with collective production processes and the development of an independent filmmaking practice in Rojava.


Screenwriting and the Kurdish Question in Cinema


On Tuesday, November 17, screenwriter Önder Çakar will lead a workshop on developing film protagonists at Sine Jin from 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. The workshop will explore the process of developing a character from an initial concept to its full realization in a screenplay.

author: Unknown
title: Shengal People’s Council calls for the recognition of the will of Yazidi society
content:
On the 11th anniversary of the liberation of the Yazidi region from the terrorist organization Islamic State (ISIS), the Shengal People’s Council called for the recognition of the will of Shengal and the Yazidi community.


In a statement on Thursday, the council recalled the resistance against ISIS and the social and political structures established since 2014. It emphasized that the ongoing process of democratic integration into the Iraqi state must be based on recognition of these achievements.


Shengal was liberated on November 13, 2015, following more than a year of fighting against ISIS. The People’s Council particularly honored the efforts of the Kurdish guerrilla forces and Yazidi defense units. It specifically commemorated the fallen commanders Dilşêr Herekol, Egîd Civiyan, Berfîn Nûrhaq, Nûjîn Amed, Çeko Çatak, Saît Hesen, Berxwedan Tolhildan, Dijwar Feqîr and Zerdeşt Şengalî.


“Just as the history of our people has been marked by attacks and fermans, its courageous people have repeatedly written stories of victory through their resistance,” the statement said. The Yazidi community uses the term

Ferman

to refer to the historical campaigns of persecution and extermination directed against its people.


‘Liberation of Shengal marked the beginning of a new phase in Yazidi history’


The People’s Council pointed out that the liberation of Shengal marked the beginning of a new phase in the history of Yazidi society. According to the council, the establishment of democratic and social institutions has enabled the Yazidi population to increasingly take control of its own affairs. In this context, the People’s Council referred to the political ideas of Abdullah Öcalan, whose philosophy, it said, has played a decisive role in shaping independent organization and social reconstruction. The council also views the current steps toward democratic integration into Iraq in connection with the Peace and Democratic Society Process initiated by Öcalan.


“Our struggle is for recognition of Shengal’s will”


The People’s Council stated that the progress achieved so far has created an opportunity to establish relations between Shengal and the Iraqi state on a new foundation. Central to this is the demand for recognition of the independent political and social structures established by the Yazidi population. According to the council, this also includes the ability to defend its own society against renewed attacks.


“Shengal was liberated through the efforts of its own sons and daughters and has now, within the framework of democratic integration, developed the capacity to defend its own society,” the statement said.


Young Yazidi women and men are taking responsibility for defending their community to prevent further campaigns of extermination, the council said, noting that Yazidi society possesses the will and determination to shape its own political representation.


“Our goal and our struggle are directed toward securing recognition of the will of Yazidi society and Shengal. As the Yazidi community and the social forces of Shengal, we have spent twelve years building our social structures with great determination and continuing our work on the basis of the will of a free society.”


The council stressed that recognition of this political will would not contradict Iraq’s territorial unity. On the contrary, it could strengthen the Iraqi state and reinforce social cohesion within the country, it said.


Call for a joint celebration on November 13


The People’s Council called on the people of Shengal, as well as members and supporters of the Yazidi community, to celebrate the anniversary of the liberation together. A central celebration is scheduled for Friday, November 13, at 2:00 p.m. in front of Medreseya Sor in the center of Shengal. The People’s Council invited the public to participate in the celebrations marking the 11th anniversary of the liberation.

author: Unknown
title: Koçyiğit: Rojin Kabaiş case extends into state institutions
content:
Gülistan Kılıç Koçyiğit, deputy parliamentary group chair of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), called for a full investigation into the death of university student Rojin Kabaiş during a press conference at the Turkish parliament. Her remarks followed an attack and threats against the young woman’s uncle in Istanbul. Koçyiğit expressed suspicions that the case involved connections to state institutions and drew parallels with the unresolved disappearance of university student Gülistan Doku.


At the beginning of her press conference, Koçyiğit addressed the explosion at the HABAŞ steel plant in the Aliağa district of Izmir province, which claimed the lives of 19 workers. She criticized the failure to hold those responsible accountable and the lack of adequate state oversight of workplace safety.


“There are no independent inspections, and no one talks to the workers. Instead, they talk to the business owners. Not a single concern raised by employees is heard. Workers are dying because these safety measures would impose costs on employers,” Koçyiğit said.


Another issue addressed at the press conference was the sinking of the Tuğberk İmamoğlu vessel in the Sea of Marmara in September. The families of nine people whose bodies have still not been recovered visited several parliamentary groups the previous day to draw attention to their situation. Koçyiğit criticized the authorities’ inaction, saying: “A state that knows when a sheep goes missing on the banks of the Euphrates has failed to recover the bodies from the Sea of Marmara for months.”


Corruption allegations and criticism of COP31


The lawmaker contrasted the deadly working conditions faced by workers with the latest revelations surrounding the investment fund scandal. While people work under life-threatening conditions for a monthly wage, millions were transferred through fraudulent financial transactions, Koçyiğit said, adding that she had received numerous messages from victims seeking public attention.


Regarding the arrest of former Minister of Family and Social Affairs and AKP deputy chair Fatma Betül Sayan, she stated: “We say, finally. But we know that attempts are being made to cover up this affair by sacrificing a handful of individuals.”


The DEM Party politician also criticized the UN Climate Change Conference COP31, currently taking place in Antalya. She accused companies such as Cengiz, LİMAK and SİMPAŞ, which are sponsoring the event, of engaging in greenwashing. “On the one hand, you destroy nature and wipe out olive trees through hydroelectric power plants, geothermal facilities and mining projects. On the other hand, you present yourselves at COP31. We do not accept this,” she stated.


“This is about women’s right to life in this country”


Referring to the recent armed attack and threats against an uncle of Rojin Kabaiş in Istanbul, Koçyiğit leveled serious accusations against state institutions. She drew parallels with the unresolved disappearance of Gülistan Doku: “As in the case of Gülistan Doku, this is also a case with connections extending into state institutions and the structures operating within them.”


Emphasizing the broader social significance of the case, Koçyiğit said: “The case of Rojin Kabaiş is not merely about the loss of one person. It is about women’s right to life in this country. We will continue to demand justice for Gülistan Doku and Rojin Kabaiş.”


The DEM Party politician called on the Ministry of Justice to ensure that both cases are fully investigated and those responsible are identified.


Criticism of extended prison terms


Finally, the DEM Party politician criticized the practices of the Administrative and Observation Boards in Turkish prisons. She said these boards continue to prevent the release of prisoners who have been incarcerated for more than 30 years and have already completed their sentences.


Koçyiğit appealed to the Minister of Justice: “We are now genuinely ashamed of having to raise these issues over and over again. I once again call on this country’s Minister of Justice: Stop keeping people in prison after they have served their sentences and allowing the Administrative and Observation Boards to make arbitrary decisions.”


Koçyiğit stressed that the ongoing violations of prisoners’ rights must end. “Do not become complicit in depriving people of their freedom,” she said.

author: Unknown
title: Students in Rojava: We will not back down until our right to education in Kurdish is recognized
content:
Protests against restrictions on Kurdish-language education continue across Rojava. On Thursday, students, parents and residents demonstrated in Hesekê, Dirbêsiyê and Rimêlan, demanding recognition of Kurdish as an official language of Syria and constitutional guarantees for the right to education in their mother tongue.


In Hesekê, hundreds of people took part in a march that began at the Kevok roundabout and continued to the Şehîd Serhed intersection. Demonstrators carried banners bearing slogans such as “Our language is our identity,” “Our rights must be guaranteed in the constitution,” “Kurdish is our red line” and “Our language is our dignity.”


PYD: Damascus must reverse its decision


At the rally that followed, Ebdulxenî Oso of the Democratic Union Party (PYD) addressed the demonstrators. He recalled the development of Kurdish-language education since the beginning of the Rojava Revolution.


“The identity of peoples is closely linked to their language and culture. In Rojava, the Kurdish language has made significant progress over the past 14 years. Kurdish has been used as the language of instruction in schools, institutes and universities. Today, our language is also used in civilian institutions and public offices,” Oso said.


Oso continued: “Any restrictions on these achievements are unacceptable. Syria is a country with a rich diversity of peoples, languages and cultures. Preserving this diversity requires a democratic system that guarantees the rights of all communities. I call on the government to reverse its decision and correct this mistake. If it does not recognize the Kurdish language, it means that it does not recognize the existence of the Kurdish people either.”


Students demand recognition of Kurdish as an official language


Students in Dirbêsiyê also protested against the restrictions. Children and young people from the Şehîd Cemil Ehmed Hesen School in the village of Til Kerem issued a statement, which was read aloud by student Sozdar Hemê.


In the statement, the students called for the protection and development of the Kurdish language and its recognition as one of Syria’s official languages. They emphasized that Kurdish is inseparable from the identity, history and culture of the Kurdish people. “Preserving and promoting our mother tongue is a fundamental human right that must not be restricted,” they underlined.


“Without language, there is no life”


Another demonstration took place in Rimêlan. Students from Girkê Legê and Rimêlan gathered in front of the Şehîd Şîlan School and marched through the city. Outside the Silêman El Helebî School, student Zîlan Berekat read a joint statement. She described education in one’s mother tongue as a fundamental right and demanded that the Kurdish language and the right to Kurdish-language education be explicitly enshrined in the Syrian constitution.


The students vowed to continue their protests until the Kurdish language and the right to education in Kurdish are recognized: “We will not back down until our right to education in our language is recognized.”


The rally concluded with the slogan “Bê ziman jiyan nabe” – “Without language, there is no life.”

author: Unknown
title: Women in Arzoxlî continue resistance against solar power project
content:
Resistance against the construction of solar power facilities continues in the village of Arzoxlî (Turkish: Kervanpınar) in the province of Amed (Diyarbakır). Residents have been holding a protest vigil against the Zenkar 1 project for 22 days. During a march from the village square to the planned construction site, Turkish gendarmerie units blocked the path of the protesting women.


The demonstrators chanted slogans such as “Our land and our water are our existence,” “We will prevail through resistance” and “No to the company.” When soldiers prevented them from entering the site, the villagers questioned the legality of their actions: “On what legal grounds are you preventing us from entering our own land?”


“They have bought everything with money”


Emine Eren, who has been participating in the protest vigil, accused the security forces of prioritizing the company’s interests over the rights of the villagers. “There is no humanity left here. People have no heart anymore. They have bought everything with money. There is no justice left to speak of,” she said.


Eren criticized the fact that residents have to protest every day against encroachments on their living environment. “Do we really have to come here every day? Our village has its own resources. If this were a good project, we could implement it ourselves.” Following the confrontation with the soldiers, the women returned to the protest tent and continued their vigil.


Legal victory against another solar energy project


Alongside their protests against Zenkar 1, residents of Arzoxlî recently secured a legal victory against another solar energy project. The Administrative Court in Amed ordered the temporary suspension of the Zenkar 2 project. However, resistance against the planned solar installations and the associated encroachment on agricultural land continues.

author: Lilli Akpaleeapik
title: Iqaluit Skating Club receives $5,000 grant
content:
The Iqaluit Skating club has $5,000 to spend after being named a recipient of this year’s Canada Post Community Grant.


Canada Post presented the grant to the local skating club on Monday morning at Astro Hill in Iqaluit.


Following the presentation of a $5,000 cheque, the Canada Post Community Foundation held an event for all attendees to celebrate the work that the Iqaluit Skating Club does for the community.


The non-profit distributes grants to schools, community organizations and other charities across the country that provide services for youth up to age 21.


The club provides programs and lessons and facilities for the community year round, with the grant aimed at supporting its inclusive skating programs.


The event also highlighted the importance and positive impacts created by community partnerships, according to Mahmooda Ahmed, who works for Canada Post.


This year, the Canada Post Community Foundation awarded over $1.3 million to 113 organizations across the country. The Iqaluit skating club was the only grant recipient from Nunavut.

author: Diana Varenik and Natascha Elena Uhlmann
title: Lessons from an 85-Day Hotel Strike
content:
You’d be forgiven for worrying, 12 weeks into a strike, that the boss is hell-bent on waiting you out. But after more than 80 days on the picket line at Seattle’s Embassy Suites by Hilton in Pioneer Square, Aspen Desmarais was undeterred. “I can live on a budget,” she said. “Been doing it since day one.”


After 85 days, on September 10, workers won the longest hotel strike in Washington state history. Their union, UNITE HERE Local 8, represents 4,000 hospitality workers in Oregon and Washington.


Desmarais, a strike captain and bartender at the hotel, worked to keep others motivated throughout the fight. She and her co-workers were “tired of people talking down to us and not treating us with respect,” she said, “when we’re the reason that place stays running the way that it does.”


Hilton’s offer, two weeks into the strike, of

one cent per hour over its previous proposal

 helped fuel outrage. The union held open bargaining, so members heard the offer firsthand. “I [felt] frustrated and disrespected,” Desmarais said. “Especially with how much hard work my co-workers put into making sure the hotel and its guests have clean spaces and stays that are welcoming.”


Fritzie Corral, an Embassy Suites breakfast attendant, had only worked at the hotel for two months before walking out. As the strike went on, she said, her son worried that she had made a mistake in taking the job.


“You see other employees that decided to stay in the hotel working," she said. “Even during that time, I still believed I made the right choice. It’s my right to voice out what I feel and to fight for my rights.”


Hilton did not respond to requests for comment.


PROTECTION FROM ICE


Workers won significant pay increases, lowered barriers for health care eligibility, and highly sought-after protections for immigrant workers. Hilton, which manages the hotel, drew protests earlier this year for housing ICE agents and for

cutting ties with

 a Minneapolis hotel that canceled ICE bookings during Operation Metro Surge.


The union’s leaders criticized Hilton throughout the strike for dismissing contract language that would protect immigrant workers. “With ICE-related killings in the news for months causing immigrant workers to worry, why is Hilton refusing to give immigrant workers’ union a heads up if ICE is staying at the hotel?” Local 8 President Anita Seth

asked

Businesswire

.


Ultimately workers won a commitment from Hilton not to punish workers who call out due to an immigration enforcement surge, plus language binding the hotel to an expedited resolution process in such an event. Workers who lose their work authorization due to immigration enforcement will now be able to return to their jobs if their work authorization is restored within four years, and retain their seniority for up to two.


Desmarais told

Labor Notes

 that making sure immigrant co-workers missing work because of ICE “knew they would have a job still and a safe place to come back to” was the “most important” win strikers fought for.


Starting in 2027, housekeepers will make over $31 an hour—a giant step above the $17.63 an hour that housekeepers make on average across the country, per the Bureau of Labor Statistics. The new contract makes them the highest-paid housekeepers in the state, according to the union. Embassy Suites workers classified as “tipped” will now make $1 more per hour than the city’s minimum wage.


Health care eligibility was also a core demand for the union. Many hotel workers under collective bargaining agreements must meet a minimum threshold of hours worked to qualify for health benefits in a given period. Seasonal layoffs, a hallmark of hotel work, often mean inconsistent coverage for workers and their families.


The new contract replaces the month-to-month eligibility standard with an annual threshold of 1,250 hours, or around 24 hours a week, to qualify.


MASS CANCELLATIONS


The strike coincided with five of the six World Cup soccer matches held at Seattle’s Lumen Field this summer, directly across from the Embassy Suites. World Cup-related leverage helped produce

quick contract wins

 this summer for service and hospitality workers in Philadelphia, New York, and Los Angeles, but not so in Seattle.


How did strikers there keep up the pressure for another 63 days after the games ended? The hotel’s proximity to Lumen Field makes it a destination for football fans when the season starts in September. On game days, the hotel sets up a …

author: Harrison Stetler
title: Is France Prosecuting a Palestinian Refugee on Evidence Extracted by Israeli Torture?
content:
How might a hostile state pursue a refugee beyond its borders? This is a question some fear is at the heart of a case currently inching its way through

France’s special-track antiterrorist justice system

. 


Four UN special rapporteurs have warned that 2024 charges brought against “Ali O”, a Palestinian national who held refugee status in France, are built on compromised evidence provided by Israel. 


“We are concerned that Ali’s arrest, detention and prosecution appear to be based on information obtained through the use of torture and other forms of abuse against Palestinians by Israeli authorities,” wrote the UN experts, including human rights lawyer Francesca Albanese, in a 28 August communication issued to France and

published in late October

.


After fleeing Palestine, Ali O settled in France in 2016 and obtained formal recognition as a refugee in 2020. Married to a French citizen and the father of French children, he was arrested at his home in Strasbourg in May 2024. He was subsequently indicted for charges of terrorist financing and conspiracy connected to militant activity in the occupied West Bank in early 2023. 


A memo from the French intelligence services to the country’s refugee administration, and included in the litigation file seen by Novara Media, claims the defendant “participated in the transfer of funds and weapons with military aims” to Palestinian armed groups.


The investigation against Ali O was opened in late 2023. Though French criminal procedure precludes the defence from uncovering certain state evidence, the French state alleges that the defendant was a past member of the Fatah Hawks, a militant group linked to the al-Aqsa Martyrs’ Brigades and affiliated with the Fatah faction of the Palestine Liberation Organisation. It also claims that the defendant conducted online searches on websites used for the dissemination of guerilla tactics and weaponry. 


“[Ali O] committed several crimes incompatible with refugee status. Our service proposes withdrawing refugee status for the concerned party,” wrote the French intelligence bureau. Authorities revoked Ali O’s refugee status in February 2025, even though he has yet to be convicted and is therefore presumed to be innocent.   


Dismissing these accusations, Ali O’s counsel claimed allegations like these would be difficult to construct without close collaboration with outside state sources, notably Israeli. “Ali’s dossier demonstrates the degree to which the French justice system has accepted the role of a subcontractor for Israeli authorities,” attorney Raphaël Kempf told Novara Media, placing his client’s case in the wider crackdown and surveillance of Palestinian nationals residing in Europe. 


Irregularities in the case file also point to Israeli influence in the case against Ali O. The French intelligence memo stipulates he participated from France in militant activity in “Judea and Samaria,” i.e. the Israeli state’s official designation for the West Bank, which is internationally recognised as Palestinian territory, including by France. 


France’s anti-terrorism prosecutorial service (PNAT) declined

 Novara Media’s request for comment. 


Ali O isn’t an unknown quantity for the Israeli state. 


Born in 1990 and raised in the Balata refugee camp on the outskirts of the West Bank city of Nablus, Ali O was 14 years old when he witnessed his younger brother’s killing by an Israeli soldier. Two years later, he was arrested and held in extrajudicial detention before receiving a four-year prison sentence for throwing stones at Israeli occupation forces. It was the first of many stints in jail, according to the biographical information compiled by activists with the Free Ali committee. After his last release from Israeli detention in 2014, he fled to Europe, passing through Italy and Switzerland before making it to France. 


“France recognised [Ali O] as a refugee because of his well-founded fear of persecution by Israeli authorities,” UN special rapporteur on torture Pau Pérez-Sales said at a 29 October press conference following the publication of the co-signed notice to the French government. 


The case against Ali O is based on evidence gathered by Israel from three Palestinian sources. The UN memo warns that one witness, Ali O’s brother, was tortured on several occasions and there are grounds to presume that the other two sources were tortured as well, habitual practices for Palestinians held in Israeli captivity. title: Di fronte alle (finte) bombe, non ci sono interessi comuni.
content:
Le evacuazioni in massa delle scuole di ieri e oggi non sono il primo tentativo di imporre la logica dell’emergenza e dell’interesse nazionale per portarci alla guerra, ma per la prima volta si abbattono su un movimento di massa giovanile e studentesco che sta facendo tremare il governo e vacillare la sua tenuta. Oltre il panico e la paura, si apre una sfida inedita per chi si è messo in movimento: trovare risposte diverse e dal basso, che parlino la lingua del contropotere rifiutando la retorica dell’unità nazionale e della difesa della Repubblica. Forse una sfida che arriva “troppo presto”, ma alla quale non è tardi per provare a rispondere.


Una cosa è certa: la

“guerra ibrida”

 svela la vulnerabilità, inietta la paura, confonde le idee.

Il punto è chi la vuole.

 Il governo italiano è in prima fila per beneficiare degli effetti della guerra ibrida in modo tale da giustificare la spesa e la retorica sulla “difesa”. Non si discosta infatti da nessun governo europeo su questo,

il mantra è prepararsi alla guerra alla Russia mascherata dalla guerra della Russia nei confronti dell’Occidente.

 


Da frigoriferi alle scuole, dai droni agli allarmi sui voli internazionali. Il metodo è quello di disorientare e legittimare le operazioni di riarmo europeo su vasta scala. Il punto non è tanto quanto un allarme o un episodio sia vero o falso ma il fatto che resti ignota la sua origine e che di fatto il governo italiano e in generale l’Unione Europea ci stanno trascinando in una guerra che diventa sempre più reale e concreta. 


Oggi l’allarme scatta nelle scuole italiane, nelle stesse ore si stanno svolgendo i colloqui Kiev -Usa- Mosca ad Abu Dhabi, ed è difficile pensare che sia casuale. La prima domanda che dobbiamo porci è: a chi giova?

 L’allarme scatta e immediatamente le scuole vengono evacuate, perché in fondo prima ancora che sia possibile pensare in maniera razionale al da farsi, è necessario delegare a chi ha pensato piani di emergenza per noi la scelta. Per ora, questo avviene in maniera grossolana, manuale, alla vecchia maniera con carabinieri e forze armate che devono finalmente poter entrare a scuola. 


In queste settimane i carabinieri si sono fatti largo in una scuola di Firenze con le pistole puntate per sgominare un allarmante tentativo di occupazione. Forze di polizia a Torino si sono sbizzarrite nel trovare vari modi per penetrare nelle scuole dove poter arrestare studenti e applicare una presenza significativa agli ingressi, dove è possibile anche che una mattina qualsiasi si venga identificati “perché è prassi”. Di questo passo quando i docenti, i dirigenti, i rettori, accoglieranno l’uso dell’intelligenza artificiale per controllare queste “emergenze”? Tutto lo sproloquiare a destra e sinistra sull’importanza della cybersecurity non è altro che la preparazione del prossimo passo in cui la “tecnologia” dovrà salvarci con l’innovazione, invece che affrontare politicamente il problema.


Lo stesso pseudonimo utilizzato in queste mail che hanno svuotato le scuole italiane era comparso negli attacchi ai voli aerei, in Bulgaria, era stato utilizzato per costruire un allarme simile in scuole e asili. Uno pseudonimo che ricorda l’immaginario sovietico, come hanno ben da sottolineare i media nostrani, e così alla Russia si abbina anche l’immaginario misogino e di violenza contro le donne: questo presunto leader della Vilayat di Misoginistan non è distante dalla sigla dei “Combattenti dello Stato Maschile” che hanno firmato i messaggi minatori dei voli aerei nelle scorse settimane.

Insomma sigle di rivendicazione che ricordano più dei meme che dei gruppi hacker. 


La guerra ibrida, quando si è in guerra, è uno degli strumenti che vengono messi in campo, non c’è molto da stupirsi.

Ma ci sembra di essere di fronte ad una guerra ibrida rivolta all’interno,

 Nord Stream docet. La guerra ibrida oggi allarga i confini e il campo di chi combatte e chi no, lo è inglobando progressivamente ogni ambito del reale, anche se la genesi si attiene al campo del virtuale. Se queste a cui assistiamo sembrano operazioni “false flag”, anche quando arriveranno risposte, simmetriche o no, da chi lo stato attacca militarmente da anni, anche senza soldati dichiarati sul campo, la colpa sarà comunque di chi ci ha trascinati in questa situazione.

author: Wolfgang
title: Kündigungen nach Krankenhausstreik 2013 im Spital „La Providence“ in Neuenburg/Neuchâtel
content:
Dossier


Auf einen ersten Warnstreik am 18. September 2012 reagierte die Geschäftsleitung mit Repression, Drohungen und Verschleppung der Verhandlungen. Auch der Staat versuchte gegen die Kampfbereitschaft vorzugehen und erklärte einen ersten Streikversuch für illegal.  Die Angestellten des Spitals haben sich nicht einschüchtern lassen und sind am 26. November in den Streik getreten. Sie kämpfen damit für den Erhalt des geltenden GAVs Santé 21, gegen die drohende Auslagerung und gegen aktuelle Entlassungswellen. Die Kantonsregierung gerät zunehmend in die Kritik… Siehe dazu:


Nach 15 Jahren bestätigt der internationale Gerichtshof für Menschenrechte das Grundrecht auf Streik der 22 ehemalige Angestellten des Privatspitals La Providence


Wegweisendes Urteil gegen die Schweiz: EGMR stärkt Streikrecht


„

Der Schweizerische Gewerkschaftsbund (SGB) begrüsst das heutige Urteil des Europäischen Gerichtshofs für Menschenrechte (EGMR) zum Streik am Neuenburger Privatspital La Providence. Der Gerichtshof stellt fest, dass die Schweiz die Gewerkschaftsfreiheit verletzt hat. Das Urteil ist ein wichtiger Erfolg für die Beschäftigten und ihre Gewerkschaften. Es macht deutlich: Wer für bessere Arbeitsbedingungen streikt, muss sich auf den Schutz seiner Grundrechte verlassen können.


Die Beschäftigten des Privatspitals La Providence wehrten sich 2012 und 2013 gegen eine Verschlechterung ihrer Arbeitsbedingungen. Sie kämpften insbesondere für die Weitergeltung ihres Gesamtarbeitsvertrags. 22 Streikende wurden fristlos entlassen, weil sie ihren Arbeitskampf fortsetzten. Das Bundesgericht hatte die Entlassungen geschützt und den Streik als unverhältnismässig beurteilt.


Der EGMR verurteilt die Schweiz im heutigen Urteil. Der Gerichtshof kritisiert insbesondere, dass für die Beschäftigten nicht ausreichend vorhersehbar war, unter welchen Voraussetzungen die Fortsetzung ihres Streiks als rechtswidrig beurteilt werden konnte. Die Schweizer Gerichte hätten die Bedeutung des Streikrechts und die Interessen der Beschäftigten stärker berücksichtigen müssen. Auch die strafrechtlichen Verurteilungen von vier Gewerkschaftssekretärinnen und -sekretären wegen eines friedlichen Streikpostens verletzen gemäss EGMR die Gewerkschaftsfreiheit.


Der SGB würdigt den beharrlichen Einsatz der Gewerkschaften VPOD und Syna – sowie insbesondere der betroffenen Beschäftigten. Sie haben fast 15 Jahre für ihre Rechte gekämpft und damit einen wichtigen Beitrag zum Schutz der Gewerkschaftsrechte in der ganzen Schweiz geleistet.


Das Urteil hat Bedeutung weit über den Einzelfall hinaus

…“

SGB-Meldung vom 6. November 2026

 


Urteil aus Strassburg: Endlich Genugtuung für Spital-Streikende


„

Im Jahr 2013 hat das Privatspital La Providence 22 Streikende in Neuenburg fristlos entlassen, weil sie sich gegen die Verschlechterung ihrer Arbeitsbedingungen gewehrt hatten. Erst jetzt, fast 15 Jahre später, bestätigt der internationale Gerichtshof für Menschenrechte ihr Grundrecht auf Streik. (…) Das Urteil ist ein klarer Sieg für die Gewerkschaften und eine Klatsche für die Schweiz. Es bestätigt, dass das Streikrecht ein Grundrecht ist und von den Gerichten nicht ausgehöhlt werden darf.


Auf der Seite der Arbeitgeber


Geklagt hatten ehemalige Angestellte des Privatspitals La Providence in Neuenburg. Ihnen drohten massive Verschlechterungen ihrer Arbeitsbedingungen. Dagegen hatten sie sich mit den Gewerkschaften in den Jahren 2012 und 2013 gewehrt. Wegen dieses Arbeitskampfes wurden 22 von ihnen fristlos entlassen. Und vier Gewerkschaftssekretärinnen und -sekretäre strafrechtlich wegen Hausfriedensbruchs verurteilt. Weder die Geschassten noch die Gewerkschaften akzeptierten diese Verletzung des Streikrechts und zogen vor Gericht. Doch die Schweizer Justiz stellte sich auf die Seite der Arbeitgeber. Auch das Bundesgericht urteilte 2019, dass der Streik illegal gewesen und die Entlassungen sowie die Verurteilungen somit rechtens seien.


Versammlungsfreiheit verletzt


Jetzt das klare Verdikt vom Europäischen Gerichtshof: Der EGMR hat einstimmig entschieden, dass die Schweiz Artikel 11 (Versammlungs- und Vereinigungsfreiheit) der Europäischen Menschenrechtskonvention verletzt hat. Und weiter: Weder die Schweizer Bundesverfassung noch die nationale Rechtsprechung würden eine Grundlage für das Gericht bieten, einen rechtmässigen Streik für unrechtmässig zu erklären, nur weil der Arbeitgeber ein Angebot unterbreitete.
