title: "Я не преступник, а заложник". История осужденного по обвинению в подготовке теракта анархиста Алексея Григорьева
content:
В феврале 2025 года суд приговорил 27-летнего анархиста из Оренбургской области Алексея Григорьева к 20 годам заключения. Его обвинили в попытке вступить в легион "Свобода России" и намерении поджечь по заданию украинских спецслужб релейный шкаф в Новотроицке. Во время следствия и суда он заявлял о пытках с применением тока. С марта 2026 года Григорьев отбывает наказание в Верхнеуральской тюрьме — по его словам, у него резко ухудшилось здоровье после избиений во время этапирования. "Idel.Реалии" рассказывают его историю.

О задержании Алексея Григорьева ФСБ отчиталась 22 мая 2023 года. В пресс-релизе ведомства говорилось, что "по указанию украинских спецслужб" он готовил поджог релейного шкафа на железнодорожной станции "Новотроицкая", а также военкомата Орска и отдела ФСБ России.

ФСБ также опубликовала видео задержания Григорьева, а также показала фотографии тайника с канистрой, бутылкой машинного масла и ацетона. На видеозаписи житель Оренбургской области сказал, что с ним связались "люди с Украины и предложили с ними сотрудничать": "Я должен был поджечь релейный шкаф, чтобы остановить работу железнодорожной станции".

Правозащитный проект "Поддержка политзеков. Мемориал" в своем недавнем докладе пришел к выводу, что сотрудники ФСБ инсценируют задержания и заставляют подозреваемых записывать признания на камеру, в том числе после пыток. Признаки постановки правозащитники обнаружили примерно в четверти проанализированных сцен задержания.

Согласно исследованию, в некоторых случаях подозреваемых специально вывозили для съёмок, заставляли повторять заранее подготовленные действия и произносить согласованные со следствием признания.

В тот же день СМИ переписку, якобы обнаруженную у Григорьева в Telegram — в ней он, по утверждению ФСБ, общается с представителем "украинских спецслужб". Собеседники обсуждают возможность закладки бомбы в здание ФСБ или военкомата, но в итоге решают использовать горючие смеси для поджога релейных шкафов.

Впоследствии в приговоре по делу Григорьева (копия имеется в распоряжении "Idel.Реалии") утверждалось, что он "15 мая 2023 года направил на электронную почту украинского военизированного объединения легион "Свобода России" заполненный им бланк анкеты кандидата на вступление".

В дальнейшей переписке с неким участником "Легиона", представлявшимся "Семеном", Григорьев якобы согласился с его предложением поджечь релейный шкаф на станции, для чего "приобрел в магазинах Новотроицка компоненты для изготовления зажигательной смеси и инструменты для вскрытия релейного шкафа".

Как следует из приговора, вечером 20 мая Григорьев сделал тайник в лесополосе у трассы Новотроицк — Хабарное и спрятал там приобретенное. После этого его задержала полицейские. Он утверждал, что добровольно передумал совершать преступления и сообщил об этом оперативникам.

Суд также утверждает, что в начале мая 2023 года на одной из остановок Новотроицка нашли листовку с призывом к российским военным сдаваться в плен ВСУ. Якобы после этого сотрудники ФСБ и вышли на Григорьева.

22 мая 2023 года Ленинский районный суд Оренбурга отправил подозреваемого в СИЗО на два месяца. В июне Григорьева внесли в реестр "террористов и экстремистов" Росфинмониторинга.

В мае 2024 года издание SOTAvision опубликовало письмо Григорьева из СИЗО, в котором он сообщил о пытках. Заключенный писал, что на него оказывают моральное и физическое давление, требуя отказаться от адвоката, и под давлением диктуют условия явки с повинной. Кроме того, Григорьев рассказал, что сотрудники следственного изолятора устраивают провокации, не отдают и не отправляют письма и не оказывают ему медицинскую помощь.

— Заключенные угрожают мне расправой и убийством, — говорилось в письме Григорьева. — Я боюсь выходить за пределы камеры. Сколько ещё терпеть эти издевательства?! Почему меня не отпускают домой?! Мое психическое здоровье ухудшается, я хочу покончить с собой. <…> У меня больная бабушка одна осталась — и всем плевать на это, она нуждается в моем уходе, она не может себе лекарства купить, она уже целый год мучается, а сотрудники ФСБ её добивают, кошмарят её.

Алексей Григорьев родился 18 декабря 1997 года. До ареста он работал продавцом в ломбарде "Пионер" в Орске.

Знакомые Григорьева рассказали "Idel.Реалии", что его воспитывала бабушка, поскольку еще в раннем детстве он остался без родителей.

— Отец покинул семью, когда Алексею было два года, мать примерно в то же время завела новую семью — и с тех пор ни с сыном, ни со своей матерью отношения не …

title: İspanya: Kiracıların isyanı genel greve dönüştü
content:
İspanya'da kiracı derneklerinin başlattığı barınma hakkı mücadelesi, ülkenin iki büyük sendika konfederasyonu CCOO ve UGT'nin katılımıyla 24 saatlik genel greve dönüştü. “Ücretler. Konut. Fiyatlar.” sloganıyla düzenlenen grev, sanayi tesislerinde üretimi durdurdu, ulaşımı aksattı ve onlarca kentte gösterilerle sürdü.


Madrid, Barselona ve diğer kentlerde grev gözcülerine yönelik polis müdahaleleri yaşandı. İçişleri Bakanlığı'nın gün içindeki verilerine göre 42 kişi gözaltına alındı.


Madrid'deki Mercamadrid toptancı halinde polisin biber gazı kullanmasının ardından en az 13 kişi sağlık ekiplerinin yardımına ihtiyaç duydu. Sendikalar müdahaleleri grev hakkının ihlali olarak nitelendirerek sorumlular hakkında hukuki girişim başlatacaklarını açıkladı.


Fabrikalarda üretim durdu, ulaşım aksadı


CCOO ve UGT, grevin özellikle otomotiv, limanlar, enerji ve ulaşım sektörlerinde etkili olduğunu bildirdi.


Sendikaların açıkladığı oranlara göre otomotiv ve deniz ve hava limanlarında iş bırakma yüzde 90'a, et üretiminde yüzde 85'e, çöp toplama işlerinde yüzde 82'ye, enerji sektöründe ise yüzde 75'e ulaştı.


Barselona yakınlarındaki SEAT Martorell fabrikasında üretim durdu. Navarra'daki Volkswagen tesislerinde de geniş çaplı iş bırakıldı. 


Tren seferleri olağan kapasitenin yüzde 50 ila 75'iyle sürdürüldü. Havalimanlarında 234 uçuş iptal edildi. Barselona'da metro ve otobüs seferleri sınırlandırıldı. Katalonya'da otoyollar, sanayi bölgeleri ve tren istasyonları çevresinde grev gözcüleri toplandı.


Eğitim kurumlarında da iş bırakma görüldü. Ancak perakende ticaret, küçük işletmeler ve bazı kamu hizmetlerinde katılım daha sınırlı kaldı.


Sendikalar grevin başarılı olduğunu açıklarken, işveren örgütleri katılımın düşük kaldığını savundu. Kiracılar Sendikası yaklaşık 4 milyon kişinin greve katıldığı öngörüsünü paylaştı. 


“Polisin görevi grev hakkını güvence altına almak”


CCOO Genel Sekreteri Unai Sordo, Mercamadrid'deki polis müdahalesini eleştirdi:


“Bu tam bir skandal. Yaşadıklarımızın cezai ve her türlü sorumluluğunun hesabını soracağız.”


UGT Genel Sekreteri Pepe Álvarez de polisin grev hakkını güvence altına almakla yükümlü olduğunu söyledi.


Polis, bazı göstericilerin yolları ve işyerlerinin girişlerini kapattığını bildirdi. Barselona'da lastiklerin yakıldığı barikatlar kuruldu; çeşitli kentlerde göstericilerle polis arasında arbede yaşandı.


“36 yaşındayım, hâlâ kendi başıma bir eve çıkamıyorum”


Genel grevin kaynağı, İspanya'da giderek ağırlaşan konut krizi. 


Madrid'de bir hastanenin bilgi işlem bölümünde çalışan 36 yaşındaki Jesús González, Reuters'a barınma sorununu kendi yaşamından hareketle anlattı:


“36 yaşındayım ve hâlâ kendi başıma bir eve çıkamıyorum.”


Ülkede ortalama kiralar son 10 yılda neredeyse iki katına çıktı. İspanya Gençlik Konseyi'nin hesaplamalarına göre ortalama aylık kira, genç bir çalışanın ortalama ücretinin neredeyse tamamına denk geliyor. 


Barselonalı 45 yaşındaki işçi Carlos Ferrer de Associated Press'e yaptığı açıklamada genel grevin gerekçesini şöyle anlattı:


“Yetkililerin bir şeyler yapması için yurttaşların baskısını hissetmeleri gerekiyor.”


Kiracı örgütleri kira artışlarının sınırlandırılmasını, sözleşmelerin otomatik yenilenmesini, tahliyelerin önlenmesini ve konut spekülasyonunun durdurulmasını istiyor.


Maricarmen'in tahliyesinden genel greve


Greve giden süreç, Madrid'de 87 yaşındaki Maricarmen Abascal'ın evinden zorla tahliye edilmesi ve ardından hayatını kaybetmesi üzerine büyüyen protestolarla hızlandı.


Kiracı örgütleri, hükümetin konut krizine karşı hazırladığı bazı önlemlerin 2 Ekim'de parlamentoda sağ partilerin oylarıyla reddedilmesinin ardından düzenlenen kitlesel gösterilerde genel grev çağrısını yükseltti.


Kiracılar Sendikası sözcüsü Alicia del Río, 11 Kasım'da şöyle konuştu:


“Maricarmen'in tahliyesiyle 40 gün önce başlayan öfke büyümeyi sürdürdü ve şimdi kentlerimizin sokaklarına taştı.”


Del Río, konutların yatırım ve rant aracı haline getirilmesine karşı mücadele ettiklerini belirtti:


“Evler, rantiyeci azınlığa hizmet etmek için değil, içinde yaşamak içindir.”


Kiracı örgütleri sendikaları harekete geçirdi


11 Kasım grevinin ayırt edici yanı, çağrının başlangıçta işçi sendikalarından değil, kiracı örgütlerinden gelmesiydi.


Kiracılar Sendikası, büyük konfederasyonlar katılmasa da küçük sendikalarla birlikte genel greve gideceğini duyurmuştu. CGT gibi örgütler çağrıya erken destek verdi. CCOO ve UGT ise 5 Ekim'de greve katılma kararı …

title: Νέα παράσταση διαμαρτυρίας των ΕΛΜΕ για την παραβίαση των ωραρίων των εκπαιδευτικών, Πέμπτη 12/11 14:00 στη στη ΔΔΕ Ανατολικής Θεσ/νίκης
content:
Γ΄ – Ε΄ ΕΛΜΕ Θεσσαλονίκης Θεσσαλονίκη, 8/11/62026


ΟΙ ΑΥΘΑΙΡΕΣΙΕΣ ΚΑΙ Ο ΑΥΤΑΡΧΙΣΜΟΣ ΤΗΣ ΔΔΕ ΑΝΑΤΟΛΙΚΗΣ ΘΕΣΣΑΛΟΝΙΚΗΣ ΔΕΝ ΘΑ ΠΕΡΑΣΟΥΝ!


ΥΠΕΡΑΣΠΙΖΟΜΑΣΤΕ ΤΑ ΕΡΓΑΣΙΑΚΑ ΜΑΣ ΔΙΚΑΙΩΜΑΤΑ ΚΑΙ ΤΟ ΔΗΜΟΣΙΟ ΣΧΟΛΕΙΟ


Νέα παράσταση διαμαρτυρίας των ΕΛΜΕ στη ΔΔΕ Ανατολικής Θεσ/νίκης, Πέμπτη 12/11, 2μμ


(κηρύσσουμε μονόωρες και δίωρες στάσεις εργασίας 12μ. – 2μμ)


Οι Γ΄ και Ε΄ ΕΛΜΕ-Θ συνεχίζουμε με αποφασιστικότητα και συλλογική δράση τον αγώνα απέναντι στις


αυθαίρετες εντολές της ΔΔΕ Ανατολικής Θεσσαλονίκης, που επιχειρούν να καταστρατηγήσουν τα εργασιακά


δικαιώματα των εκπαιδευτικών και να επιβάλουν νέα δεδομένα στη λειτουργία των σχολείων, ενώ και στη


Δυτική παρουσιάζονται ανάλογα φαινόμενα, με ευθύνη κάποιων Διευθυντών/τριών με “υπερβάλλοντα ζήλο”,


πρόθυμοι να υλοποιήσουν τους κυβερνητικούς στόχους συγκάλυψης των κενών στα σχολεία και δημιουργίας


τετελεσμένων για την εφαρμογή του 30ωρου.


Η ΔΔΕ Ανατολικής Θεσσαλονίκης για άλλη μια φορά, μετά τον πρωταγωνιστικό ρόλο που επέδειξε με τον


πρωτοφανή αυταρχισμό για να επιβάλει την αξιολόγηση, ξανά στο γνώριμο ρόλο του λαγού που ξέρει καλά να


εφαρμόζει, έστειλε αυθαίρετες οδηγίες για την παραμονή των μαθητών στο σχολείο μέχρι τη συμπλήρωση της


6 ης και 7 ης ώρας του διδακτικού ωραρίου, ακόμη και όταν στα σχολεία υπάρχουν κενά γιατί δεν προσλήφθηκαν


εκπαιδευτικοί. Να τα μετατρέπουν σε «εικονικά μαθήματα» και να καλύπτονται από εκπαιδευτικούς σε ρόλο


παιδοφύλακα, που δεν προβλέπεται από καμία εκπαιδευτική διαδικασία που ισχύει για το ωράριο διδασκαλίας


και εργασίας των εκπαιδευτικών.


Οι Γ΄ και Ε΄ ΕΛΜΕ-Θ από την πρώτη στιγμή καταγγείλαμε ότι η επίκληση της ασφάλειας των μαθητών


χρησιμοποιείται ως πρόσχημα για τη συγκάλυψη της υποστελέχωσης και την επιβολή πρόσθετων υποχρεώσεων


στους εκπαιδευτικούς, στο πλαίσιο της προσπάθειας εμπέδωσης του λεγόμενου «30ωρου» και της συγκάλυψης


της πολιτικής λιτότητας και περικοπών της κυβέρνησης στην εκπαίδευση.


Από την πρώτη στιγμή κινητοποιηθήκαμε και απαιτήσαμε την ανάκληση της οδηγίας. Πραγματοποιήσαμε


παράσταση διαμαρτυρίας στην Περιφερειακή Διεύθυνση Εκπαίδευσης Κεντρικής Μακεδονίας στις 23/9 και στη


ΔΔΕ Ανατολικής Θεσσαλονίκης στις 2/10. Αντιπροσωπείες των Γ΄ και Ε΄ ΕΛΜΕ-Θ συναντήθηκαν με τη


διευθύντρια της ΔΔΕ, Ζ. Βαζούρα, ζητώντας την άμεση απόσυρση του επίμαχου εγγράφου. Εκείνη αρνήθηκε


κατηγορηματικά, χαρακτηρίζοντας την οδηγία «απολύτως νόμιμη», χωρίς ωστόσο να επικαλείται συγκεκριμένη


νομοθετική διάταξη, υπουργική απόφαση ή εγκύκλιο. Η στάση αυτή κατέδειξε την πρόθεση της διοίκησης να


επιβάλει αυθαίρετες πρακτικές έξω από το θεσμικό πλαίσιο και τις ανάγκες της εκπαιδευτικής διαδικασίας.


Στις 9 και 10/10 πραγματοποιήθηκε συνάντηση του προέδρου της ΟΛΜΕ και του Δ.Σ. της Δ΄ ΕΛΜΕ-Θ με τον


Περιφερειακό Διευθυντή Εκπαίδευσης, Α. Κόπτση. Αντί να υπάρξει ουσιαστική παρέμβαση για την ανάκληση της


οδηγίας και να δοθούν σαφείς απαντήσεις, ο Περιφερειακός Διευθυντής, μέσα από υπεκφυγές, ουσιαστικά


κάλυψε τις ενέργειες της ΔΔΕ. Αναμένουμε ακόμη την επίσημη ενημέρωση της ΟΛΜΕ για τη συνάντηση, καθώς


και μια σαφή ανακοίνωση καταγγελίας των αυθαιρεσιών. Αντί για καταγγελία και οργάνωση κινητοποιήσεων, η


ΟΛΜΕ με ανακοίνωσή της υπενθυμίζει τις νομοθετικές ρυθμίσεις που είναι ήδη γνωστές στους συναδέλφους,


χωρίς να απαντάει πώς θα γίνουν αποδεκτές από ΔΔΕ που τις παραβιάζουν.


Παράλληλα, απευθυνθήκαμε σε όλες τις ΕΛΜΕ της πόλης, επιδιώκοντας κοινή κινηματική και νομική


παρέμβαση. Προτείναμε την οργάνωση νέας κινητοποίησης στη ΔΔΕ Ανατολικής Θεσσαλονίκης στις 30/10, τη


νομική σύνταξη γνωμοδότησης για τις αυθαίρετες παρατυπίες της Βαζούρα και άμεσα την πρώτη νομική


παρέμβαση με κατάθεση εξώδικου στη Διεύθυνση για τις παρατυπίες της.


Οι Γ΄ και Ε΄ ΕΛΜΕ-Θ προχωρήσαμε στην υλοποίηση των συλλογικών μας αποφάσεων, ενώ οι υπόλοιπες ΕΛΜΕ


αρνήθηκαν τη συμμετοχή τους στην κινητοποίηση και στις νομικές ενέργειες.


Στην τελευταία παράσταση διαμαρτυρίας (30/10) επιδώσαμε εξώδικο στη ΔΔΕ Ανατολικής Θεσσαλονίκης, ενώ


παράλληλα κοινοποιούμε στα σχολεία τη νομική γνωμοδότηση που τεκμηριώνει τις καταγγελίες μας και


αποσαφηνίζει το θεσμικό πλαίσιο για το εργασιακό ωράριο και τα καθήκοντα των εκπαιδευτικών.


Για ακόμη μία φορά, η διευθύντρια της ΔΔΕ, Ζ. Βαζούρα, απουσίαζε, επιλέγοντας να μην αντιμετωπίσει


αυτοπροσώπως τα εκπαιδευτικά σωματεία και τα ζητήματα που θέτουν. Η επικοινωνία έγινε με διοικητική


υπάλληλο, στην οποία εκθέσαμε εκ νέου το πρόβλημα και ζητήσαμε να μεταφερθεί στη διευθύντρια το …

title: KESK Samsun Şubeler Platformu: Atakum Belediyesinde işten atılan işçiler yalnız değildir
content:
Kamu Emekçileri Sendikası (KESK) Samsun Şubeler Platformu, Atakum Belediyesinde işten atılan işçilerle dayanışma açıklaması yaptı. “Emeğin hakkı, işçinin onuru ve örgütlü mücadelesi teslim alınamaz” denilen açıklamada, Atakum Belediyesindeki çalışma koşullarına da tepki gösterildi.

KESK Dönem Sözcüsü Uğurcan Albak imzasıyla yayımlanan açıklamada, “Atakum Belediyesi’nde aylardır ücretlerini alamadıkları için haklarını arayan, insanca yaşam ve güvenceli çalışma koşulları talep eden işçi arkadaşlarımızın işten çıkarılması, yalnızca birkaç emekçinin işsiz bırakılması değildir. Bu karar, emeğin haklı taleplerine karşı geliştirilmiş açık bir baskı ve sindirme politikasıdır. Samsun’un Atakum ilçesinde yaşananlar, yerel yönetimlerin emek karşısındaki tutumunu ve siyasi söylemleriyle uygulamaları arasındaki çelişkiyi bir kez daha gözler önüne sermiştir. Kendilerini emekten, halktan ve demokrasiden yana tanımlayan yönetimlerin de emekçilerin en temel hakları söz konusu olduğunda bu ilkelerin gereğini yerine getirmediği görülmektedir” ifadelerine yer verildi.

İşçinin ücretini istemesinin suç olmadığı vurgulanan açıklamada, “Emeğinin karşılığını talep etmesi, sendikal örgütlenme hakkını kullanması ve insanca çalışma koşulları için mücadele etmesi en temel demokratik ve sendikal hakkıdır. Bu hakları kullanan işçileri işten çıkarmak, sorunları çözmek değil, emekçileri işsizlik tehdidiyle susturmaya çalışmaktır. Belediyeler, hangi siyasi anlayışla yönetilirse yönetilsin, kamusal sorumluluklarının ve emek karşısındaki yükümlülüklerinin gereğini yerine getirmek zorundadır. Sosyal belediyecilik, emekten yana olmak ve halkçı yönetim anlayışı, seçim dönemlerinde kullanılan söylemlerle değil; çalışanların ücretlerinin zamanında ödenmesi, iş güvencesinin sağlanması, sendikal haklara saygı gösterilmesi ve emekçilerin iradesinin tanınmasıyla mümkündür” denildi.

Atakum Belediyesi’nde yaşananların, yalnızca belediye işçilerinin sorunu olmadığı, Samsun'da emeğiyle geçinen bütün işçilerin, kamu emekçilerinin ve emek örgütlerinin ortak problemi olduğu vurgulanan açıklamada, “Çünkü biliyoruz ki bir işyerinde işçinin hak arama mücadelesine yönelen saldırı, başka işyerlerindeki emekçilere de verilmiş bir gözdağıdır. İşçi sınıfının tarihsel kazanımları, bağımsız ve öz iradeleriyle gelişen bağımsız, demokratik, mücadeleci sendikal örgütlenme ve birleşik sınıf dayanışmasıyla elde edilmiştir. Emekçilerin iradesini esas alan, mücadeleyi dar pazarlıklara sıkıştıran ve işverenlerin politikalarına yedeklenen sendikal anlayışlara karşı gerçek bir emek ve demokrasi mücadelesini büyütmek zorundayız. .Sendikalar, yalnızca üyelerinin aidatlarını alan, toplu sözleşme dönemlerinde masaya oturan kurumlar değildir” vurgusu yapıldı.

Açıklamada talepler şu şekilde sıralandı:

“İşten çıkarılan bütün işçiler derhal işlerine iade edilmelidir.

Birikmiş ücretler ve işçilerin tüm özlük hakları eksiksiz ödenmelidir.

İşçilerin sendikal örgütlenme ve hak arama özgürlüğüne yönelik baskılara son verilmelidir.

İşçilerin iradesi ve çalışma yaşamında demokratik hak ve özgürlükler güvence altına alınmalıdır.

Emekçileri işsizlik ve yoksullukla karşı karşıya bırakan uygulamalardan vazgeçilmelidir.”

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Murder of Vesile Akın leaves five children without their mother
content:
On 9 November, Vesile Akın, 35, was attacked with a knife on Bismarck Street in Düren, in Germany’s North Rhine-Westphalia state, by her 39-year-old husband, Ferhat Akın. The couple had been living separately due to severe marital problems. Vesile Akın, a mother of five originally from Mardin (Mêrdîn), died in hospital from her severe injuries. Ferhat Akın, who fled the scene, was subsequently caught by police.


She had previously requested protection


It was reported that Vesile Akın had contacted the police and requested protection because she had been threatened by her husband. Reports indicate that police had previously taken action against him due to their marital problems and his threats, and that restraining measures had been imposed. However, the woman reportedly continued to be harassed.


Despite her previous complaints and the protective measures reportedly put in place, Vesile Akın was murdered. Her death has raised serious questions about the effectiveness of security measures and mechanisms designed to protect women from violence.


Calls for investigation into possible failures


The murder of Vesile Akın has once again highlighted the importance of ensuring that women facing threats of violence receive timely and effective protection. Calls have been made for a review of the previous complaints filed in connection with the case, the protection orders issued, and the security measures taken. There have also been demands for any possible negligence to be exposed and for those responsible to face the necessary legal action.

author: Unknown
title: Fuel crisis in Kobanê takes heavy toll on residents
content:
The increase in fuel prices across Syria has deepened the economic crisis in Kobanê. Following the rise in fuel costs, prices for food, transport and other essential goods have also increased. In the city, where the cost of many products has doubled or tripled, people's purchasing power continues to decline, while concerns over heating are growing ahead of the winter months.


Rising fuel prices are particularly affecting traders and small business owners involved in commerce and production. Higher transportation and production costs are being passed on to consumers through increased prices. Meanwhile, difficulties in obtaining diesel have forced residents to turn to electric heaters for warmth, placing additional pressure on the electricity network.


Speaking to ANF, residents and shopkeepers in Kobanê said they would face numerous difficulties this winter. They stated that although the amount of fuel being distributed had not changed, the prices of almost every product they purchased had increased.


The cost of transporting a truckload of goods has doubled


Kamıran Baz, a business owner in Kobanê, said there had been serious difficulties in obtaining fuel this year. He explained that residents struggling to find diesel had begun purchasing electric heaters, which was also having a negative impact on the electricity network.


Noting that rising fuel prices had increased transportation costs, Baz said that transporting a truckload of goods, which previously cost $100, now cost $200 — twice as much.


Emphasising that rising diesel prices were directly affecting not only transportation but also the prices of goods and services, Baz said shopkeepers were being forced to pass their increased costs on to consumers.


Prices increased


Mihemed Memiş, who works in metal fabrication and also sells stoves, said the increase in fuel prices had raised production costs. Stating that almost all products had become more expensive this year compared with last year, Memiş called for diesel prices to be reduced. He said: “Everything has become much more expensive this year compared with last year. Our current demand is for diesel prices to be reduced somewhat. I manufacture doors, and whereas I previously sold each door for 30 US dollars, I now sell them for 40 US dollars. This is because diesel has become so expensive.”


No diesel for stoves


Memiş said he had to run his generator for long hours to keep his metal fabrication business operating. He added that rising diesel prices had forced him to increase the cost of manufacturing doors. He explained that they had also started selling stoves ahead of the approaching winter season. However, because diesel was difficult to obtain and insufficient quantities were being distributed, people could not afford to buy stoves. Stressing that the fuel shortage was affecting both production and people's ability to heat their homes, Memiş called for prices to be reduced and the problems surrounding fuel supplies to be resolved.

title: YRK Commander pays tribute to the martyrs: We will ensure that their goals are achieved
content:
On 5 November, the Press Center of the People’s Defense Forces (HPG) announced the identities of nine guerrilla fighters from Rojhilat who lost their lives between 2006 and 2022 in various regions of Kurdistan.


On 9 November, the HPG Press Center announced the identities of 15 guerrilla fighters from the Maku city of East Kurdistan who joined the Kurdish freedom movement and lost their lives at different times and in various locations between 2007 and 2024.


Speaking to ANF, Şiyar Şevger, a member of the Command Council of the East Kurdistan Units (Yekîneyên Rojhilatê Kurdistan, YRK), made the following remarks in memory of the martyrs:


https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/2ff679a0_20261111095750_2026-11-11-habermerkezi-siyar-sevger-yrk-komutanligi-uyesi-nirxandin-1.mp4


“I dedicate this process that has been initiated to all our martyrs. I commemorate all our martyrs across the four parts of Kurdistan and bow respectfully before their memory.


Recently, the names of martyrs from East Kurdistan (Rojhilat), as well as followers of Apo from Rojhilat who fell in North Kurdistan (Bakur), have been announced. These martyrs have fostered a spirit of unity among Kurds. The martyrs have consolidated the paradigm put forward by Leader Apo [Abdullah Öcalan] to defend the Kurdish people. The martyrs are leading the way for humanity in the Middle East. The paradigm they have championed is intended to serve all humanity and the unity of the Kurdish people.


In fact, the martyrs have enabled us to understand ourselves and our history. More importantly, they have helped us recognize our enemies who have carried out massacres against our people. It is thanks to Leader Apo’s ideas and philosophy, together with the sacrifices of the martyrs, that we have reached this point today. Their goals will undoubtedly be achieved, and the struggle they waged will not have been in vain.


As the people of Rojhilat, we must honor and stand by the martyrs with great pride. Regardless of which city or village they come from, all our people, families and patriots must rally around the families of the martyrs, come together and show solidarity with them. They must not be left alone. The pain of every family is the pain of all Kurds. Our families have paid a heavy price and sacrificed their loved ones. Their grief is immense. Therefore, no one should leave them alone. We owe to the martyrs who gave their lives to defend our honor.


There are many martyrs from Sine in particular. There are martyrs from our other cities as well, but Sine is a city of resistance and revolution. All our people in Sine must unite around these families and stand by them. We have nothing to fear.


The role of our mothers in this revolution is particularly important. Everyone must stand by the mothers who raised their children and entrusted them to this movement. Mothers are the hope of the Kurdish people and the peoples of the Middle East. As long as our mothers are alive, Kurdistan will undoubtedly achieve success.


To the martyrs whose names have been announced so far, particularly those from Rojhilat and the other parts of Kurdistan, and to all the martyrs whose names will be announced in the future, we make this pledge: We will certainly uphold their struggle and ensure that their goals are achieved.


Recently, some reports have appeared in the media questioning why the names of our martyrs have been announced so late. I believe all our people know that we are a movement engaged in struggle in the mountains of Kurdistan. The Apoist Movement has fought against the occupiers of our homeland everywhere, including in the mountains. It has carried out this struggle in the face of all kinds of technology, weapons and chemical weapons.


Amid such intense warfare, there was no opportunity to announce the deaths of our comrades in a timely manner. A peace process began following Leader Apo’s call. title: The importance of Kurdish democracy
content:
While the Kurdish people and their friends everywhere have been eagerly anticipating “national unity,” news that even the existing administration in Southern Kurdistan has split into two has, frankly, caused considerable astonishment. Moreover, it has provoked significant anger and backlash. At the same time, it has prompted everyone to reassess their expectations and views and question the reasons behind this situation.


Yet the call made in recent months by Kurdish People’s Leader Abdullah Öcalan for the establishment of a “Democratic Unity Government” had generated considerable hope and expectations among the public. National unity was also the most widely discussed issue in the Kurdish press and public discourse. Although everyone expressed it from their own perspective, the need for national unity was the issue on which there was the greatest consensus. Both political awareness and collective sentiment reflected this need.


Admittedly, the persistent fragmentation among Kurdish principalities throughout history left those who contemplated and advocated national unity with little hope or confidence. This situation has been a constant source of criticism and frustration. The experience of Southern Kurdistan offered little reason for optimism in this regard.


Although the Kurdistan National Congress (KNK) was established a quarter of a century ago, it has been unable to fulfill its role or function effectively because certain parties have refused to participate and have obstructed its work. Despite nearly two years having passed since the elections in Southern Kurdistan, parliament had not convened, and a new government had not been formed.


Undoubtedly, all of this led to disappointment among Kurdish society and its supporters, weakening their faith in the prospect of national unity. Nevertheless, the Kurdish people remained determined and steadfast in their pursuit of unity, aware of the immense importance of Kurdish national unity for the Kurds, the Middle East and humanity as a whole. Considerable knowledge and understanding have been developed on this issue, accompanied by an increasingly strong sense of its significance. Accordingly, the Kurdish people never abandoned their demand for unity, while continuously questioning the factors obstructing it and seeking ways to overcome them.


The stance and efforts of the Kurdish Freedom Movement on this issue have always been positive. In fact, the movement has consistently devoted a substantial proportion of its resources to efforts aimed at achieving national unity. Abdullah Öcalan’s creative approach and extensive efforts, in particular, have always been worthy of recognition.


Indeed, it was Öcalan who carried out all the preparations for the establishment of the Kurdistan National Congress. Had he not been subjected to an international conspiracy, his aim was to organize the national congress under favorable conditions and through effective methods, assume its leadership and ensure that all activities were coordinated at the highest level through this institution. This was also the primary reason he chose to travel to Europe when confronted with a conspiratorial campaign against him.


This leadership project was thwarted by the October 9 and February 15 attacks of the international conspiracy. Although the KNK was subsequently established on the basis of those preparations and has continued its activities for a quarter of a century, its achievements have fallen far short of realizing Öcalan’s vision.


Why, then, has Kurdish national unity not been achieved despite so much discussion and demand, and why has the KNK not been made effective? In fact, this is one of the most important questions facing the Kurds today, perhaps even the most important, and one that must be answered accurately and adequately. The current developments in Southern Kurdistan provide an opportunity to raise this question courageously and seek answers. The discussions conducted in this context are marked by a considerable lack of courage and an overly superficial approach. Moreover, the rhetorical grandstanding of nationalist perspectives prevents these discussions from becoming comprehensive and in-depth.


According to the nationalist perspective, such discussions are essentially unnecessary because the national leadership of the Kurds is embodied by the Barzanî family! From this standpoint, national unity means rallying around the Barzanî family! Furthermore, Kurds are …

title: Families of fallen guerrilla fighters demand access to their graves
content:
Nearly three decades after the deaths of their loved ones, families of fallen Kurdish guerrilla fighters gathered for a two-day commemoration. Organized by MEBYA-DER (Association for Solidarity, Assistance, Unity and Culture of Families Who Lost Relatives in the Cradle of Civilizations), the event honored 19 people who lost their lives in the Kurdish freedom struggle during the 1990s. For many families, it was the first opportunity in years to mourn their children and siblings together. Their most important demand remains unfulfilled: they want to know where the remains of their loved ones are located and to be able to visit their graves.


The families linked their commemoration to the hope of an end to the decades-long war. They emphasized that the ongoing Peace and Democratic Society Process must produce concrete results. They said they did not want other families to suffer the same loss or spend decades living without certainty about the fate of their loved ones.


https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/6a4204e4_20261110234226_2026-11-11-amed-filiz-bayram_mehmet-emin-kilic_seniha-yolay-sehit-aileleri-sehit-anma_1.mp4


“As a mother, this is my only demand”


Seniha Yolay is among the mothers who still do not know where their children are buried. Her son Şahabettin Yolay, who went by the name Siyabend in the guerrilla movement, joined the PKK in 1994 and fell in 1998. She had not seen him since he left home. It was only years later that the family learned of his death, without ever receiving further information about his whereabouts.


“My son left the house saying he was going to school. He never came back. In 1998, we learned that he had lost his life. Since then, we have heard nothing more about him. I kept asking questions, but no one could tell me anything. Today, after 30 years, we held a memorial service for him. I want to know where my son’s grave is. As a mother, this is my only demand,” Yolay said.


Yolay stated that being able to mourn her son alongside other families now held great significance for her. For many years, she added, the families had been left alone with their grief and uncertainty.


“Being able to mourn them, even after all these years, is very important to us. The fighting has continued for decades. This peace process must achieve its goal, and no more bodies should be brought home. We families want peace. We do not want anyone else to suffer or lose their life.”


Yolay emphasized that the families had never forgotten their loved ones, despite the many years that had passed.


“This bloodshed has continued for 50 years. It must stop. From now on, people should no longer have to live in fear of receiving another news of death.”


“We want them to have a grave”


Filiz Bayram also attended the commemoration. Her brother Meki Bayram, known by the name Çiya Dilbirîn, joined the PKK in 1992 and was martyred in 1994. The passing decades have done nothing to diminish the family’s memories of him or their grief.


“My brother is gone. I hope that from now on, no one else will lose their life. The peace process must finally be realized through concrete steps. No one should have to suffer anymore. Enough is enough,” Bayram said.


She noted that the collective memorial service had brought back memories that remained as vivid as ever for the families, despite the passage of time.


“After 33 years, we are mourning here and shedding tears once again. To us, everything feels as though it happened yesterday. No mother, no sister ever forgets their fallen loved ones or those days. We have forgotten neither the suffering we endured nor the people we lost.”


Bayram called for an end to the armed conflict and a peace process that would go beyond political statements.


“The war must finally end, and the sounds of tanks and artillery must fall silent. We have endured everything imaginable over the years. Now, peace must finally come to this country. Genuine peace.”


Above all, however, she said she wanted to have a place where she could commemorate her brother.


“We want them to have graves. And if there are no graves, we at least want to know where their remains are. We want to be able to stand at their graves, even if only once. This is not just our demand, but the demand of every family in the same situation.”


Many families have still been unable to say goodbye

title: Freedom for Abdullah Öcalan vigil in Strasbourg enters its 750th week
content:
The freedom for Abdullah Öcalan vigil, held in Strasbourg, France, since June 25, 2012, has entered its 750th week. Through the protest, which has continued for more than 14 years, participants are demanding the physical freedom of the Kurdish leader who has been incarcerated in İmralı Island Prison since 1999.


During the new week of action, Tori Orak, Kurbet Dağ and Adalet Rojhilat from the Liège region of Belgium have taken over the vigil.


In a joint statement, the activists commemorated the fallen members of the Kurdish freedom movement whose deaths have been announced in recent months. They reaffirmed their remembrance with the slogan “Şehîd namirin” (Martyrs are immortal).


Call for support for the peace process


The activists called on the families of the martyrs and the entire Kurdish population to support the Peace and Democratic Society Process initiated by Abdullah Öcalan. They emphasized that they wanted to see Öcalan free and once again among the people.


The group said they had taken responsibility for the vigil this week as representatives of the Kurdish community in Liège.


“We hope that the entire Kurdish people will embrace this process, organize themselves and prepare for the developments ahead,” the activists said.

title: Nine Kurds, including seven political activists, remain forcibly disappeared in Iran
content:
Nine Kurdish citizens, including seven political activists, remain forcibly disappeared months or years after their arrests by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Intelligence Organisation and the Ministry of Intelligence of the Islamic Republic of Iran.


They are Osman Mameh, Arman Khalegh-Panah, Edris Feqhi, Mohsen Ghaderi, Sara Rashidi Kachalanlou, Zahra Pir-Dehghan, Parvin (Akhtar) Rasegh Ghezelbash, Khaled Barzanji and Sirwan Habibi.


Seven are members of the Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK) or the Free Women’s Society of Eastern Kurdistan (KJAR). Their arbitrary arrests took place in Bukan, Saqqez, Baneh, Orumiyeh, Paveh and Kamyaran from August 2021 onwards, without minimum legal safeguards.


The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has established that security and judicial authorities verbally informed the families of Ghaderi and Khalegh-Panah that the two men had been killed.


Neither family has received official documentation or a death certificate substantiating the claim, and neither man’s body has been returned.


The other families have also received no clear answers about the fate or whereabouts of their loved ones, despite repeatedly approaching security and judicial authorities. The authorities concerned have denied knowing about the arrests.


All nine have been denied access to independent lawyers of their own choosing and all contact and visits with their families since their arrests.


In light of the evidence and circumstances of each case, KHRN considers the authorities’ refusal to acknowledge the arrests or disclose the individuals’ fate and whereabouts to constitute the crime of enforced disappearance.


These continuing violations affect both the disappeared individuals and their families, who are denied the right to know the truth about what has happened to their loved ones and where they are held.


Given the continuing nature of enforced disappearance and the international obligations of the Islamic Republic of Iran, KHRN calls on the international community to pursue these cases urgently and exert effective, meaningful pressure on the authorities to disclose the disappeared individuals’ fate and whereabouts and ensure accountability.


This appeal is directed particularly to the UN Human Rights Council, the UN Special Rapporteur on the situation of human rights in the Islamic Republic of Iran, the UN Special Rapporteur on torture and other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment, and the UN Working Group on Enforced or Involuntary Disappearances.


KHRN calls for:


– Increased international pressure on the responsible authorities

: Use official communications, public statements and diplomatic and human rights mechanisms to require the authorities of the Islamic Republic of Iran to acknowledge responsibility for the arrests, disclose the disappeared individuals’ fate and end their enforced disappearance.


– Guarantees for the liberty, safety and rights of the disappeared individuals:

Demand an immediate end to secret detention, disclosure of places of detention, access to independent lawyers of the individuals’ own choosing and their families, and judicial and independent oversight.


– Independent and effective investigations:

 Demand prompt, independent, impartial and effective investigations into the arrests, transfers and secret detention, including the roles of IRGC Intelligence Organisation and Ministry of Intelligence forces and contradictory claims that some individuals may have been killed.


– Support for families and their right to the truth:

 Require documented and transparent information about the disappeared individuals’ fate, an end to threats, intimidation and pressure against families, and guarantees of their right to seek the truth and access justice.


– Accountability and an end to impunity:

 Identify and hold accountable everyone who ordered, carried out or bears official responsibility for these continuing enforced disappearances, through investigations and prosecutions consistent with fair-trial standards.


Names and details of the disappeared individuals:


Edris Feqhi


Edris Feqhi, a Kurdish political activist from Sanandaj and a PJAK member, was arrested on 24 July 2021 after being wounded in an IRGC ambush in the mountains around Bukan.


KHRN’s investigations indicate that IRGC forces shot him in the leg. He initially managed to hide, but forces from the IRGC’s Hamzeh Seyyed al-Shohada Headquarters arrested him while he was …

author: Unknown
title: Kurdish political prisoner sentenced to 15 years in prison and fined in Iran
content:
Branch 26 of the Islamic Revolutionary Court in Tehran has sentenced Kurdish political prisoner Ahmad Tamouei to a total of 15 years in prison and a fine of 12.5 billion rials on charges of “assembly and collusion against national security” and “carrying and possessing weapons,” the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has reported.


The court issued the sentences in recent months against Tamouei, who is held in Greater Tehran Central Penitentiary.


Under Article 134 of the Islamic Penal Code, which governs sentencing for multiple offences, only the most severe punishment, 10 years’ imprisonment and the fine, will be enforceable.


Tamouei, a political activist from Salmas, had previously spent 14 years in Orumiyeh Central Prison before his release in 2021.


He then moved to Tehran, where he worked as a driver for the ride-hailing service Snapp.


In the early hours of 23 February 2026, Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) forces violently arrested him without a warrant at a checkpoint on Kargar-e Jonoubi Street in Tehran and took him to a security detention facility.


IRGC forces subjected him to severe physical and psychological torture for one day before transferring him to Ward 2A of Evin Prison on 24 February.


Following the outbreak of war, Tamouei and several other detainees were moved from the ward to a secret security detention facility in eastern Tehran. He was transferred to Greater Tehran Central Penitentiary on 4 March.


His case was opened at Branch Three of the Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor’s Office in Tehran’s District 33, and was referred to Branch 26 of the Islamic Revolutionary Court in Tehran after the issuance of an indictment.


Background


Tamouei was previously arrested by IRGC intelligence forces in Mahabad on 24 October 2007 and taken to the IRGC intelligence detention facility in Orumiyeh.


In an open letter written in 2016 to Ahmed Shaheed, then UN Special Rapporteur on the situation of human rights in Iran, Tamouei described being tortured for two months in solitary confinement at the facility following his arrest on charges of “membership of PJAK”.


The methods of torture described in his letter included “electric shocks”, “suspension of the body”, “flogging” and “mock execution”.


In February 2008, Branch One of the Islamic Revolutionary Court in Mahabad sentenced him to 15 years in prison and internal exile to Orumiyeh Central Prison on charges of “enmity against God” (moharebeh).


The sentence was upheld in summer 2008, and he was transferred to Orumiyeh Central Prison to serve it.


During his 14 years and two months in prison, the Ministry of Intelligence’s special office inside the prison repeatedly threatened and interrogated him over his participation in strikes by political prisoners.

author: Dominique Gené - Local Journalism Initiative Reporter
title: Award-winning Mary Paningajak sees art as a way to heal
content:
Mary Paningajak grew up surrounded by art in Ivujivik.


She watched her father, Tivi Paningajak, make prints and sculptures, and she remembers visiting his studio.


“One time, he let me make a screen print,” Paningajak said in an interview Tuesday at Kuuujjuaq’s adult education centre.


She was nine years old when she first started making art and spent years learning different tools and techniques.


Now 65, her artistic practice has earned her northern Quebec’s artist of the year award from Quebec’s Council of Arts and Letters, or the Conseil des arts et des lettres du Québec. It’s a $15,000 prize that recognizes her contribution to Nunavik’s arts community.


The council’s director general Véronique Fontaine presented the award on Nov. 8, during the opening night of the Path to 100 festival in Kuujjuaq, which commemorates the anniversary of the signing of the James Bay and Northern Quebec Agreement.


“I was so surprised to hear that I won because there are lots of artists in Canada and Quebec. I was thinking, how come they chose me?” Paningajak said in an interview.


Mary Paningajak demonstrates one of the printmaking techniques she taught participants at the Path to 100 festival, using a spoon to press an inked design onto paper in Kuujjuaq on Nov. 10. (Photo by Dominique Gené)


Working in printmaking, graphic arts and sculpture, she draws inspiration from Inuit history, personal experience and her community.


Pursuing art in Ivujivik, a community of about 412 people on the northern tip of the Ungava peninsula, comes with practical challenges.


“We only have one store, and it doesn’t have any art supplies inside. It’s hard to get materials because we have to travel south by plane or ask people to order things for us,” she said.


Despite those challenges, Paningajak’s work has been exhibited across Canada.


Sikutsajaq, 

a solo exhibition, inaugurated the Centre Sanaaq in Montreal in May 2025. 


Sharing her knowledge of art is also an important part of her work.


During Path to 100, Paningajak led a printmaking workshop, showing participants how to create prints using rubber plates.

Participants drew designs onto the plates, carved them into the rubber and rolled ink over the raised surfaces before transferring their images onto paper.


“I hope that what they learned, maybe some of them will be interested in making more art,” Paningajak said.


The festival invited artists and community members to reflect on Nunavik’s past and imagine what the next 50 years could look like.


For Paningajak, that future includes giving younger generations opportunities to express themselves and find healing through art.


She said making art has helped her work through trauma from past abuse.


“It was important to me to heal through the paper, and I want them to heal in any way they can in the future,” she said.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Otra muerte por asbesto en el subte: anuncian medidas de fuerza
content:
La Asociación Gremial de Trabajadores del Subterráneo y Premetro (AGTSYP – Metrodelegadxs) informó una nueva muerte causada por la exposición al asbesto, un cancerígeno mortal. Ya son 7 los trabajadores fallecidos y 130 afectados por esta causa.


En 2011, Mauricio Macri –entonces jefe de Gobierno de la Ciudad– adquirió sin licitación previa al Metro de Madrid 36 vagones que se encontraban fuera de circulación en España.


A principios del 2017, los trabajadores españoles avisaron a los Metrodelegados que los subtes que se habían vendido a la Ciudad de Buenos Aires, que Macri y Rodríguez Larreta habían ido a comprar, estaban atestados de asbesto. Esos mismos coches eran los que había estado enfermando a los trabajadores del Metro de Madrid con las afecciones que empezaron a afectar a las y los trabajadores argentinos del Subte. También las y los pasajeros están en riesgo.


Entonces comenzó la lucha de los trabajadores de la AGTSyP por la eliminación de este mineral cancerígeno, que en la Argentina está prohibido desde 2003.


Uno de los invitados al VIP fue el empresario Aldo Roggio.


Es el dueño del Subte.


Está semana se murió el 7mo trabajador del subte por exposición al asbesto, un material cancerígeno.


Se había jubilado y le dejaron de cubrir los estudios.


— ari lijalad (@arilijalad)

November 11, 2026


El sindicato señala que el asbesto está presente en toda la red del subte porteño, no sólo en los trenes sino también en instalaciones, transformadores, tendidos eléctricos, infraestructura edilicia.


Compartimos el comunicado:


OTRA MUERTE POR ASBESTO EN EL SUBTE


MEDIDAS DE AUTODEFENSA


Desde la Asociación Gremial de Trabajadores del Subterráneo y Premetro (AGTSYP – Metrodelegadxs) lamentamos anunciar el fallecimiento de un compañero jubilado que trabajó durante 30 años expuesto al asbesto, por lo que el servicio se encontrará interrumpido el día jueves 12 de noviembre, desde las 21hs hasta el cierre.


El compañero trabajó en los talleres Polvorín / Bonifacio y en el Taller Rancagua, uno de los lugares con mayor exposición al asbesto de toda la red.


Los trabajadores expuestos al asbesto tienen controles médicos periódicos, pero estos controles cesan al momento de jubilarse. Nuestro sindicato viene reclamando hace años que los jubilados continúen en vigilancia médica, para detectar a tiempo las enfermedades derivadas de esta contaminación y poder evitar muertes como la de nuestro compañero.


La afección por exposición al asbesto tiene una latencia de 40 años, lo que implica que décadas después de haber trabajado en el Subte y Premetro, pueden despertarse enfermedades relacionadas a la exposición.


En el subte hay 7 trabajadores fallecidos y 130 afectados por la exposición al asbesto. No podemos seguir lamentando muertes que son evitables, nadie tendría que morir por su trabajo.


Todas las personas que trabajan en el Subte y Premetro deben ser incorporadas a Vigilancia Médica, que debe extenderse también a las y los trabajadores jubilados. Seguimos exigiendo un subte y premetro libre de asbesto.

Otra muerte por asbesto en el subte: anuncian medidas de fuerza

 se publicó primero en

Indymedia Argentina Centro de Medios Independientes (( i ))

title: Ex-Met Police Boss Works As Paid Advisor for Palantir
content:
A former head of the Metropolitan police, who was ousted amid scandals over misogyny and racism in the force, is now working as a paid advisor for spytech firm Palantir, the

Bureau of Investigative Journalism has revealed

. 


Cressida Dick resigned as the force’s commissioner in 2022 after London mayor Sadiq Khan publicly said he had lost confidence in her, a move seen as effectively sacking the senior officer. 


In September 2025 she joined Palantir, the Bureau reported on Tuesday, becoming the latest of a number of high-profile public figures taking up work for the firm. 


Former Labour deputy leader Tom Watson

became the firm’s newest senior vice president

 in September this year, while former Conservative defence minister Leo Docherty

joined the firm

 in February 2025.  


Palantir has supplied technology to the Israeli military throughout its genocide in Gaza and has worked with ICE amid its campaign of

abductions and killings

 in the US. 


Palantir told the Bureau that Dick’s role was to advise the firm “on how our software could help improve the delivery of services in the public sector, drawing on more than 40 years of public service in a variety of roles.”


Dick told the outlet: “My role is limited to providing advice on the ways in which products such as theirs may assist public sector services. I do not and have not ever lobbied or advocated for Palantir with any organisation or individual in any sector, nor have I ever introduced Palantir to any contact of mine.”


In 2005, Dick was in charge of the operation during which police shot and killed Jean Charles de Menezes after mistaking him for a suspect in the 7/7 bombings. 


Earlier this week,

the Citizens reported

 that Palantir had won a five-year contract with Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire and Hertfordshire police forces worth £10m. Palantir also has a £9m contract to oversee the firearms licensing system for all of the UK’s police forces.


“It never ceases to amaze me how willing people are to pay money to Palantir for the shoddy goods that they deliver,” Martin Wrigley, a Liberal Democrat MP, told the Bureau. “They think themselves the best in the world but they are just not that good – and keep on hiring people to bend ears to get them in via the back door.”

author: Jake Johnson
title: Democratic Lawmakers Demand Removal of Provisions Deepening US-Israel Military Ties
content:
The group of 12 Democratic senators says the proposed legislation would give Israel greater leverage over US weapons and technology.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Sen. Chris Van Hollen, who is considering a bid for Senate majority leader against Sen. Chuck Schumer, led a group of Democratic lawmakers on Tuesday in demanding that congressional leaders scrap a bipartisan effort to more closely integrate the American and Israeli militaries, warning the initiative would threaten U.S. national security and risk further complicity in Israeli atrocities.

In a letter to Democratic and Republican congressional leaders, Van Hollen (D-Md.) and 11 other members of the Senate Democratic caucus demanded exclusion of three specific provisions from the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), warning they would “constrain the administration’s ability to independently determine how best to protect U.S. national security and would lock in long-term commitments despite our serious concerns with the Israeli government’s actions in Gaza, the West Bank, and other parts of the region.” Schumer did not sign the new letter.

Two of the provisions raised in the letter — Section 1217 of the Senate-passed NDAA and Section 219 of the House version of the bill — would establish a “United States-Israel Defense Technology Cooperation Initiative” aimed at accelerating “bilateral defense technology research, development, testing, evaluation, coordination, and industrial cooperation.”

Lawmakers from both chambers must reconcile the differences between the House and Senate NDAAs before final passage, creating another opportunity for opponents of US-Israel military integration to strip out the provisions.

The senators warned in their Tuesday letter that the “agreements and projects these provisions envision threaten U.S. national security interests by handing Israel leverage over American weapons systems and military technology.”

“Should these provisions be enacted, it would further increase Israel’s leverage over the United States through some of the most sensitive technologies in warfare. That is not in the U.S. interest,” the lawmakers wrote. “If enacted, these agreements would create long-term dependencies by embedding Israeli technology into the U.S. defense industrial base that could make future policy changes costly or difficult to implement.”

“We do not share, let alone co-produce, many of these sensitive technologies even with our closest partners, including NATO or other treaty allies,” they added. “To do so in this instance would be unwise, especially as the government of Israel continues to pursue policies in Gaza, the West Bank, and other parts of the region that are inconsistent with US interests and values.”

The lawmakers also warned against passage of Section 618 of the Fiscal Year 2027 Intelligence Authorization Act (IAA), which would require the executive branch to “expand and enhance intelligence sharing with the government of Israel.” The IAA is usually included in the NDAA.

“The provision would tie the president’s hands from limiting intelligence sharing with Israel, even when doing so may be necessary to protect US national security,” the senators wrote. “That would be irresponsible and especially troubling given public reports that the Defense Intelligence Agency recently raised the counterintelligence threat from Israel to its highest level.”

The senators’ letter came a week after President Donald Trump declared on the day of the midterm elections that he and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reached an agreement to end the roughly $4 billion in military assistance that the U.S. provides to Israel each year.

“This is where Section 219 of the NDAA comes in,” Drop Site reporter Julian Andreone wrote in response to the president’s announcement, referring to the military integration provision. “They’re going to transfer all of the aid behind closed doors and cut it from the appropriations process.”

Rep. Ro Khanna (D-Calif.) argued in a social media post earlier this week that removal of the military integration language from the NDAA “needs to be a top priority” in the lame-duck session of Congress.

“I am pushing every Democrat and our leadership to get Section 219 out of our defense bill,” Khanna said.

ιώργου Μητραλιά


Υπάρχουν -σπάνιες- στιγμές στις οποίες η ιστορία της ανθρωπότητας επιταχύνεται σε βαθμό που να προκαλεί ίλιγγο. Και αυτό ακριβώς συμβαίνει σε αυτό το ανεπανάληπτο φθινόπωρο του 2026, που βλέπει τους τυράννους να τρέμουν, ακόμα και να καταρρέουν κάτω από τα ταυτόχρονα πλήγματα των λαών που εξεγείρονται σε μια ντουζίνα χώρες, κυρίως στην Ευρώπη αλλά και πέρα από αυτήν. Είναι σαν να παρακολουθούμε την επανάληψη της πολύ μακρινής «Άνοιξης των Λαών» του 1848, με τη (σημαντική) διαφορά ότι σήμερα το επίκεντρο αυτών των λαϊκών σεισμών βρίσκεται στην απέναντι ακτή του Ατλαντικού, στις Ηνωμένες Πολιτείες της Αμερικής.


Ας μιλήσουμε λοιπόν για τις Ηνωμένες Πολιτείες και τον ιστορικό σεισμό που συνιστούν τα αποτελέσματα των πολυδιαφημισμένων ενδιάμεσων εκλογών τους. Τελικά, αν υπάρχει κάτι που προκαλεί έκπληξη, αυτό δεν είναι τόσο

η συντριπτική ήττα

 των Ρεπουμπλικάνων (1), όσο μάλλον η έκταση του θριάμβου των αντιπάλων του Τραμπισμού. Πράγματι, ενώ οι δημοσκοπήσεις προέβλεπαν την πιθανή εκλογή ενός Δημοκρατικού ακόμη και στο Κάνσας μετά από 94 χρόνια (!), σχεδόν κανείς, με εξαίρεση τον ίδιο τον ενδιαφερόμενο, δεν πίστευε στην εκλογή ενός Αφροαμερικανού στο Μισισιπή μετά από… 150 χρόνια, μετά από ενάμιση ολάκερο αιώνα! Τι συνέβη, λοιπόν, και φτάσαμε σε μια τέτοια ιστορική ανατροπή;


Η απάντηση σε αυτό το ερώτημα, που έχει κρίσιμη σημασία για την συνέχεια των γεγονότων, δίνεται από την πολύ σοβαρή και αξιόπιστη

δημοσκόπηση

 του CNN (2) αμέσως μετά το κλείσιμο των καλπών. Και το πρώτο πράγμα που μας δείχνει αυτή η δημοσκόπηση είναι ότι η πλειοψηφία εκείνων που ψήφισαν υπέρ των Δημοκρατικών υποψηφίων δεν αυτοπροσδιορίζονται ως… Δημοκρατικοί. Πράγματι, το 35% αυτών αυτοπροσδιορίζεται ως «ανεξάρτητοι» και το 23% ως «Δημοκράτες Σοσιαλιστές (DSA)». Πράγμα που σημαίνει ότι το 58% των δημοκρατικών ψηφοφόρων απορρίπτει το Δημοκρατικό Κόμμα και ψηφίζει υπέρ του μόνο και μόνο επειδή θέλει να απαλλαγεί από τους Ρεπουμπλικάνους του Τραμπ! Με αυτά λοιπόν τα δεδομένα, το ερώτημα που προκύπτει είναι ποιο είναι το κύριο κίνητρό τους όταν επιλέγουν μια τέτοια πολιτική στάση. Η απάντηση της δημοσκόπησης του CNN διαψεύδει κατηγορηματικά όλα όσα λέγονται και γράφονται για το θέμα αυτό: το πρώτο (47%) κίνητρο των δημοκρατικών ψηφοφόρων ονομάζεται «

democracy

» και βρίσκεται πολύ μπροστά από το δεύτερο, που ονομάζεται «

economy

» (37%).


Συνοψίζοντας, οι Δημοκρατικοί ψηφοφόροι παρακινήθηκαν κυρίως να ψηφίσουν όπως ψήφισαν, όχι λόγω των –πολύ πραγματικών– υλικών προβλημάτων τους που απορρέουν από τις αποτυχίες της οικονομικής πολιτικής του Τραμπ, αλλά μάλλον λόγω της επιθυμίας τους να υπερασπιστούν όλα όσα αντιπροσωπεύει η «δημοκρατία», όπως δηλαδή τις δημοκρατικές και κοινωνικές ελευθερίες και δικαιώματα που απειλούνται άμεσα από τον Τραμπ και το αντιδημοκρατικό και φασιστοειδές καθεστώς του! Είναι λοιπόν αυτονόητο ότι ένα τέτοιο κίνητρο προδίδει την ύπαρξη μιας πολιτικής συνείδησης πολύ πιο προχωρημένης από εκείνη που περιορίζεται να αντιδρά (ακόμη και βίαια) στα υλικά προβλήματα της καθημερινής ζωής.


Κατά συνέπεια, δεν είναι τυχαίο ότι αυτή η δημοσκόπηση του CNN επιβεβαιώνει αυτό που τόσες άλλες είχαν διαπιστώσει προηγουμένως: δηλαδή, ότι ένας ολοένα και μεγαλύτερος αριθμός Αμερικανών πολιτών απορρίπτει τον καπιταλισμό και τάσσεται υπέρ του «σοσιαλισμού», ακόμα κι αν ο “σοσιαλισμός¨” του είναι κάτι συγκεχυμένο και όχι πολύ σαφές. Και αυτό εξηγεί με τη σειρά του, τη σημαντική επιτυχία των «σοσιαλιστών», ριζοσπαστικών προοδευτικών και λοιπών αριστερών υποψηφίων στις ενδιάμεσες εκλογές. Έτσι, οι DSA κατάφεραν να εκλέξουν μια συντρόφισσά τους δήμαρχο του Λος Άντζελες, με αποτέλεσμα οι δύο μεγαλύτερες πόλεις της χώρας, η Νέα Υόρκη και το Λος Άντζελες, καθώς και η διοικητική της πρωτεύουσα, η Ουάσιγκτον D.C., να έχουν πλέον δημάρχους των DSA! Και επιπλέον, οι DSA πέτυχαν να εκλέξουν 8 από τα μέλη τους στη Βουλή των Αντιπροσώπων, στα οποία θα πρέπει να προστεθούν τουλάχιστον άλλοι 6 επίσης νεοεκλεγμένοι βουλευτές, οι προεκλογικές εκστρατείες των οποίων υποστηρίχθηκαν ενεργά από τους DSA.


Ωστόσο, αν και αποτελούν τη μεγαλύτερη αριστερή οργάνωση της χώρας, οι Δημοκρατικοί Σοσιαλιστές της Αμερικής (DSA) απέχουν πολύ από το να οργανώνουν ή να εκπροσωπούν όλους τους σοσιαλιστές, τους προοδευτικούς ριζοσπάστες και λοιπούς αριστερούς, τόσο στην κοινωνία όσο και στο Κογκρέσο των Ηνωμένων Πολιτειών. author: Joshua Fechter
title: Texas Democrats Take Aim at Data Centers, Flock Cameras and Immigration Enforcement
content:
Democrats have taken control of the Texas House, but their proposals face resistance in the GOP-controlled Senate.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Riding high after their success in last week’s election, Democrats in the Texas Legislature unveiled an aggressive agenda Monday as bill filing opened for the 2027 session: Expand Medicaid. Boost the minimum wage. End tax breaks for data centers. Ban Flock cameras. Legalize marijuana.

Other ideas included undoing a state law that requires sheriffs to partner with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement and forbidding border wall construction at state parks.

Democrats also filed proposals to end the state’s year-old school voucher program and boost per-pupil funding for public schools. They also eye building high-speed rail stretching from Dallas to San Antonio.

The 90th session of the Texas Legislature will convene Jan. 12 in a new era under a Democratic governor and divided Texas Legislature.

The opening of the bill-filing period marks the unofficial opening of the next legislative session. As of 5 p.m. Monday, more than 1,260 bills had been filed, with much more to come before bill filing ends March 12.

Most legislation will fall short of the governor’s desk, but Monday’s flurry offered an early glimpse of lawmakers’ priorities.

Democrats took majority control of the Texas House, but many of their proposals can expect heavy resistance in the Senate, where Republicans still hold the majority after last week’s midterm elections. And while Republicans took a drubbing in last week’s voting, bills filed Monday signaled they haven’t abandoned their priorities.

Republican lawmakers filed bills aimed at getting rid of property taxes, forbidding local governments from hiring lobbyists and making English the official language of the state of Texas.

There also were signs of common ground, particularly when it comes to tangling with data centers, wrangling property tax bills and enacting term limits for statewide officials.

First out of the gate Monday morning were House and Senate bills to expand access to Medicaid. Under Republicans, Texas has long held out on expanding Medicaid under the Affordable Care Act — which would send the state up to $10 billion a year and cover an additional 1 million Texans. Texas is the most populous state to not allow Medicaid expansion.

State Rep. John Bucy, D-Austin, filed a bill that would direct the Texas Health and Human Services Commission to file a federal plan to expand Medicaid. State Sen. Judith Zaffirini, D-Laredo, filed a companion bill in the Senate.

Bucy acknowledged that any move to expand Medicaid health insurance coverage would face pushback from the Texas Senate, where Republicans continue to hold a majority.

“We do think there’s going to be a lot of room to find compromise,” he said. “The House and the Senate need to find compromise to get things done for the people of Texas.

Medicaid in Texas mostly covers low-income children, new moms and older adults. It does not cover working-age adults who either earn too little to afford health insurance on their own or work for an employer that offers health insurance.

Rep. Jolanda Jones, D-Houston, filed a bill to require school officials to notify parents when there is not a full-time nurse or equivalent working on a public school campus during normal school hours. Currently, Texas does not require each public school to have a school nurse on campus.

On reproductive health, state Rep. Donna Howard filed an omnibus bill to repeal the state’s abortion ban and related statutes.

“The purpose here was to say, OK, we’ve had over a decade of restrictions on access to abortion healthcare, now we need to look at a reset,” Howard said. “Take it out. Let’s reset. Let’s talk about what can we do here that we can find some common ground on that makes more sense now that allows women to get the healthcare that they need.”

Howard’s bill would also repeal a 2023 state law passed that bans gender affirming healthcare for minors.

State Rep. Tom Oliverson, R-Cypress, filed several consumer-related healthcare bills, including one targeting penalties many Texans have complained about when they try to get medical treatment after getting a referral from a physician who is not in their insurance network.

author: Alex Cuadros
title: Bill Gates’ $29B Stake in Landfill Company Tied to Major Methane Emissions
content:
Gates has called on businesses to fight climate change. But his own investments tell a different story.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

In November 2015, world leaders descended on Paris to negotiate a historic agreement to limit global warming. But on the summit’s opening day, attention turned to a private citizen slouched awkwardly in a chair on stage: Bill Gates.

Gates, with his characteristic flop of sandy hair, grinned impishly as President Barack Obama called him a “visionary” and a “driving force” behind a pair of pledges that both saw as key to the larger agreement. First the world’s largest economies would double their spending on research into clean-energy technologies. Then investors like Gates would back the startups that emerged. The Microsoft cofounder had already enlisted two dozen other billionaires to join the effort.

For Gates, who’d become increasingly consumed by this unprecedented threat to human well-being, the moment marked his arrival as a leading figure in the fight against climate change.

“If we back over 50 different breakthrough approaches, we know that several of those will give us the solution that we need,” Gates said during his own speech. He would invest at least $2 billion of his own money in companies developing geothermal wells, new kinds of nuclear reactors and machines that pull carbon from the air, to name just a few.

With much less fanfare, however, Gates has put more than double that amount into a very dirty, old-school industry. At the time of the Paris summit, he was already the dominant shareholder of America’s No. 2 landfill operator, Republic Services. He has since increased his stake to 38% of the company, a position worth $29 billion.

While fossil fuels get most of the attention, scientists increasingly see landfills as a crucial climate issue. They’re responsible for as much as a fifth of the country’s emissions of methane, a highly potent greenhouse gas, studies show. Republic alone generates as much climate pollution as 3 million gasoline-burning cars each year, according to its own reports.

One might imagine that a landfill operator with Gates as its largest shareholder — and with three people closely linked to Gates on its board — would lead the way in tackling those emissions. Even after seemingly softening his stance on global warming in a controversial blog post last year, Gates remains one of the world’s most prominent voices on the issue. As he did in his bestselling 2021 book “How to Avoid a Climate Disaster,” he continues to advocate for cutting emissions, and he has called on his fellow business leaders to do their part.

Gates, though, has failed to make Republic live up to his own climate principles, a ProPublica investigation has found. Federal inspectors have repeatedly found methane escaping from Republic landfills at levels above federal limits. The company has refrained from adopting the ambitious emissions-reduction goal embraced by its main competitor. Republic has even lobbied against policies that could make the wider industry cleaner, including by keeping organic waste out of landfills in the first place.

“It seems very likely that Bill Gates has the power to influence Republic’s behavior to make it more climate-friendly, even if that costs the company profits,” said Ann Lipton, a legal scholar who studies corporate governance at the University of Colorado, Boulder.

As for whether he should, in her words, “put his money where his mouth is,” Lipton said, “you can leave it to the reader to make the moral judgment.”

Gates didn’t respond to repeated requests to discuss his landfill investments, and ProPublica couldn’t find any public comments he’s made about them. But the bet has proven wildly lucrative. Since November 1999, when he emerged as the owner of 5% of Republic’s shares — “It’s ‘Garbage In’ for Gates,” the New York Post headline read — the company’s stock price has soared thirtyfold. And Gates has personally received $2.6 billion in dividends, a ProPublica analysis of securities filings shows.

In those early days, Gates hadn’t yet awakened to the threat of global warming. It was a different time. Microsoft Windows ran on more than 80% of personal computers. author: Simon Childs
title: Millions of Workers Shut Down Spain With First General Strike in 14 Years
content:
Spanish workers braved stormy weather to go on general strike in protest against the country’s housing crisis on Wednesday.


Unions reported 90% turnouts among dockworkers and carmakers, as millions downed tools three weeks before a snap general election. There were

“total stoppages”

 at Volkswagen’s factory in Navarre and SEAT’s in Barcelona, organisers said.


Around 85% of meat industry workers, 82% of waste collection employees and 75% from the energy sector are also taking part, they added. In healthcare and ⁠social services roughly 38% are striking while 35% of postal service workers have also joined.


The 24-hour strike, Spain’s first in 14 years, is backed by the country’s two biggest unions, UGT and CCOO, as well as tenants’ associations fighting rising rents and evictions.


“We won’t stop until we transform this country’s housing model from top to bottom so that houses are for living instead of being at the service of the rentier minority,” said Alicia del Rio of the Madrid Tenants’ Union.


Mass protest marches were planned for Wednesday afternoon despite the expected arrival of two storms, Charles and Bruna.


Unions pointed to a 10% drop in electricity demand across the country, saying it shows that activity in energy-intensive industries such as steel processing had come to a halt.


Barcelona’s metro is only running during peak commuting hours. Protesters swarmed Madrid’s municipal bus depot in an attempt to stop busses from moving and dragged wheelie bins into roads in order to stop traffic. Shops in Barcelona were closed in anticipation of unrest.


The CCOO union

said on X

 that 13 people in Madrid needed medical attention after police fired pepper spray at picketers. “It’s a disgrace that workers are being prevented from exercising their right to strike,” the union said.


Spain has witnessed weeks of protests over housing, sparked by the eviction and subsequent death of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal. 


The country  has a deficit of 750,000 homes, which is set to grow to over a million by 2028. The average rental price of a home – €1,176 – is equivalent to 98.7% of the average young person’s monthly salary, according to the Youth Council of Spain.


The protests have led Spain’s government to call a snap election on 29 November, after it was unable to pass housing reforms in the legislature, where it lacks an outright majority. 


With the far-right ahead in the polls, Spanish Socialist Workers’ Party prime minister Pedro Sanchez is hoping to mobilise his base around the housing crisis despite criticism from protesters that his government has failed to address the issue for years. 


A train c that killed dozens on the high speed line south from Madrid last month – the country’s fourth deadly train crash this year –  has also damaged confidence in Sanchez’s government.

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: Six hopefuls in running for Kitikmeot Inuit Association president
content:
Six candidates have put their name forward in the Kitikmeot Inuit Association’s presidential election.


The organization that manages lands in trust for Kitikmeot Inuit will elect its president, a vice-president and three regional board of directors on Dec. 14.


Two other Inuit organizations, Nunavut Tunngavik Inc. and Qikiqtani Inuit Association, will also host their

leadership elections

 the same day.


The KIA presidential nominees are Jeannie Ehaloak, Rosabelle Klengenberg and Lawrence Otokiak from Cambridge Bay; Simon Komangat and Raymond Quqshuun Sr. from Gjoa Haven; and David Audlatak Nivingalok from Kugluktuk, according to a news release from the organization.


Since late June, Nivingalok has served as acting president after KIA announced former president James Eetoolook had to take leave “for personal matters.”


James Aiyout, Abel Aqqaq, David Aqqaq, and Ashoona Iroqiut hope to be elected to the board to represent Taloyoak.


Kugluktuk and Kugaaruk have one person running for their community’s spot on the board of directors: Leah Kadlun put her name forward for the Kugluktuk seat, and Tars Angutingunirk put his name forward to represent Kugaaruk.


The nomination period for KIA’s social and cultural vice-president position has been extended until Friday.


Successful candidates will hold onto their roles until 2030.

author: Jesse Hagopian
title: Paulo Freire’s Revolutionary Approach to Literacy Still Threatens Those in Power
content:
The new documentary Reading the World reveals how teaching literacy in Brazil became a struggle for political power.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

In 1963, Brazilian educator Paulo Freire helped launch a revolutionary literacy campaign in the impoverished northeastern Brazilian town of Angicos, where hundreds of rural workers learned to read and write in just 40 hours of instruction. Freire’s approach was about much more than literacy. Rather than emphasizing memorization and repetition, he developed “Culture Circles” where participants discussed their experiences, examined the conditions shaping their lives, and developed the critical consciousness to challenge oppression.

The experiment helped lay the groundwork for Freire’s groundbreaking book, Pedagogy of the Oppressed, which would become one of the most influential works in the history of education. But the literacy campaign was violently interrupted when a U.S.-backed military coup overthrew Brazilian President João Goulart in 1964. Freire was imprisoned and forced into exile, while students burned or buried their educational materials to escape persecution.

A powerful new documentary Reading the World (Lendo o Mundo) explores this formative period in Freire’s life, before he became an internationally celebrated educational philosopher. Drawing on rare archival footage of 1960s Brazil and the memories of the farmers, students, and educators who participated in the Culture Circles, the film reveals how Freire’s ideas emerged from grassroots struggles for literacy, land, voting rights, and democracy.

The film, which premiered in New York and aired on PBS WORLD Channel this October, arrives at a time when educators in the United States are confronting renewed censorship, book bans, and political attacks on teaching about racism and inequality.

I spoke with Catherine Murphy, co-director of Reading the World, about the revolutionary potential of literacy, the political forces that sought to destroy Freire’s educational experiment, and why his ideas continue to threaten those in power.

The interview that follows has been lightly edited for clarity and length.

Jesse Hagopian: One of my favorite moments in the film is the opening scene, when Paulo Freire tells his audience that he wants to have a dialogue with them rather than give a lecture. He also promises that if he doesn’t know an answer, he won’t lie. It seems like such a simple statement, but it represents a profound departure from traditional teaching. Who was Freire, and what made his approach so revolutionary?

Catherine Murphy: Paulo Freire was a Brazilian educator born in Recife in 1921. He became one of the world’s most celebrated educational philosophers. His most famous book, Pedagogy of the Oppressed, was published while he was in exile.

I also love that opening quote because it lays the groundwork for the entire film. Freire says that ever since he was a child, he understood that not knowing is part of knowing.

That gets to the essence of Freire’s philosophy: Knowledge belongs to all of us. Knowledge is generated by all of us. Education is a reciprocal, collective process. It’s about sharing what we know, and learning from each other. Freire critiqued what he called “the banking model of education” and favored a “dialogic” process based on horizontal dialogue, problem-posing, and really listening to each other.

As Freire became internationally recognized, he was increasingly invited to speak at conferences and educational institutions around the world. But his collaborators repeatedly told me stories about how he didn’t want to simply deliver lectures. He wanted dialogue with people, to listen.

When Freire visited the Highlander Center in 1987 or attended the Chicago Alternative Schools Network Conference in 1977, he wanted to know what people were doing themselves. What were popular educators doing? What were classroom teachers, community educators, and activists doing? What was working? What were they struggling with?

Freire was willing to share his ideas and experiences, but he also wanted to learn from others.

That is a beautiful lesson for all of us, not only in formal educational spaces, but in life.

Before we get into Freire’s literacy campaign, can you describe the conditions in northeastern Brazil in the early 1960s? How did illiteracy help maintain existing relations of economic and political power?
